News.title: Fury as MoD splashes almost £4k a time on chauffeur driven trips for staff – while Army CANCELS exercises to save £30m
News.content:
DEFENCE officials spent almost £4,000 a time on chauffeur-driven road trips for staff — while the Army cancels exercises to help save £30million.

New figures show the Ministry of Defence paid £3,850 each for 13 one-way journeys, including a 65-mile hop between two bases in the South East.



MoD travel records show its bill for taxis and chauffeur-driven cars was £1,932,244 from April 2024 to April 2025 — over £37,000 per week.

The bills, revealed in a freedom of information request, come after top brass were told to halt any large-scale training unless troops are about to deploy.



But Darwin Friend, of the TaxPayers’ Alliance, said: “Taxpayers will be astonished to see defence chiefs riding around in chauffeur-driven cars.

“With the defence budget already under enormous pressure and major training exercises being cancelled, shelling out millions of pounds on taxis and luxury travel is simply unacceptable.

“The MoD needs to crack down on waste and ensure scarce resources are focussed on the frontline.”

An MOD spokesperson said: “This Government is committed to securing value for money for taxpayers and cracking down on waste.

“These journeys involved multiple passengers and a significant amount of baggage.

“As a large organisation with remote sites across the UK and bases around the world, our staff sometimes need to travel to locations that are not always accessible by public transport.”

News.title: Moment bank robber throws chilli powder at staff before fleeing with handful of looted cash
News.content:
THIS is the moment a masked robber hurls chilli powder at bank staff before making off with over £3,000 in cash.

Footage shows a man in a white mask entering the bank before unleashing his spicy weapon on unsuspecting staff members.



Suraj Borker, 28, was arrested within 30 minutes of the incident at a State Bank of India branch in Maharashtra’s Nagpur district on Friday.

Cops allege Borker committed the robbery “out of greed for money“, The Indian Express reports.



The incident triggered widespread panic among the employees when Borker allegedly burst into the bank and assaulted them with chilli powder around 6 pm.

Footage captures Borker chasing down the employees to get a closer and more precise aim for his attacks.

Amid the chaos that ensued, Borker jumps the counter before allegedly grabbing a handful of cash – totalling around £3,503 – and fleeing.

A brave bank employee immediately chased down the accused along with officers who happened to be patrolling the area at the time.



The cops say Borker is currently unemployed, which may explain his wild actions.

It has also been reported that Borker was in a significant amount of debt which could further explain his decision to allegedly undertake the robbery.

Investigators are currently reviewing CCTV footage as part of their inquiry into the incident.



Police are now trying to find out whether anyone else was involved with him in the planning of the crime.

The entire sum of stolen money was recovered by police.

The footage has since gone viral on social media with one Facebook contributor saying: “At least it’s not a gun – way to spice up bank robberies”.

Earlier this year several armed thieves held 25 people hostage at an Italian bank.

The hostages were released around two hours into the terrifying ordeal after long negotiations between the cops and robbers.



The terrifying incident occurred at a Crédit Agricole branch in Naples in mid-April.

The armed robbers were believed to have escaped into the sewer system as authorities finally stormed the bank.

SWAT teams stormed the bank shortly after the reported heist before releasing the captured pair – but the perpetrators were nowhere to be seen.

News.title: Church of Scotland reverend suspended over church worker affair claims
News.content:
A MINISTER who quit to become a priest is being investigated over claims he had an affair with a former church worker.

Reverend Brian Casey, 55, is being probed by Kirk bosses over his switch to a breakaway Catholic church as well as allegations that he committed adultery.



The twice-divorced cleric, who was axed as minister of Glasgow’s Springburn Parish Church, denies cheating on his spouse, Sharon Logan, 56.

The minister-turned-priest has insisted they had split before he began a relationship with community worker Helen Carroll, 61.



Estranged wife Sharon said: “I am furious. I had suspicions about affairs going on for years. He just walked out of the manse.”

We told last year how the cleric had left his manse in Springburn, Glasgow, to join the Old Catholic Apostolic Church — and was calling himself Father Casey.



But in a blast at the Church of Scotland investigation into infidelity claims, he hit out: “They have said it’s an extra-marital affair with, amongst others, Helen Carroll. All of which is c**p.

“I’m suing the church for that accusation. I’ve spent £40,000 on a lawyer.

“I moved out of the manse in April 2025 and we got together the following month. We started to see each other as friends and it turned into something more.

“Don’t think we are having rampant sex everywhere we go because that’s not true. We still see each other two or three times a week.



“There’s no physical relationship at the moment.”

Rev Casey said he “won’t be engaging with the disciplinary process”.

He continued: “My relationship with my wife broke up in 2021. Church law is that I’m not allowed to leave the manse.



“So I slept on the couch for the last four years of our marriage.”

Helen helped Rev Casey — who once dressed up as Captain Kirk to lead the funeral of a Star Trek superfan and even gave a Vulcan salute — set up the St Jude’s Community in the city last year.

Months earlier, he was supported by members of his Springburn congregation in a fight to keep his job as minister amid claims he was being forced out as part of a restructuring drive.

Despite his claims that their marriage ended in 2021, his wife Sharon wrote an article backing her husband that was posted to Facebook in March last year.

She said it was “heartbreaking to watch the man you love” struggling to sleep due to “stress, pressure and uncertainty”.



Ms Carroll, who runs a community hub, said she was employed by the Church of Scotland after working with Rev Casey during the pandemic, but left in 2024.

She said the couple then became involved in a wellbeing cafe in early 2025.

She told The Scottish Sun on Sunday: “I started seeing him in March, April last year. It sticks out like a sore thumb that as soon as he moves out of the manse, we start having a relationship.

“It’s not true that I broke up his marriage.”

A Church spokesman said Rev Casey is “currently under administrative suspension pending the conclusion of disciplinary proceedings”.

News.title: Veteran crime scene investigator who had stroke after dealing with 50 murders a year SUES police for £100k
News.content:
CSI STRESS COMPO Veteran crime scene investigator who had stroke after dealing with 50 murders a year SUES police for £100k

A CRIME scene investigator who had a stroke after dealing with around 50 murders a year is suing his police force for more than £100,000.

Paul Tebbutt, 68, worked for 37 years on forensic investigations after killings and suspicious deaths.

After becoming crime scene co-ordinator in 2012, he says he investigated 45 murders and 100 suspicious deaths each year.

In 2017, he estimates he dealt with 100 to 200 deaths and worked 45 hours a week.





The next year he attended the highest number of murders in the West Midlands, and he worked alone after his partner quit and was not replaced.

That same year he appeared on the BBC show The Real CSI and spoke about how the nature of his work affected him.

The job would expose him to “cumulative levels of harmful occupational stress”, according to documents filed by his lawyers at London’s High Court.

He claims the harrowing nature of his work, coupled with an excessive workload, led to him suffering a stroke in 2023.



The claim acknowledges the nature of his work was inherently stressful, but he alleges West Midlands Police did not have a system to monitor how much pressure he was under.

Mr Tebbutt, from Coventry was unable to go back to work in a police station as it filled him with anxiety and fear and worked from home.

He was later classed as permanently disabled, and medically retired in April 2024, the negligence claim states.

West Midlands Police said: “As this is an ongoing matter, it would be inappropriate to comment.”

News.title: Man, 34, arrested for ‘murder’ after punter assaulted after ‘altercation’ outside pub
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

PUB 'MURDER' Man, 34, arrested for ‘murder’ after punter assaulted after ‘altercation’ outside pub

A MAN has tragically died after allegedly being attacked outside a pub.

Cops have arrested a 34-year-old man on suspicion of murder following the “altercation” in Barnsley, South Yorkshire, last night.

Officers rushed to The Star Hotel in Cudworth at around 11.30pm.

The victim, aged in his 50s, was discovered with serious injuries, before being urgently rushed to hospital.





However, despite the best efforts of medical teams, the man sadly died of his injuries, South Yorkshire Police said.

The force quickly launched a murder probe and arrested a 34-year-old man.

He remains in police custody while investigations continue.

Cops do not believe anyone else was involved in the man’s death.

The victim’s family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

Detective Inspector Laura Procter, from the Major Crime Team, urged anyone with information to get in touch.

She said: “This was a devastating incident that has left a man dead.

“Our officers worked at pace through the night to identify and arrest a suspect and we do not believe that any others were involved.



“As our investigation continues, I would ask that anyone with information that could help with enquiries please gets in touch.”

In a statement, the force added: “You can report online or by calling 101, quoting incident number 1240 of 11 September 2026.

“If you wish to report information anonymously, please contact Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or visit the Crimestoppers website.”

News.title: Lucy Letby allowed to comfort-eat chocolate and binge-watch reality TV in jail after death of doctor ‘boyfriend’
News.content:
JAILED baby-killer Lucy Letby has been allowed to comfort eat and binge-watching reality shows including Four in a Bed – as she grieves for a doctor she was infatuated with.

Letby, 36, has become “reclusive” since the death of consultant Mark Deakin, 53, and been allowed to skip prison classes and workshops due to her heartbreak.



A source said: “It is pretty obvious Letby is devastated and the staff have been giving her the equivalent of compassionate leave.

“She has become more reclusive and spending hours in her cell.



“She has been watching shows including Four in a Bed and Dinner Date and comfort-eating, with chocolate including Galaxy Ripples and Kinder Buenos her favourites.

“When officers come and call her for something, Letby often says ‘one more episode’ and stays in her cell on her own.

“Staff are taking it easy on her and have to monitor her state of mind as she is currently classed as vulnerable because of what’s happened.

“Although the doctor was not related to her, they are treating it like a bereavement.

“Staff are also doing things like removing newspapers from the wing, which might mention the story.

“The only person Letby wants to mix with is Sara Sharif’s Mum Beinash Batool – she is leaning on her for support.



“They play chess and cards together for hours on end and there’s a view that it helps Letby take her mind off things.”

The Sun on Sunday revealed last month that the married doctor – who gave evidence against Letby at her trial – had died.

The Dad of two applied for anonymity and was referred to as Doctor A during the case.

But he was named after an order protecting his identity was lifted earlier this month at the Appeal Court.



Dr Deakin worked with Letby at the Countess of Chester Hospital in 2016 at the time of her arrest for the murders of babies on its neonatal unit.

Letby called him her “best friend” and “love” in hand-written notes found at her home, and the pair swapped more than 1,300 Facebook messages over three months in 2016.

In one of the most dramatic scenes of the trial, Letby broke down in tears and tried to leave the court as the medic confirmed his name from behind a screen.

During the 10-month trial, which ended in August 2023, Prosecutors called the doctor Letby’s “boyfriend”.



They said she attacked babies to create “crisis situations” knowing he would dash to attend.

At the later Thirlwall Inquiry into baby deaths in 2024, the registrar later said he had been “misled” and “maybe manipulated” by Letby.

Doctor Deakin had moved on to work at Alder Hey children’s hospital in Liverpool before his death.

But he was sacked over messages he and Letby had exchanged when they both worked at the Countess of Chester Hospital.

He was found slumped in his car at a retail park the day after his dismissal and died nine days later.



Letby was convicted of seven murders and seven attempted killings from 2015-2016 and is serving a whole-life order at HMP Bronzefield, Surrey.

Letby, of Hereford, maintains her innocence but has lost two bids to challenge her convictions.

The Criminal Cases Review Commission is considering evidence claiming natural causes and poor care caused deaths and could order a retrial.

A spokesperson for Sodexo, which runs Bronzefield, said it could not comment on individuals.

News.title: Romanian toyboy who inherited £250k estate from ex-vicar lover, 81, when he died flaunts life of luxury
News.content:
CASH SPLASH Romanian toyboy who inherited £250k estate from ex-vicar lover, 81, when he died flaunts life of luxury

A ROMANIAN toyboy who inherited a £250,000 estate from his late pensioner lover when he died now flaunts a life of luxury.

Florin Marin, now 33, was left a £2,000-a-month pension as well as a lump sum of £150,000 when his partner, Philip Clements, a former vicar, died aged 81 in 2020.



Mr Clements, from Eastry in Kent, moved to Romania in 2017 in order to be with Mr Marin.

He sold his home in Sandwich, Kent, for £215,000 to buy a flat in Bucharest and transferred ownership into his husband’s name.



Their marriage raised concerns with the couple also making an appearance on Jeremy Kyle’s former show on ITV.

At the time, Mr Clements said: “I love him to bits – if we were permanently separated, I would be the most unhappy person in the world.”



He had been an Anglican priest for 50 years but retired before tying the knot with Mr Marin.

The couple had met on the gay dating app Grindr in 2015.



Since Mr Clements’ death, Mr Marin has been in two long-term relationships.

First, with Spaniard Jeronimo and then Giovanni Messina, a 50-year-old German-Italian hotel boss.

Mr Marin has now revealed that he and Mr Messina opened up their relationship two years ago and he now has a new “mistress” – a 50-year-old Bulgarian businessman.

He told the Daily Mail the pair met in May during Gran Canaria Pride on a naked cruise ship.

Mr Marin loves to travel but said he “does not spend a penny” on his luxury trips or designer clothes.



Instead, they are funded either by his new lover or Mr Messina, Mr Marin claimed.

He added that Mr Messina sometimes got jealous and competitive with his new beau.

Last month he took a trip around the east coast of the US, visiting Pennsylvania, Washington DC and New York City.



In several online videos, he displays his business-class seat as he drinks champagne and does his skincare routine during the flight from Frankfurt to New York.

During the visit, he also posts videos of the view from his hotel overlooking Times Square as well as footage of him dancing and taking part in TikTok trends in the famous square.

Other videos on his account show off his love of luxury fashion, with clips showing him unboxing designer gifts he says are from his Bulgarian businessman.

He has also claimed that Mr Messina has put his hotel business in his name so he can earn an income and is secure.

This is separate from the £2,000 he gets monthly from Mr Clements’s pension.



The relationship between Mr Marin and Mr Clements caused harsh criticism from the ex-vicar’s family, with his brothers calling Mr Marin a “gold-digger”.

Mr Marin told the paper he and Mr Clements had splashed £1million during their five-year relationship.

Mr Clements fell ill shortly after moving to Romania in May 2020, having run out of medication during the coronavirus lockdown.

While he tested negative for Covid-19, he died on May 31.

Mr Marin said his husband had refused to go to hospital for several days, and developed a fever and became disoriented, before Mr Marin insisted on taking him to hospital.



Mr Marin started dating Mr Messina in 2022 and moved to Germany to be with him.

He said in 2024: “I do have expensive extravagant holidays, maybe too many.

“I met my new partner on the Planet Romeo, it’s a gay app… Giovanni is a lovely man and I am very much in love.

“We met when I was a bit low and suffering from anxiety – I can’t stay a widow all my life, you know.”

He added he had fond memories of his former husband, thought of him constantly and was “very grateful” to him, calling him a “lovely gentleman”.



Mr Marin said: “We were so happy together and I’m sad he is not with me anymore. He secured my life, he did everything to make sure I was happy and I think about him all the time.”

Mr Marin also revealed he has a big portrait of him in his house, “so I have him with me all the time” and still had his armchair and walking stick which he kept in his home in Romania.

His relationship with Mr Clements’s brothers though is still tense, with Mr Marin revealing he didn’t speak with the two blood brothers.

He told the paper: “Philip was my husband and I was entitled to what I got.

“People will always talk and have their opinions which is fine, but they don’t make me feel bad or guilty.”

News.title: Fury as a staggering 200,000 families rake in more in benefits than the typical Brit earns in a year
News.content:
A TOTAL of 200,000 families receive more in benefits than the typical worker earns in a year.

That is the same as the population of Norwich pocketing over £39,039 each.



In a written answer slipped out by the Government, Welfare minister Baroness Sherlock admitted: “200,000 families in the UK received more than £39,039 in state support.”

Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Helen Whately uncovered the shocking statistic.



She blasted: “Our welfare system is so out of touch it pays those on benefits more than those who go out to work.

“Every pound paid above the wage of the average worker is a signal by Labour that effort is optional. A welfare system should act like a trampoline — cushioning your fall and propelling you back on to your feet.



“Under Labour, it has become a net that engulfs you and makes it almost impossible to climb out.”

The welfare and pensions bill has ballooned to £334billion.

But PM Andy Burnham said last week he will not cut benefits to fund defence.

He insisted: “We do everything to support our national security but it cannot come at the expense of social security.”



The Department for Work and Pensions said: “Last year, the amount of people receiving awards over £30,000 was under two per cent of the total.

“We’re reforming welfare to end the culture of people being signed off and written off.”

News.title: Manchester incident recap: Teen suffers 'possible life changing injuries' in 'substance attack'
News.content:
A police cordon is in place by the Arndale shopping centre in Manchester city centre after a boy in his mid-teens had an "unknown substance" thrown at him

A teenager has suffered a "potentially life-changing" injury after an "unknown substance" was thrown at him in Manchester city centre.

Police, fire crews and colleagues from the North West Ambulance service are outside the Arndale shopping centre opposite the Printworks with a large cordon in place.

Officers rushed to the scene at 6.10pm where they established a substance which has not yet been identified was thrown following an argument.

A statement from Greater Manchester Police read: "The victim, a male in his mid-teens has received an injury that has been described as not life-threatening but potentially life-changing. A 19-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of assault and remains in custody."

News.title: Massive blaze rips through Yorkshire landmark with warning to keep windows closed
News.content:
Massive blaze rips through Yorkshire landmark with warning to keep windows closed

Fire crews are tackling a massive blaze at Dalton Mills, a well-known landmark in Keighley, Yorkshire, with road closures in place and police advising residents to keep windows and doors closed

View 2 Images The fire ripping through Dalton Mills (Image: West Yorkshire Police)

A massive fire is ripping through a Yorkshire landmark used for TV set for Peaky Blinders and Downton Abbey.

‌



Firefighters are at Dalton Mills, a disused building in Keighley which is ablaze with a cordon and road closure in place.

‌



Residents are being urged by police to keep their windows and doors closed due to the smoke while Dalton Lane is closed to all traffic.

‌



A statement from West Yorkshire Police reads: "Please be aware that Dalton Mills are currently on fire. Dalton Lane in Keighley is currently closed to all traffic, as our colleagues from West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service are working to bring the situation under control.

View 2 Images The fire is at a landmark in Keighley (Image: West Yorkshire Police)

"We advise people to stay away from the area, and residents in the vicinity to keep all doors and windows closed."

‌



The site has suffered a handful of major fires over the last four years. More than 100 firefighters battled a blaze in March 2022. Another major fire broke out at the mill in July 2025 with 12 fire engines sent to the scene. The site also suffered a serious fire in 2011.

Local councillor Caroline Firth said that the fire was a "disaster" for Keighley. She said on Facebook: "I'm here at Dalton Mills who I want to support as it is too dangerous for pedestrians but this is a disaster for Keighley. This mill could have been saved by now, something I've been fighting for.

"There is a mechanism to do it and I call on Reform to enact this mechanism. We had someone waiting in the wings to take this building on and regenerate it. I call on the council to treat this site the priority it deserves."

Article continues below

Many other people have also taken to social media to express their sadness at the blaze. "Not again Absolutely shocking used to be a lovely building," wrote one person and another said: "This is the closest section to the bus museum, just hope that doesn't catch fire. It did last time. Very worrying. Such a beautiful Mill, a real loss to Keighley."

While a further person said: "Honestly, I don’t know why people are shocked anymore. How many times does this place have to go up before we start asking whether it’s even worth continuing to throw time, money and emergency resources at it?

"At some point, you have to ask whether it would be more sensible to call it a day and stop putting our firefighters and public resources through this over and over again."

News.title: Nigel Farage's crypto friends include Ben Delo who made fortune in Hong Kong
News.content:
Nigel Farage's crypto friends include Ben Delo who made fortune in Hong Kong

Ben Delo may have handed over a record-breaking £36million political donation, but the crypto billionaire is known for living far more modestly than his extraordinary fortune might suggest

View 3 Images Nigel Farage's party has received the biggest-ever donation from an individual (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

You'd assume the man behind the single largest-ever political donation makes a habit of splashing his cash.

‌



But apparently this couldn’t be less true of Ben Delo. The UK’s youngest self-made billionaire, 42, reportedly enjoys nothing more than using special-offer vouchers to pay for his McDonald’s meals. He once admitted to owning just three pairs of shoes – trainers, leather brogues and flip-flops.

‌



He used to spend weekends dressing up as kids’ book character Where’s Wally. And he converted a large windowsill in his Hong Kong flat into a single-bed Airbnb, to cover some of the rent. Delo came from semi-humble beginnings. The eldest of four siblings, he was born in Sheffield around the time of the miners’ strike to mum Claire, a teacher, and dad Andrew, a civil engineer.

‌



He was the class clown at school, which got him kicked out three times, and he was later diagnosed with Asperger syndrome.

Patriot Platform leader Danny Tommo Thomas plans to lay siege to asylum centres READ MORE :

View 3 Images Ben made his fortune after co-funding crypto trading platform BitMEX (Image: Charlie Bibby/FT)

He recalled in a 2016 interview: “The head teacher, when he kicked me out, said he had aged two years in those three months. I was then out of school for the rest of that year.” The family later relocated to Thame, Oxfordshire, where Delo went to comprehensive Lord Williams’s School.

‌



It was here that his dreams of earning big bucks began – he used his home economics classes to make pizzas to flog to pupils and teachers. And at 16, he wrote about wanting to be an “internet entrepreneur, millionaire [and] computer programmer” in an annual pupil review.

This new-found confidence ramped up when he got a place at Oxford to study maths and computer science. Fellow students recall he once turned up to a formal dinner wearing a wetsuit with his gown – the rules stipulated a gown and a “suit”. After short spells at the US Patent and Trademark Office and several hedge funds, he founded the crypto currency trading platform BitMEX in 2014.

Four years later, the Times named him the UK’s youngest self-made billionaire. Things looked bad in when in 2022 he was convicted in the US for failing to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls in BitMEX... but luckily, President Trump pardoned him in 2025.

‌



View 3 Images Christopher Harbone matched Ben Delo's £36 million donation to Reform UK (Image: Linedin)

Once a Tory Party donor, billionaire Christopher Harborne has already given millions to Reform UK over the years. The crypto tycoon is estimated to be the sixth-richest UK billionaire, with a personal fortune of around £18.2bn.

Over the past seven years, Harborne had given more than £22million to Reform, accounting for two-thirds of all funding received by Nigel Farage’s party. Before he matched Ben Delo’s £36million donation, Harborne’s £9million had been the largest single amount ever given by a living donor.

‌



According to his lawyers, Harborne is an “intensely private person” and has given no public explanation of his reasons for donating. Crypto currency has turbocharged Harborne’s wealth. He is one of half a dozen owners of crypto firm Tether, which is often branded the most profitable company per employee in history.

Harborne grew up in Mosborough, a village near Sheffield. Mark Vellacott, a close friend of his late sister Katharine, once said that he was similar in character to his mother Joan, a Yorkshire woman who was from a well-off background.

Aerospace businessman Vellacott said of Harborne: “Chris does not like anything that’s going to control him.”

Article continues below

After private school in Westminster, Harborne followed his father Edgar to Cambridge, where he studied engineering and rowed for his college. Moving to Thailand in 1996, Harborne joined a market research firm owned by a member of the powerful Bulakul family. Later, he made his first political donation – some £10,000 to the Tories.

Harborne’s lawyers have said in court filings that he has given money to various groups, including victims of the 2004 tsunami and remote Thai tribes.

News.title: Man dies in blaze on 17th floor of London tower block with a child rescued
News.content:
Man dies in blaze on 17th floor of London tower block with a child rescued

London Fire Brigade raced to a fire in a flat on the 17th floor of a tower block in Poplar, east London, where a man sadly died at the scene while two adults and a child were rescued

View Image The fire was at a block of flats in Poplar (Image: Google Maps)

A man has tragically died in a fire on the 17th floor of a block of flats in east London where two adults and a child were rescued.

‌



London Fire Brigade were called to the fire in Poplar at 4.35am this morning and around 70 firefighters tackled the massive blaze which broke out in a two-room flat and balcony in the 22-storey residential block.

‌



Half of the property on the 17th floor of the block of flats in Blackwall Way was damaged with the fire brought under control by 6.41am.

‌

And sadly the fire service has said that a man died at the scene of the fire while two adults and a child were rescued by crew wearing breathing gear.

There were a further 50 people who had left the building before the emergency services arrived and they are currently at a provided rest centre.

‌



An LFB spokesperson said: “Ten fire engines and around 70 firefighters were called to a flat fire on Blackwall Way in Poplar. A two-room flat and balcony on the 17th floor of a 22-storey residential block of flats was damaged by fire.

“Two adults and one child were rescued by firefighters wearing breathing apparatus. Sadly, a man was declared dead at the scene. A further 50 people left the building before the Brigade arrived on scene and are currently at a rest centre.”

Crews from across east London were sent to help tackle the blaze and now the fire service is looking into the cause with several factors being looked into. The LFB added: “A range of factors are being investigated regarding the cause of the fire.”

Article continues below

While a London Ambulance Service statement read: "We were called at 4.44am to reports of a fire in Blackwall Way, Poplar. We sent ambulance crews, our tactical response unit, an incident response officer and paramedics from our hazardous area response team to the scene. We also dispatched London's air ambulance."

It added: "Sadly, a person was pronounced dead at the scene. Two other patients were taken to hospital, and a third was treated at the scene and discharged."

An early statement from the fire brigade said: “The Brigade’s 999 control officers were called at 0435 and mobilised crews from Poplar, Whitechapel, Plaistow, Stratford, Shadwell, East Ham, East Greenwich, Bethnal Green and Greenwich fire stations. The cause of the fire is under investigation.”

News.title: Trump Ireland visit live: No 10 responds to Trump's support for united Ireland
News.content:
Donald Trump declared his support for a united Ireland while taking questions alongside Taoiseach Micheál Martin this morning.

The US President is visiting Ireland for two days, and has said he would "love to see" the unification of the Republic of Ireland with Northern Ireland. "The UK would have something to say about it but I think it would be a great thing," he said. There were gasps in the room as he said it.

In response, Downing Street referred to what Andy Burnham said in the House of Commons on Wednesday - that he "will stick to [the Good Friday Agreement] 100%".

Trump also weighed in on the Falklands, saying he did not know if the UK is “going to be willing to travel that far” should there be a dispute with Argentina, adding he was “sure I’ll be called into that potential disaster” and would be able to “settle it out”.

Meanwhile, controversial aide Natalie Harp has been spotted among the US delegation in Ireland. Questions have been swirling about her personal relationship with the US President as she is reported to have frequently left "intimate" letters for him, saying things like "You are all that matters to me," and "I don't ever want to let you down...I want to bring you joy."

News.title: Patriot Platform leader Danny Tommo Thomas plans to lay siege to asylum centres
News.content:
Patriot Platform leader Danny Tommo Thomas plans to lay siege to asylum centres

EXCLUSIVE: Danny "Tommo" Thomas, the convicted attempted kidnapper, spoke out after his group recently carried out protests in both Dover and Portsmouth

View 5 Images Far-right activist, Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo spoke to us (Image: Getty Images)

The convicted criminal behind the masked anti-migrant group Patriot Platform wants to target asylum centres, we can reveal.

‌



Danny "Tommo" Thomas, whose balaclava-clad followers have brought chaos to both Dover and Portsmouth in recent days, has suggested he wants followers to camp outside shelters for days to stop officials transporting migrants. Under Thomas' plans, the protesters would operate 24/7 blockades, with members from around the UK maintaining the barricade in shifts.

‌

Any actions that get in the way of processing asylum applications could slow down the number of deportations and removals - which is also up significantly under this government."

‌



Portsmouth protesters face arrest for wearing masks as more rallies planned READ MORE :

View 5 Images Danny "Tommo" Thomas' balaclava-clad followers have protested in both Dover and Portsmouth in recent days

Thomas revealed the plot in an interview with fellow rabble rouser Tommy Robinson, real name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon. The convicted attempted kidnapper said: "I predict in the next six months, the Patriot Platform, with one message through a secure app, will be able to bring five to 10,000 people to a location within a matter of hours."

He said one target could be Piddington, Oxfordshire, where asylum seekers could be housed at a nearby former MoD site. Thomas said: "A prime example, Piddington, where the migrants are about to to go in. How powerful would it be if 5,000 men, when they know the MO, because we've proven who we are, what how our conduct is, that we surround that camp, we take tents, we sit there for days and we don't let them get in till they can't bring them in."

‌



Thomas, who was privately educated in Hampshire, added: "We're trying to do something that's never been done before in a way that it's never been done before to get results that we've never seen before."

Thomas, who was jailed for his part in the attempted armed kidnapping of a man in 2016 before turning to Christianity, also suggested to Robinson, 43, that Brits turning away from the religion has caused moral decline over the last "80 or 90 years". The dad-four claimed: "Christianity was at the forefront of how you behaved. Girls were purer back then because they're under a Christian journey and we've lost all of this."

Thomas spoke about how Patriot Platform was initially formed by a group of men from south London before other members later held further gatherings inside churches and the group held a recruitment day in Coventry on August 22. He claimed that one member was "landed on" and removed from the group after being found to be drunk the night before they travelled to Dover last Saturday.

‌



View 5 Images Thomas was seen standing in water livestreaming an operation to rescue around 140 migrants who were brought into the harbour at Portsmouth on Sunday night (Image: Barry Williams/PA Wire)

He also claimed a prospective member was kicked out for racism and added: "Lads have had slaps. There's people that have had slaps to stay in line." Thomas served as a tank driver with the King’s Royal Hussars, but his Army career was cut short and he was discharged on medical grounds before seeing active service.

He says his group's tactics were inspired by meeting a leader from a paramilitary-style group in Northern Ireland. Thomas said: "I went with one of the most senior members of that area. He said when we drove around and all the fires are up and all, he said to me 'Danny, do you know what happens to someone that walks out of the house and comes onto the street with a beer can? They get battered'.

‌



"When the men go to work in Northern Ireland... no drugs, no alcohol, there's people, there's a structure. If someone of that structure puts something in place to maintain calm and someone steps out of line, they get dealt with now. So, I've taken that."

Suggesting his group will also follow in the footsteps of left-wing protest groups such as Extinction Rebellion and Just Stop Oil, Thomas said: "We've got to start using the fact that they use the law against us. We have now lawyers who are the only people that communicate with the police. None of our members talk to police officers at any point in time.

"What they are given is a piece of paper in their pocket. When they unfold that piece of paper, it gives them under the Human Rights Act what it is that they're there for, why they're there, their intentions, and at the bottom it says, "Please contact this lawyer for any questions you have. And in Dover, that's exactly what happened. [The police] were confused. They didn't really know what to do."

‌



View 5 Images Flags were waved on an anti-illegal immigration march in Portsmouth today (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

Describing his group, which he has claimed more than 40,000 people have signed up to, Thomas claimed "it is not a white nationalist movement". He added it is a "pure resistance, non-violent, non-confrontational pure Christian national resistance movement to take control".

He claimed: "These are not far-right thugs. No alcohol, no drugs, no thuggery, no shouting. Every member is encouraged to give their life to Jesus. Every member is encouraged to go to church. And let me tell you now, that is happening."

‌



The plot emerged as hundreds of protesters from other groups today held an anti-migrant demo in Portsmouth, leading to three arrests, including a 76-year-old man, from Southampton, arrested on suspicion of wearing/using an item to conceal identity at a protest, a 33-year-old man, from Portsmouth, arrested on suspicion of obstructing a highway and a 16-year-old boy from Portsmouth held on suspicion of violent disorder, in relation to violent public disorder at Eastney Marina last Sunday.

Earlier in the day, a man appeared in court in Portsmouth accused of throwing a bottle towards a police line at an anti-migrant protest. Del Leon Somerville, 42, of Paulsgrove, is charged with violent disorder and assaulting a police constable in the execution of their duty.

His first appearance at Portsmouth Magistrates' Court, sitting at the city's crown court, on Saturday, came ahead of further protests planned in the city in the afternoon. He did not enter any pleas at the short hearing to charges of violent disorder between September 5 and 8 in Portsmouth, and assaulting a constable on September 11 in Waterlooville.

Article continues below

View 5 Images Police and protesters clashed during an anti-illegal immigration demonstration in Portsmouth today (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

Prosecutor Lucy Paddick told the court he was accused of throwing a bottle towards a police line and was allegedly heard telling officers to f*** off as the bottle was thrown. Somerville is also alleged to have kicked out at PC Peskett, making contact with the officer's right thigh, when he was arrested, the court heard.

He was remanded into custody at the hearing, supported by members of his family in the courtroom, ahead of his next appearance at Portsmouth Crown Court on September 16. Assistant Chief Constable Tony Rowlinson said Somerville's arrest was the "first of what we fully anticipate to be a number of arrests" and hoped it would send a "clear warning" to those planning future disruption and disorder.

News.title: Man becomes first arrested for 'concealing his identity' hours after face covering ban
News.content:
Man becomes first arrested for 'concealing his identity' hours after face covering ban

Hampshire Police used newly introduced powers during rival demonstrations in Portsmouth, where three people were arrested and hundreds of protestors were kept apart

View 3 Images Men wearing balaclavas at a recent protest in Dover (file image)

A man became the first person to be arrested on suspicion of concealing his identity just hours after a new ban came into force.

The restriction took effect at 10am on Saturday, with police warning those attending rival demonstrations in Portsmouth not to wear face coverings used to conceal their identity. Hampshire Police said it would use new powers under the Crime and Policing Act 2025 to “allow peaceful protest and prevent violence”.

During the protest, three people were arrested, including a 76-year-old man from Southampton on suspicion of wearing or using an item to conceal his identity at a protest.

View 3 Images A new face-covering restriction was in force during the march (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

Portsmouth protesters face arrest for wearing masks as more rallies planned READ MORE :

A 33-year-old man from Portsmouth was also arrested on suspicion of obstructing a highway, while a 16-year-old boy, also from Portsmouth, was arrested on suspicion of violent disorder in relation to a similar protest at Eastney Marina last Sunday.

The measures came amid wider concerns over masked demonstrations, after around 300 protesters blocked access to the Port of Dover last week. Groups from South Coast Patriots had called for a peaceful march through Portsmouth city centre on Saturday afternoon, while a counter-protest was also organised by Stand Up To Racism.

Around 300 people joined the counter-protest, with both sets of demonstrators kept apart by police when they arrived at Guildhall Square.

A separate order also allowed officers to require people to remove masks and other items being used to conceal their identity. Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones said: “I’m pleased that today’s protests in Portsmouth took place without major issue.

“Thankfully, we didn’t see repeated scenes of Sunday night with assaults on police officers and criminal damage to police vehicles and people’s property.”

View 3 Images The counter protest was organised by Stand Up To Racism (Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire)

She thanked officers for their work and their impartial use of the power to ask people to remove face coverings.

The warning came after a 42-year-old man became the first person to be arrested as part of a probe into violent disorder in Portsmouth last weekend where crowds gathered at Eastney Marina overnight on Sunday after a dinghy arrived in the area having crossed the English Channel.

Hampshire Police said official vehicles were damaged and a small number of officers were injured at the scene, before around 200 people were dispersed at around 4am on Monday.

Speaking on Friday, Assistant Chief Constable Paul Bartolomeo said: “It is important to stress that this power will apply to any groups that attend the protest and will be enforced equally and impartially. Let me be clear, these powers are not being implemented to prevent protest but they are being used to help prevent crime and disorder, while making communities feel safer.”

Hampshire Police said several of its vehicles, alongside those of the coastguard and Border Force, were damaged during the previous weekend’s disruption, while a small number of officers were treated at the scene for injuries. No-one in attendance was seriously injured.

News.title: Man 'murdered in flat' was 'lovable and cheeky' regular at local pub
News.content:
Man 'murdered in flat' was 'lovable and cheeky' regular at local pub

Thomas ‘Tommy’ Carey, of Lambeth, south London, died from head injuries at his flat sparking a murder investigation and his local pub has now paid tribute saying "he was loved by so many"

View 3 Images Thomas Carey died of head injuries (Image: Jam Press)

A man who died from head injuries at his flat sparking a murder investigation was a "lovable and cheeky" regular at his local pub in south London which paid tribute

Thomas ‘Tommy’ Carey, of Lambeth, 39, died before emergency services arrived at his home in Poynders Road, Brixton Hill, on Friday, September 4.

And now staff at The Hope pub said he would never be forgotten and that his ‘second home’ would ‘never be the same.’

View 3 Images A murder investigation is underway into his death (Image: Jam Press)

In a tribute on the West Norwood The Hope Pub’s Facebook page, a tribute described Thomas as a ‘lovely customer,’ who was a ‘cheeky chap with a smile on his face’, reported MyLondon.

The touching tribute read: “One of our lovely customers, Tommy. Known to so many people in this area as the cheeky chap with always a smile on his face.

"Tommy was a big kid at heart, with an even bigger heart. A lovable character who will be hugely missed by everyone who knew him.

“Every morning, he was one of the first in - a coffee, a BuzzBall and a chat with myself and everyone else who knew and loved him. You genuinely couldn’t say a bad word about Tommy. He was loved by so many.

“We are shocked, absolutely gutted, and finding it so hard to understand. WHY?? Sleep tight, our lovely Tommy. Our mornings will never be the same without you. You will always be part of the Hope - your second home - and we will make sure you are never forgotten."

View 3 Images Staff at The Hope pub have paid tribute to Thomas (Image: Google)

It continued: “If anyone who knew Tommy thinks they may have any information that could help, however small or insignificant it may seem, please contact the Metropolitan Police on 101 and quote CAD number CAD7021/04SEP26.

"Any information could be good information and may help us get justice for our Tommy. Fly high, Tommy. You will be missed more than you’ll ever know you actually didn’t realise how loved you were my darling. Thomas John Carey.”

Police arrested two men in their 30s on suspicion of murder on Tuesday, September 8. A woman in her 30s was also arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder.

Then on Thursday Leroy Heffron, 38, of Sangley Road, Catford, was charged with murder and held in custody. The other man was bailed pending further enquiries and the woman is in police custody.

Detective Chief Inspector Alison Foxwell, who is leading the Met Police investigation, said: “We are pleased with the progress of the investigation into Thomas’ death, and our thoughts remain with his family and friends at this difficult time.

“Our enquiries remain ongoing, and we continue to appeal for information. We urge anyone who may have seen or heard anything unusual on in the evening of Thursday, 3 September into the early morning of Friday, 4 September to reach out and speak to us.”

Detective Chief Superintendent Emma Bond, who leads policing in the local area, said: “We know this incident has caused concern and sadness across the local community, particularly among those who knew Thomas. Residents may continue to see an increased police presence in the area over the coming days. If you have any questions or concerns, please speak to one of our officers on patrol.”

News.title: Dramatic insider warnings over AI fall flat with some in Silicon Valley
News.content:
Each September, a who's who of executives from across Silicon Valley descends on San Francisco's Palace Hotel to charm investors at a conference hosted by the investment bank Goldman Sachs.

This past week, between talk of growth and potential returns, tech titans found themselves addressing the abrupt resignation of Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon.

Coxon, a 27-year-old who worked at OpenAI before joining its chief rival Anthropic, said on Tuesday that people building artificial intelligence (AI) believed the technology could destroy humanity.

They are "gambling with our lives", he said, "these will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything".

Coxon is by no means the first AI insider to publicly sound the alarm. There have been a string of high-profile resignations from both Anthropic and OpenAI in recent years over apparent safety concerns, and some current Anthropic employees even echoed Coxon's post.

"We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade," a team lead at Anthropic, Evan Hubinger, posted on X.

While Coxon said explicitly in his posts that his warnings were "not marketing", some executives and investors in Silicon Valley have reacted with scepticism to a recent flurry of insiders sounding the alarm.

Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly preparing for potentially record-setting initial public offerings, and some in the tech sector have suggested the latest stark comments about the dangers of AI may be designed to generate hype by signalling the power of these products.

Anthropic's boss, Dario Amodei, has come under fire for saying AI technology could wipe out half of entry-level white-collar jobs and will "test who we are as a species".

One conference speaker, Grindr CEO George Arison, told the BBC he believed this week's comments from Coxon and others were indicative of an "anti-civilisational worldview at Anthropic".

He called them "dangerous" and said they had prompted him to instruct some engineers at the LGBTQ+ dating app to stop using Anthropic's technology.

"It is irresponsible for us as stewards of our shareholders' money to be relying on a business that does what this company does, in terms of its public statements," he said.

"Maybe they actually believe it," Arison said. "Or you could argue they're saying it because it's a great way to gin up more investor support, because the only way to justify these valuations is to actually claim: 'I'm going to take over every industry and I'm going to take over every job, and my AI is going to be doing all that work.'"

Anthropic was valued at $965bn (Â£713bn) in its most recent fundraising round earlier this year.

The BBC has asked Anthropic for a response to the statements.

In an essay posted early on Saturday, Amodei called for a slowing of AI model development and global regulation - and said the risks associated with AI were "serious".

News.title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record
News.content:
Harborne has already donated millions to Reform and Farage, who is currently under investigation by the parliamentary standards commissioner over whether he should have declared a Â£5m cash gift from Harborne ahead of the 2024 election.

Farage has argued that he was under no obligation to register the "purely private" gift, as it was unrelated to his parliamentary or political activities.

The party is also facing scrutiny after a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week showed two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations.

The Metropolitan Police has said it is investigating, while the party denies any wrongdoing.

The force is also looking into donations given to the party by Fiona Cottrell, mother of longstanding Farage ally George Cottrell, as well as a company controlled by Tice.

Harborne wrote on Saturday that he had "already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life", while Reform was a "start-up party" that lacked "the benefit of hundreds of years of patronage".

"A start-up party needs more money than can be provided by membership fees alone, to build and sustain itself and be ready for government," he said.

Harborne and Delo's donations mark the largest sums received by a UK political party since they had to begin declaring them in 2001.

Delo, who also announced his donation in a Telegraph op-ed, said he was giving the money away because he wanted a "fair fight and a level playing field". He said in April he was moving back to Britain from Hong Kong.

Addressing the recent scrutiny of Reform's finances, he said: "My conclusion from Reform's recent troubles is that they should spend less time trying to raise funds to compete on equal terms and more time preparing for government."

Last year, he was given an unconditional pardon by US President Donald Trump over a breach of anti-money laundering laws at his crypto trading platform, BitMEX, to which he had pleaded guilty in 2022.

There are currently no restrictions on the amount of money UK-based donors can give to political parties.

However, the Labour government has introduced a Â£100,000 cap on donations from British citizens living overseas, and plans to introduce a similar one for those who have recently returned to the UK.

There were nine donations of Â£1m or more to political parties in 2025. The largest was Â£9m given to Reform UK by Harborne.

Labour had five donations of Â£1m or more - totalling nearly Â£10m - and the Conservatives had three of Â£1m each.

Labour said Reform and Farage still had "serious questions" to answer about their finances.

Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said Reform were "drowning" in "sleaze and scandal".

She added: "It's time Farage and Reform came clean with the public, fully co-operated with the ongoing police investigations and prove they're not just in it for themselves."

Rachel Millward, deputy leader of the Green Party, told BBC News it wanted a cap on donations from individuals of Â£500,000.

She said the donations to Reform were "absolutely staggering amounts", adding: "What I am very frustrated about is the influence of extreme wealth and the super rich. What I want to see is people in politics representing the needs of their communities and ordinary people."

Liberal Democrat Cabinet Office spokeswoman Lisa Smart called for the government to introduce emergency legislation to cap donations.

She said: "These are eye-watering amounts of money. This is real emergency for our democracy. It presents a very clear and present threat."

Labour MP Stella Creasy and other backbenchers had proposed an amendment to the Government's Representation of the People Bill that would stop donors giving parties over Â£100,000 a year.

But the amendment was never debated in the Commons after the government said it would set up a task force to investigate the issue. The bill will be debated in the House of Lords on Monday.

Duncan Hames, Director of Policy and Programmes at campaigning charity Transparency International UK, said: "This is a watershed moment, with two billionaires pledging Â£72m to one political party in less than 48 hours.

"This situation is now completely out of control, and makes an irrefutable case for government to bring forward an annual cap on political donations, and fast."

News.title: Trump's comments on a united Ireland may have targeted audience across the Atlantic
News.content:
When another world leader meets US President Donald Trump the only certainty about what might happen is the uncertainty about what might happen.

This was exactly the case ahead of President Trump's two-day visit to Ireland.

Nobody could have predicted that by the end of the first day, the main global headline would be his desire to see a unified Ireland.

As the shockwaves of his remarks rippled through this island and Great Britain, it was unclear whether this represented a new US administration policy, or an off-the-cuff remark from a president who likes to take questions from reporters, and likes to give answers.

News.title: 'Skimpflation' warning as tinned mackerel alternative hits more supermarket shelves
News.content:
A growing trend of supermarkets selling a cheaper, less nutritious alternative to tinned mackerel is an example of "skimpflation", a consumer group has said.

Princes - which supplies major supermarkets - has substituted jack mackerel, an entirely different species, for mackerel, with similar tins also being sold by Lidl.

The switch has been spurred by dwindling stocks of Atlantic mackerel after years of overfishing, with its Chilean counterpart more sustainable and a third of the cost.

"It's a real concern when manufacturers quietly downgrade everyday staples like these as shoppers can end up paying the same price for a product that delivers significantly less nutritional quality," Sue Davies, head of food policy at Which?, said.

Jack mackerel contains about half as much omega-3 and around a third as much vitamin B12 as traditional mackerel.

The shift has prompted complaints from some consumers over differences in taste and texture, as well as concerns about how clearly the replacement fish is being labelled.

Princes announced last October, external that it was changing all of its tinned mackerel products to jack mackerel, saying the species meets the Marine Stewardship Council's sustainability standards.

The firm said its jack mackerel products were "clearly identified" and had been introduced following extensive product and consumer testing, describing it as having a "milder flavour and meatier texture".

Lidl is selling jack mackerel under its house brand. Lidl GB said it was "committed to sourcing fish and seafood from responsibly managed fisheries".

Davies from Which? said: "While manufacturers face genuine supply chain pressures and sustainability challenges, they have a responsibility to shoppers to be completely upfront when they change a product's recipe."

She added: "Skimpflation - quietly changing ingredients to cut costs - has become increasingly common, but it can feel particularly sneaky as shoppers may not realise a product has changed until they get it home and eat it."

News.title: Burnham and Badenoch revive red versus blue politics as Reform land 'gobsmacking' donations
News.content:
Look closely at the posters, placards and online posts. Your eyes aren't deceiving you if Labour's red seems a little deeper and the Conservatives' blue a little truer.

Politics seems to have found a new rhythm, one that feels a little familiar, despite Reform's jaw-dropping new donations putting it back in the headlines today.

For the avoidance of doubt, the scale of that initial Â£36m gift to Nigel Farage's party alone is like something from a different political universe.

"It's a gobsmacking sum," a senior figure involved in running successive election campaigns for one of the big parties tells me.

That was even before another Reform donor pledged to match that astonishing sum with another Â£36m, saying the first donation had provoked his "competitive spirit".

But one cabinet minister is enjoying what they see as a newly obvious difference between Labour and the Tories. "It's clarifying," they say, a clear gap between Labour and the Tories' "sense of purpose and values".

A member of Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch's top team tells me, "normal jogging is reasserting itself", hopeful they're at the start of a more straightforward, routine moment in politics after years of craziness, with smaller parties vying to shove the traditional tribes out of the way.

The standout moment was at the despatch box this week when Prime Minister Andy Burnham declared that national security couldn't come at the expense of social security - a phrase immediately seized on by the Tories, interpreting it as the PM saying he'd never cut welfare spending to pay for defence.

News.title: I never got to experience my baby's scan, but blind parents like me can now feel them
News.content:
When I attended pregnancy scans a decade ago, the best the sonographer could do to involve this blind expectant mum was to turn up the volume on the heartbeat.

But now, parents like me can receive tactile 3D models created from their scans, allowing them to have a special moment with their unborn baby.

Reece Finnegan-Knight, who has been blind since his teens, is one of the first people to experience a 3D-printed model of his baby's scan with his wife, Sophy, as part of a new pilot scheme.

At their routine 12-week scan, Sophy had attempted to describe what she was seeing for Reece, but he struggled to feel involved in the moment.

Afterwards, when the couple showed the sonogram to their loved ones, Reece said it felt like "friends and family knew more about my baby than I did".

But he said the 20-week scan was more positive.

"The sonographer described everything to me, and explained why what she was seeing meant that everything looked good," he says.

News.title: Hardened activists are changing tactics and mobilising the anti-migrant vote
News.content:
At around seven o'clock last Saturday morning, dozens of men dressed in black climbed into the backs of lorries in a quiet Kent village called Preston-next-Wingham.

The men had arrived under cover of darkness the night before, leaving their cars everywhere: in the village hall car park and on the recreation ground.

In an operation with a degree of military precision, the small fleet of lorries departed for Dover just after sunrise, where the men staged an intimidating show of strength near the port.

In disciplined, serried ranks, they wore paramilitary-style balaclavas as they blocked roads around the port. There were at least three waves of arrivals, including the men who had spent the night in Preston-next-Wingham. Glaring ominously at motorists and police officers, they stood their ground.

Hardened anti-immigration campaigners were using their newly developed tactics for the first time.

It bore little resemblance to the running battles seen in cities in the Midlands in the days of Tommy Robinson's original vehicle, the anti-Muslim English Defence League (EDL).

"I seriously thought we'd been invaded by Russians," a Dover resident, Robin Burkhardt, told the BBC.

The main organiser Danny Thomas, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, said on Instagram afterwards: "This is our warning."

The style of protest is a new development in the crowded world of British hard-right and far-right politics. It was visually striking, and the men - who were part of a new group called Patriot Platform - chanted "Christ is King" as well as "Stop the Boats".

On Sunday, using a social media live stream, Thomas was able to organise a second, more impromptu protest of a few hundred people in his home city of Portsmouth.

His activists tried to block coaches that had come to collect migrants, who had arrived illegally, brought ashore after making the long journey from Normandy in France.

On Thursday, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood met senior police officers and urged them to make full use of their powers to stop activists wearing face coverings.

"These scenes have caused disruption for people and, given that people are dressed in black wearing balaclavas, there is a fear factor and obvious malign intent being communicated to our residents," she said.

"This makes it different from other protests, so we need to make sure we are learning lessons."

Some of Patriot Platform's disruptive, eye-catching tactics seem to have been borrowed from environmental groups like Just Stop Oil. But its leaders are also getting ideas and funding from the growing "Christian nationalism" seen in the United States.

Its organisers say they are building a working-class "voting bloc" to persuade political parties on the right to adopt their agenda.

News.title: When an avalanche killed climber Nirmal Purja, his friends faced the hardest mission of all
News.content:
As he picked his way past the frozen slope towards two bodies, Mingma Gyalje Sherpa knew his friends were gone.

Together, the three of them had climbed the world's highest peaks, under crisp mountain skies and in treacherous snowstorms. Nirmal Purja and Kili Pemba Sherpa were two of the strongest climbers Mingma G had ever known.

But this July, an avalanche swept through Pakistan's Broad Peak while the two were on their way up, engulfing everything in its path.

The drone images seemed clear: no-one had survived.

And yet, as Mingma G came closer to the fluorescent down suits, sharp against the snow, he couldn't shake the idea they were waiting for him.

"I told them: 'It's ok. You don't have to be here in the cold anymore.'"

Speaking to the BBC in Islamabad, he recalls the terrible moment he reached for their bodies.

Holding one of them, he promised: "I'm here to take you guys home."

News.title: Three arrests at rival protests in Portsmouth
News.content:
The new powers came into effect at 10:00 BST. Participants on both sides were not seen to be wearing any face coverings when the marches started.

The city centre protests follow disorder on 6 September, when police attended Eastney Marina as hundreds of demonstrators blocked roads in an attempt to stop coaches carrying 120 migrants, who had crossed the Channel in a dinghy, from leaving the city.

On Saturday, up to 500 anti-migrant protesters held Union and St George flags while some wearing Portsmouth Patriot branded clothing gathered outside All Saints Church on Commercial Road shortly before midday on Saturday.

The crowd chanted "stop the boats" as they marched to Guildhall Square.

About 300 people joined the counter-protest.

Both sets of demonstrators were kept apart by police when they arrived at the square.

Speaking before the march, Simon Magorian, of Stand up to Racism Portsmouth, described the demonstrations in Eastney as a "horrible spectacle".

He said: "Portsmouth is actually a good functioning multi-cultural city.

"We are now organising to have the broadest possible opposition to what we see as a fascist street movement and we're not going to allow them to get a grip on Portsmouth or any other town - this is quite terrifying."

News.title: Oscar-winning film producer Jeremy Thomas dies aged 77
News.content:
Oscar-winning producer Jeremy Thomas, whose films included The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, has died aged 77.

The British filmmaker "passed away peacefully" surrounded by family and loved ones at his home in Oxfordshire on Friday, his publicist said in a statement.

Thomas built an international reputation over a career spanning five decades, working with directors including David Cronenberg, Nagisa Oshima, Julien Temple and Nicolas Roeg and backing independent films alongside mainstream successes.

His best known film, Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor, won nine Academy Awards, including best picture, and earned Thomas an Oscar as producer in 1988.

The critically-acclaimed biographical drama about the final monarch of China's Qing dynasty starred Joan Chen, Peter O'Toole and Vivian Wu.

Thomas repeatedly collaborated with Bertolucci, also producing The Sheltering Sky, Little Buddha, Stealing Beauty and The Dreamers.

He also worked with several British directors at the start of their careers including Ben Wheatley, Jonathan Glazer, Stephen Frears and David Mackenzie.

Thomas's other credits include Oshima's Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence, starring David Bowie, Cronenberg's A Dangerous Method, Roeg's Bad Timing and Eureka, Fast Food Nation, The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle, and the film adaptations of the JG Ballard books Crash and High-Rise.

After beginning as a film editor, London-based Thomas landed his first production role on the 1976 Australian film Mad Dog Morgan.

In 2006 he received the European Film Academy's award for Outstanding European Achievement in World Cinema and in 2009 was made a CBE in the New Year Honours.

Thomas's latest collaboration with Japanese director Takashi Miike, Bad Lieutenant:Tokyo, is due to premiere at the Toronto Film Festival on Monday.

News.title: Elderly woman found dead named by police
News.content:
An elderly woman whose death sparked a murder investigation has been named by police.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) said Jill Gant, aged 88, was found dead at an address on Appleford Drive in Abingdon, Oxfordshire at about 14:20 BST on Thursday afternoon.

Her family are being supported by specially trained officers.

A 36-year-old man from Abingdon who was arrested on suspicion of murder remains in police custody.

News.title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK
News.content:
A tiny snail found in only one lake in the UK has been dubbed as precious as an Egyptian artefact as conservationists bid to save it.

Several British zoos are setting up so-called ark populations of the glutinous snail, one of Europe's rarest species, using creatures bred in a back garden in Ceredigion.

"Beguiled by their cuteness," conservationist Ian Hughes has made it his "life-defining" mission to protect the threatened mollusc, which was once widespread in UK waters.

"There was a point where we'd got more snails in our garden than have ever been seen in the wild," he said.

News.title: Six people rescued after yacht gets tangled in fish farm
News.content:
Six people have been rescued after a 46ft yacht got into difficulty off the coast of Northern Ireland.

Red Bay Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) spent seven hours at sea in the early hours of Saturday morning off Cushendall, County Antrim.

Belfast Coastguard received a distress call from the boat, which had been travelling from Oban in Scotland to Portugal.

The yacht lost all power and steering after making contact with a fish farm in Red Bay, in 60 knots of wind, causing it to become trapped.

A lifeboat was launched at 03:22 BST, with an inshore lifeboat also launched.

In a statement Red Bay RNLI described the weather conditions as "difficult" due to "Force 9 gusting winds, driving rain and the darkness of night".

The RNLI crew observed that those on the yacht were safe and, given the difficult weather and sea conditions, the decision was made "for the sailors to remain onboard the yacht and for the lifeboat to standby until daylight broke" at 07:30.

At 09.30 the lifeboat crew "successfully freed the yacht from the fish farm and brought the sailors safely to Glenarm".

Those on the yacht stayed onboard the vessel while it was towed by the RNLI, who said there were no injuries.

The yacht is now receiving repairs.

Speaking following the call out, Paddy McLaughlin, Red Bay RNLI Coxswain said: "This was a challenging call out in difficult weather conditions, but we were delighted to bring the sailors to safety, and we would like to wish them well.

"We would also like to commend our colleagues in the Coastguard and thank our crew who responded quickly in the middle of the night, launched our lifeboats in darkness and made their way to the scene in what were gale force conditions, and for then spending seven hours at sea."

News.title: Four arrested during gangland violence 'day of action'
News.content:
Police have arrested four men during a pre-planned "day of action" as part of an ongoing investigation into gangland violence.

Police executed warrants at addresses in Bellshill and Motherwell on Friday and also recovered four stolen vehicles.

One of the men arrested, a 29-year-old, was charged after a car crashed into a house in Eaglesham on Friday 21 August. There were no reports of any injuries. He is due to appear in court on Monday.

It brings the total number of arrests as part of Operation Portaledge to 81.

News.title: Driver threatened with knife as bus hijacked and chased in police pursuit
News.content:
A man has been arrested after a hijacked bus was brought to a stop after a police chase.

The driver of the bus was threatened at knife point by a man, who then allowed passengers to leave the bus. However, the bus driver was kept on board.

Videos circulating on social media appear to show a Translink Goldliner coach being driven at speed through residential streets while being chased by a Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) patrol car.

Police said the bus was hijacked in the Beltany Road area of Omagh, Co Tyrone, shortly before 13:00 BST on Saturday.

The man who hijacked the bus then made off in the direction of Newtownstewart and a pursuit ensued along the A5 through Victoria Bridge and Sion Mills. The pursuit lasted nearly 20 miles.

"The bus was eventually stopped in the Head of the Town area of Strabane and a man, aged in his 30s was removed from the bus and subsequently arrested," said a PSNI spokesperson.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service (NIAS) said two people were taken to South West Acute Hospital for treatment.

The NIAS added that they had dispatched two "emergency crews to the incident" and had initially treated to two patients "at the scene".

A number of reports of collisions involving the stolen bus and other vehicles, including a police car and damage to property have been received by police, who are appealing for information.

The Fountain Street and Drumallagh areas in Strabane remain closed at this time and the public are asked to avoid the area.

Sinn FÃ©in councillor Brian Barney Harte said a wall was damaged at the side of a house in Strabane during the pursuit.

He said people were shocked and distressed, adding that his thoughts were with those involved.

"How there has not been a fatality is only by a miracle," he said.

"Numerous cars and properties have been damaged and people have told me of near misses of pedestrians, some pushing prams."

Barney said the bus came to a stop right beside a children's play park and that a police helicopter was involved in the chase.

A spokesperson for public transport operator Translink NI said: "We can confirm an incident occurred involving a Goldliner coach travelling on the Beltany Road in Omagh this afternoon.

"We are assisting the PSNI with their investigation including use of onboard CCTV and would ask anyone with information relating to the incident to contact the police."

News.title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying
News.content:
MPs have voted against proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end.

Following a debate in which both sides made emotional speeches, the House of Commons voted 286 to 270 - a majority of 16 - against the proposed legislation.

The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill would have allowed adults with fewer than six months to live to apply to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

A similar bill in the last parliamentary session was supported by MPs before stalling in the House of Lords. The decision from MPs on Friday rules out the prospect of changes to the law on assisted dying in the short term.

The bill tabled by Labour MP Lauren Edwards will make no further progress, although MPs and peers could make another attempt in the next parliamentary session.

Assisted dying is an issue that has been debated for hundreds of hours in Parliament over the last two years and would have represented one of the biggest societal changes in recent years had it been approved.

MPs were given a free vote, meaning they were not required to vote along party lines.

Safeguards within the bill included a requirement that a person applying for an assisted death had the approval of two doctors and an expert panel.

But critics said it included too few measures to protect vulnerable people from being coerced into ending their lives, while some say improving palliative care should be the priority.

Free rail transport will be provided over Remembrance weekend to the bereaved relatives of armed forces personnel killed in service, under a new Ministry of Defence initiative.

Under the scheme, eligible families can select one designated next of kin to travel without charge across National Rail networks to attend commemorative events on November 7 and 8, as well as in future years.

Veterans minister Calvin Bailey stated that providing backing to relatives of those who have "given everything for their country" ought to be "a given".

Although Mr Bailey, a former RAF officer who served alongside US special operations forces in Afghanistan, declined to disclose the specific funding allocated for the initiative, he guaranteed that no eligible family members will be turned down.

Speaking at the Cenotaph in central London, he said: "The scheme’s been costed, it’s funded, and it will be continued beyond this year.

"We think this is an essential part of of commemoration. It’s something that I feel perhaps should have just been a given, and I hope it because this shouldn’t be a discussion point.

"This should have been something that we have been doing for a long time. When people give everything for their country, we should give them ensure that their families are able to feel as though they’re part of that connective tissue."

Veterans minister Calvin Bailey ( House of Commons )

He added: "Coming here is a significant event, but coming here can come at great personal expense.

"It’s an emotionally difficult period for those people that have lost someone, but it’s a very significant thing to be at the heart of our national commemorations, and as we’ve heard from those members of bereaved families today, being here in any number helps them to ensure that connection remains.

"This is a small but very significant lifting of the barriers of cost of living and the challenges that people have either with distance or with cost to ensure that they’re part of these commemorations."

The policy expands upon the Government’s existing free travel offer for serving personnel and veterans.

Mr Bailey confirmed he has asked the Department for Transport to ensure there are no "unnecessary impediments" over the Remembrance Day weekend resulting from train delays or cancellations.

Mikki Brett, the widow of the late CPO Stuart Brett – who served in the Weapons Engineering branch of the Royal Navy and died in service in April 2023, said: "It’s fantastic news that the in-service bereaved have been recognised for the support given to their loved ones with free train fares to remembrance events this year."
