Enzo Maresca has revealed he ignores the record-breaking prices he paid for players as he believes the transfer market is “crazy”.

The Manchester City manager equalled the British record when spending £125m on Enzo Fernandez this summer, having already paid £116m for Elliot Anderson, but said he will not judge them on their transfer fees.

Maresca committed £301m to new midfielders, including Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi, and more than £400m to new signings during his first transfer window in charge.

But he admitted the fees are not his concern, saying: “I don’t pay much attention to the price because I don’t pay the money. It’s more about good players.”

Manchester United, who host City on Sunday, also bought three midfielders this summer, but for a cheaper price of an initial £148m.

And Maresca added: “The ones who arrived here and joined United are all top players. That’s the most important thing. How much the club paid for them? I don’t think it’s correct to judge players on how much we pay because the market is crazy.”

Maresca praised City for the way they have replaced the departed duo of Rodri and Bernardo Silva with Fernandez, Anderson and Bouaddi.

And he pointed to the successful way that City have been able to replace their great players in the recent past.

He said: “I feel very lucky because these three players arrived, the three midfielders, Enzo, Eliot and Ayyoub. And I also said that this club, when [Sergio] Aguero left, everyone was worried, Erling [Haaland] arrived, Fernandinho [left], Rodri arrived, David Silva [left], [Kevin] De Bruyne arrived.

“So one of the big achievements of this club has been to replace players and it's not easy. Before, the club was Txiki [Begiristain, the former director of football] when he was here, now the club with Hugo [Viana]. So for sure I feel very lucky because it's not easy to replace these kind of players, they are top players.”

Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka helped maintain Arsenal’s perfect start in the Premier League with a 2-0 win over Sunderland.

Following a controlled first half, the Gunners were handed a scare 11 minutes after the restart when the hosts were awarded a penalty, but David Raya made a brilliant save to palm Enzo Le Fee’s spot-kick against the left post.

A dramatic twist saw Arsenal lead just two minutes later through a fantastic top-corner finish from Guimaraes, his first goal since joining in the summer from Sunderland’s bitter rivals Newcastle.

open image in gallery Bruno Guimaraes scored his first Arsenal goal ( PA )

More drama followed in stoppage time when Reinildo Mandava was sent off and Saka scored from the penalty spot to cement Arsenal’s fourth Premier League win from as many games, while the Wearsiders slipped to their second league defeat.

Sunderland named an unchanged team from their draw at Brentford, while Arsenal made four switches from their midweek Champions League victory over Napoli as Riccardo Calafiori, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz all started.

Arsenal offered an early glimpse of danger when Declan Rice picked out Saka, who got in behind before flicking a tame effort into the arms of Robin Roefs.

Former Arsenal man Granit Xhaka then threatened for the hosts when his whipped free-kick found Dan Ballard, who headed wide.

open image in gallery Sunderland threatened at times ( PA )

The Gunners controlled the tempo but struggled to break through the Black Cats’ defence and Gabriel Magalhaes saw his low strike from outside of the box fizz wide.

Martin Odegaard moved unmarked behind Sunderland’s defence before cutting the ball back for Havertz and the forward blasted over, before coming close again moments later with a hooked effort which Roefs tipped over.

Arsenal’s frustrations continued as Mikel Arteta was shown a yellow card and Sunderland began to sniff around the visitors’ box when Thomas Meunier’s strike was deflected behind before Le Fee fired wide.

The Gunners looked to strike on the stroke of half-time when Saka’s cross was flicked away by Xhaka.

open image in gallery Arsenal remain perfect in the Premier League ( pA )

Sunderland looked bright after the restart as Meunier’s effort was blocked and the hosts had an opportunity to take the lead from the penalty spot in the 56th minute.

Referee John Brooks pointed to the spot when Ballard was brought down by Ezri Konsa in the area and Le Fee’s penalty was denied by Raya.

The champions suddenly took the lead in the 58th minute when Guimaraes fired a superb strike from outside of the area, which crashed off the underside of the crossbar and into the net.

The visitors nearly caught Sunderland on the break when Odegaard played in Saka, who was denied by Roefs and Ballard made a goal-line clearance from the resultant corner.

open image in gallery Bukayo Saka sealed the points from the penalty spot in added time (Owen Humphreys/PA) ( PA )

Guimaraes curled an effort just wide and the Black Cats then had a promising opportunity when Nordi Mukiele’s backheeled effort was blocked.

Jurrien Timber’s header from a free-kick was ruled out for offside and Mukiele came close again for Sunderland, hooking a strike over before having another effort saved by Raya.

Late drama followed when Reinildo was shown a second yellow card at the death and Saka slotted home from the penalty spot in the seventh additional minute to seal three points.

PA

News.title: South Africa v New Zealand LIVE: Latest updates as Springboks and All Blacks battle in Baltimore
News.content:
( AP )

South Africa and New Zealand conclude a thrilling four-Test series with one last meeting in the novel surroundings of Baltimore.

The Springboks took an unassailable 2-1 lead in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series with success in the last encounter on South African soil last week, and the world champions will seek to make another statement here. A strong side has been named by Rassie Erasmus as he looks to avoid a drawn series – with the All Blacks sure to be highly charged after consecutive defeats and the loss of captain Ardie Savea to a shoulder injury.

This clash takes place at the home of the NFL’s Baltimore Ravens, and takes place in the USA in the name of rugby’s global expansion. With two World Cup Stateside on the horizon in the men’s and women’s game, this is another useful staging post for the sport as it looks to build fans and showcase its thrills and spills – and what better fixture to do exactly that?

Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani disclosed what he told Mayor Zohran Mamdani during their viral face-to-face exchange at Friday’s ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terror attacks.

The two men shook hands and briefly exchanged words at the Manhattan ceremony, which drew scores of political figures, including all living former presidents.

Before the event, Giuliani had publicly opposed Mamdani’s attendance and claimed that the city’s first-ever Muslim mayor wants his religion “to dominate us.”

In a livestream afterward, Giuliani, a Republican who was in office during the 2001 terrorist attacks, recounted his interaction with Mamdani, a democratic socialist elected last year.

“Now, I shook hands with Mamdani,” Giuliani told Tony Carbonetti, his former chief of staff.

open image in gallery Rudy Giuliani revealed what he said to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during their viral handshake at the 9/11 anniversary ceremony ( AP )

“Did you wash them afterward?” Carbonetti replied.

“No,” Giuliani said. “I am not, at a ceremony like this…I am not gonna cause any ridiculous anything.”

Giuliani said he believed he had extended his hand first, though he acknowledged Mamdani may have initiated the handshake.

“So we shook hands and I said to him, ‘I pray for you,’ and he said ‘thank you,’ and we just went our ways,” he said.

“I think both of us knew, both of us had ended up facing each other, so we knew we could create a distraction, and either one of us could’ve turned around and said ‘go to hell,’ and that becomes the whole story, instead of these poor people,” Giuliani continued, referring to the 2,753 people who died at the World Trade Center. “And I commend him also for shaking hands with me.”

open image in gallery Bill Clinton, Michelle Obama, Barack Obama, Jill Biden, Joe Biden, Laura Bush, George W. Bush, Michael Bloomberg, JD Vance, Rudy Giuliani, Howard Lutnick, George Pataki, Kathy Hochul, Bill Hochul, Zohran Mamdani and New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill attend ceremony to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terrorist attacks ( Getty Images )

Less than one week earlier, Giuliani told Newsmax that he opposed Mamdani attending the downtown event. “It offends me that he's coming,” he said before making broader anti-Muslim claims.

“They have every desire to take us over,” he said. “This is not, ‘they want to be just another religion.’ They want to dominate us...Mamdani is a clear — a clear — supporter of that. All of the Muslims he supports are murderers.”

Other Republicans, including former New York Governor George Pataki, also urged Mamdani to skip the event. Some cited his association with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, who once said that “America deserved 9/11.”

Mamdani, who has called the 2001 attacks “horrific,” confirmed before Friday that he would attend the ceremony, as previous mayors have.

“I will proudly honor the families, the survivors, the first responders forever impacted by that horrific terror attack by standing alongside them at this year's 9/11 commemoration, reaffirming that we will never forget the solemn day felt by all of us who call this city home and, frankly, by all of us who call this country home,” he told City & State.

Last week, Mamdani also appeared to take a veiled swipe at Giuliani when he released more than 170,000 pages of internal records indicating that officials misled the public about the safety of the air around Ground Zero after the September 11 attacks.

“People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air,” Mamdani said during a news conference.

The Independent has contacted the mayor’s office for comment.

Leading tech figures Sam Altman and Elon Musk have aligned themselves with a call from the head of Anthropic for the artificial intelligence (AI) sector to "slow down" and allow safety measures to keep pace.

In an essay titled “We Must Pace the Frontier”, Dario Amodei warned that the development of AI has been "advancing drastically faster" since the summer.

He expressed concern that, at current rates of progress, AI could be equipped within six to 12 months to command a swarm capable of taking over the internet.

The entrepreneur, whose company developed the Claude AI assistant, proposed a three-stage roadmap designed to foster innovation at a "balanced rate".

"I believe that if slowing down bought us even an extra year or two before models reach critical levels of capability, and we used that time to advance alignment, we could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong," Mr Amodei said.

Prominent industry voices have rallied behind the essay, including Mr Musk and Mr Altman.

Replying to Mr Amodei’s essay on X, Mr Musk wrote: "Dario is right."

OpenAI chief executive Mr Altman wrote on the platform: "I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier. This has been a primary topic of discussions we’ve had at OpenAI in recent weeks.

"Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same. We’ll have more to share soon."

Mr Amodei’s proposals include granting external evaluators access to monitor corporate safety mechanisms and log potential risks.

"Anthropic is unilaterally committing to this step now," he said.

Subsequent stages would demand international co-ordination across the wider industry and among governments globally, including authoritarian states.

Highlighting how rapidly the technology is evolving, Mr Amodei said tech firms "can and should voluntarily work together to set standards".

Anthropic has previously disclosed that it stopped bad actors using its systems for harmful ends, such as cyber attacks, surveillance, and work that could assist in creating biological weapons.

Worry over potential harm from AI deepened this week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, stating that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

Elon Musk supported Amodei’s call for a slowing down of AI development ( Reuters )

The warnings follow an admission in July by OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, that its system had independently breached another company in an "unprecedented cyber incident."

Elsewhere, Altman said in a Fortune interview published Saturday, that OpenAI will not go public in 2026 citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence.

"I actually think that, given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don't feel pressure on that," Altman told Fortune.

When asked whether 2026 is off the table in favour of 2027, Altman said, "I would say not 2026. Yeah, we got a lot of stuff to do, like meeting this moment of what is going to be required for safety and alignment, and how the industry and governments can work together."

News.title: Sunderland v Arsenal LIVE: Premier League champions continue unbeaten start thanks to Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka
News.content:
Bruno put Arsenal in front ( PA )

Bruno Guimaraes was sprung from the bench to set Arsenal on their way to a battling 2-0 win away to Sunderland, with Bukayo Saka adding a penalty deep in added time to ensure the champions' 100% start to the season continues.

The half-time substitute Guimaraes, formerly of Newcastle United, drove a right-footed attempt in off the bar before cupping his ears in front of the home fans.

Guimaraes' goal arrived moments after David Raya had saved Enzo Le Fee's penalty kick, following a foul by Ezri Konsa on Dan Ballard.

Raya also produced a brilliant late save to deny Nordi Mukiele from close range as Mikel Arteta, who was booked in the first half for stepping out of his technical area, saw his team bag a late second when Saka was fouled in the box and converted his own spot kick.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes picks perfect moment to score first Arsenal goal
News.content:
Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée was denied by a superb David Raya stop from 12 yards, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players
News.content:
Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

News.title: Lando Norris on pole for Spanish GP but adds voice to critics of ‘Madring’
News.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen predicted that overtaking would be “practically impossible” in the race. “[The Madring] has a tendency of maybe creating some big shunts in some places,” the Dutchman said. “It reminds me a little bit of Jeddah in a way – fast corners and the walls being very close.

“The only thing that’s already a bit disappointing is that many of the braking zones are angled. This means it’s practically impossible to attack a competitor because you’re braking and simultaneously turning right or left. And that’s the worst thing you can do if you want to create an overtaking opportunity.”

Norris agreed with Verstappen that it would be very difficult to overtake, although that is no bad thing for him provided he can hang on to the lead at the start.

The Briton, though, described the decision to build what is now the longest pit lane on the F1 calendar as a big disappointment.

“I think it has a lot of potential,” Norris said of the Madring. “Just certain things need to be improved. Like the pit lane, which is like six kilometres long. It’s the longest pit lane of the year and the biggest pit loss of the year [in terms of the time it will take to pit – an estimated 25 seconds]. So that just makes overtaking worse. Not overtaking, but it makes the desire to box and do different strategies worse.

“You know, if we’re going to build a new track and spend so much money in building a new track, this is probably one of the main factors, I would say, is you have a short pit lane so people can pit and you then create overtaking.”

Norris described his pole lap as “one of the best laps of his career” and his team principal Andrea Stella fully agreed, describing it as “a masterpiece”.

News.title: Bomb squad rescues rusty Red Roses
News.content:
Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald went over for further tries to add to player-of-the-match Abi Burton’s first-half score.

Moloney-MacDonald’s try wide out on the left was a show-stopper for the crowd of 9,251 in the North West and demonstrated that England have style to go with solidity. But it was the power game that did for Australia.

The Wallaroos scored tries of their own through Faliki Pohiva and Eva Karpani but spent the vast majority of the game manning the defensive barricades. They did so admirably for 40 minutes but when the dam wall blew it blew spectacularly.

They did not help themselves with sin-binnings in either half for Samantha Wood and Karpani, but over 80 minutes the odds will always be stacked in favour of the full-time side against the part-timers.

“The reality is that even at our best we’re probably not good enough. We will be,” said Tim Walsh, Rugby Australia’s director of women’s high performance. “We need an environment where they can concentrate on being full-time athletes. That’s the vision Rugby Australia have and that’s where we’re headed.”

The game was England’s first with the smaller ball being trialled in the women’s game by World Rugby and they only converted four of their eight tries, a statistic which may be seized upon by those who do not care for it. A rugby pitch is not a sterile laboratory though and the swirling, blustery conditions should be taken into account in any dissection of its value.

News.title: Jordan Cox looks a Joe Root clone as pair steer England home
News.content:
There is perhaps no batsman in Test history as accustomed as Joe Root to walking in with the scoreboard reading “not many for two” and his team in a tight spot.

That is where Root found himself once again soon after 11am on Saturday. His team were two for two, with both openers out for ducks, and the problems of the third evening bleeding into the fourth morning. A chaotic and patchwork Pakistan team suddenly believed Mohammad Abbas could inspire their defence of 130.

A familiar position for Root, sure, but not the young man at the other end, the rookie No 3 Jordan Cox. Together, they eased England out of a creeping crisis with such aplomb that the target was chased swiftly enough that the few thousand at Edgbaston were refunded 50 per cent of their ticket prices because so few overs were bowled. When Cox hit the winning run, a scrambled single into the off side, Root’s relief was palpable. His team had been tested, and he felt they would be “better for it”.

They had won his first series since returning to the captaincy 3-0, but not without a scare at the last. The scorecard will record this as a routine England eight-wicket win and, for the most part, it was. But England were rattled by Razaullah, a 21-year-old who spent the first two Tests of this series in Mardan, in the mountains of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region near Pakistan’s border with Afghanistan. Having bowled quickly, he wreaked havoc on the third evening with his 63-ball 81, taking England from the brink of an innings victory to an awkward chase.

Razaullah’s partner with the bat was Abbas, who provided England with an almighty fright on the fourth morning. First ball, Ben Duckett was caught behind. The ball was angled in, demanding that it was played, then nipped slightly away, taking the edge. Duckett’s trudge off was glacial, with his curious Test summer over. He has scored England’s only century of the season, but failed to make fifty otherwise. In this series, he has averaged just eight.

News.title: Razaullah’s incredible hitting scrambles England’s minds
News.content:
England will look to complete the series whitewash as they hold a commanding position coming into day three of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston in what could be the final day of the English Test summer.

England finished up their first innings on 453 on day two, with a mammoth 320-run lead over Pakistan. Five England batsmen passed the fifty mark; Emilio Gay, Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith and Ollie Robinson, but none went on to convert those half centuries into hundreds. It means that Ben Duckett’s century against New Zealand at Trent Bridge back in June will be the only England Test hundred of the summer, the first time that has happened in a six-Test summer. England managed 21 half centuries over the course of the summer, so it works out as 4.76% conversion rate.

Having seen England pile on the runs, Pakistan then lost a wicket with the first ball of their second innings, with Saim Ayub making a pair to sum up a miserable return to their Test side for the opener having been jettisoned in as part of wholesale changes for the visitors. Abdullah Shafique followed three balls later, with Robinson taking both wickets as his fine summer continued. Robinson now has 28 wickets across four Tests this summer at a staggering average of 7.75. Joe Root made history yesterday, taking his 220th catch, the most by an outfielder in Test history. Rain though prevented England the opportunity of potentially wrapping up a two-day finish in a Test in this country for the first time since 2000.

Pakistan will resume on 52/2, still 268 runs behind England, with Azan Awais resuming on 29 not out and will be joined by Shan Masood, who is on 21. Pakistan are yet to reach 200 or bat more than 51 overs in this series so the series whitewash may not be a million miles away. Will we see any rare Pakistan resistance in this series or will England’s seamers dominate again? Play on day three from Edgbaston is set to get under at 11am and it could be the final day of not just the series but the English Test summer.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6pc in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6pc, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7pc.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney smoked and drank beer with other players while on England duty, explosive new book by Andy Carroll claims
Sports.content:
WAYNE ROONEY smoked cigarettes and drank beer with other players while on England international duty, according to an explosive new book by one of his Three Lions teammates.

Former Newcastle and Liverpool striker Andy Carroll has lifted the lid on secrets from inside the England camp, ­including how Rooney invited stars to join him for the drinking session during a ­training camp.



In exclusive extracts from Andy’s autobiography Owning It, he calls Rooney “one of the good guys” who was “normal” and “very, very funny”.

Andy, who also played for West Ham, got his first England call-up in 2010 under strict Italian boss Fabio Capello.



He writes of Rooney: “He’d call me at two in the ­afternoon and say, ‘Andy, my room, now’. ‘Nah’, I’d say, ‘not now Wazza, it’s too early’.

“But he’d always bully me into submission. I’d find him lying on his bed watching TV, smoking (his lips would sometimes be bulging with snus — smokeless tobacco — as well) and swigging a bottle of beer.



“He’d be surrounded by cartons of fags, crates of lager and ­bottles of wine (which he got the hotel manager to deliver to his room), and soon his room would be full of players. No one got smashed, it was just Wazza’s way of breaking the monotony with a couple of drinks, which was preferable to lying on our beds and staring at the walls.”

According to Carroll’s book, the “get togethers” happened around 2010-2011, during Cappello’s time as the England manager.

Despite the Italian coach’s reputation as a tough disciplinarian, Carroll’s book de­tails how the squad manag­ed to un­wind be­hind closed doors.

And in another extract, he reveals a prank Rooney, now 40, played on the England team physio Rod Thornley, in front of him and midfielder ­Steven Gerrard.



Carroll writes: “When I told Wazza about the three-man lift prank (when two players hold someone down while another sits on him) he got very excited and exclaimed, “We’ve got to get Rod Thornley.”

The “joke” involved Rooney — who scored 53 Three Lions goals and won 120 caps — sitting on top of Thornley on the physio-room treatment table, according to Andy.

Carroll, who now plays for National League South side Dagenham and Redbridge, says: “Rod was screaming, me and Gerrard were crying laughing, and Wazza had never looked so pleased with himself.”



Wayne Rooney said: “I don’t normally comment on falsehoods written about me — but I will address this one.

“Andy knows that he and I never really socialised. I bumped into him once, coincidentally, whilst on a holiday — but that’s about it.

“As for this ‘tale’ about me drinking on England duty, it’s a complete fabrication.

“I don’t know where the story comes from. It’s disappointing.”

Andy made his debut for England in a 2-1 friendly defeat against France at Wembley in November 2010, months after the Three Lions had crashed out of the World Cup in a last-16 defeat to Germany.



He featured in the same squad as Rooney — who went on to be England skipper and is now a TV pundit — 11 times as he made nine appearances for the national team.

In the book, No9 Carroll reveals that England’s so-called “Golden Generation” was plagued by a North-South divide.

The Three Lions had star players including Rooney, Gerrard, Frank Lampard, Joe Cole, John Terry, ­Ashley Cole and Jamie Carragher at the time, but failed to win any major ­silverware.

Geordie Carroll writes: “When I turned up to my first England camp, I was properly ­anxious.



CAPELLO IN MIX-UP OVER GRANNY SEX By MICHAEL HAMILTON IN an embarrassing incident, Andy Carroll reveals England’s then- manager Fabio Capello appeared to confuse him with another player. Recounting how Capello enlisted the services of his centre-back to discipline him, the striker writes: “One evening, John Terry knocked on my door. ‘The gaffer wants a word’, he said. “ ‘What, why?’ I said, confused. “ ‘He’s not happy with your behaviour outside of football.’ ” “I later found out John had gone to Capello and said he needed to speak to me because I was out of control. “No sooner had I walked into this meeting with Capello than he started berating me. ‘You’re always in the media for drinking and sleeping with grannies,’ he said. “I was thinking, ‘What is this fella on about? Has he got me mixed up with one of my teammates?’ “In the end, I just had to accept it. ‘Yeah all right,’ I said. ‘It won’t happen again.’ ”

“These guys were known by every football fan, and I looked up to every one of them.

“It was a bit like your first week at secondary school. There were even rival gangs.

“The lads from the northern clubs would sit on one side of the room and lads from southern clubs would sit on the other side — apart from one rogue Man United player who’d sit with the southern group because he didn’t want to sit with the ­Liverpool players.

“There were players who literally didn’t speak to each other and were reluctant to pass to each other in training.

“It’s depressing to think that England didn’t give themselves a proper chance of winning anything during that period because of those petty rivalries within the group. I got the impression the southern players looked down on the northern players.



“In the end, I gravitated towards the northern group.”

Explaining life under Capello, Carroll says: “The gaffer Fabio was slightly crazy. One day me and Ashley Young decided to head down for a meeting 15 minutes early.

“I was sitting on the floor looking at my phone when Capello walked in, marched over and snatched it out of my hand.



“ ‘We are trying to work here’, he barked. ‘You’re disrespectful f***ing using your phone’.

“With that, he threw the phone at my chest.

“I thought, ‘I’m 15 minutes early for your meeting, what is your problem?’ Ashley, who had hidden his phone up his shirt, looked terrified.”

He added: “Capello would let us have a glass of wine and dessert with lunch and dinner — chocolate cake, ice cream, whatever — but wouldn’t allow ketchup.

“It made no sense — why wine and dessert but no ketchup?”



Carroll, whose career has been plagued by injuries, made the England Euros 2012 squad after missing out on the World Cup two years earlier.

He scored in a thrilling 3-2 win over Sweden in the group stages but the Three Lions, by this time led by manager Roy Hodgson, crashed out in the quarter-finals on penalties to Italy.

Talking about that shootout failure, Carroll writes: “I got flak after the game for not taking a penalty but I had no say in it. I don’t recall anyone announcing who would take the first five in an actual shootout.



“And against Italy, (coach) Gary Neville just pointed at players and said, ‘One, two, three, four, five — you’re our penalty takers’.

His picks included Ashley Young and Ashley Cole, neither of whom were strikers, even though me and Theo Walcott were on the pitch.

“As it was, the two Ashleys missed and (Italy’s midfielder Andrea) Pirlo scored the naughtiest penalty I’ve ever seen — a little dink down the middle — and we were out.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Getting knocked out was ­horrible. Imagine being nine days into a two-week holiday, having a total blast and someone kicking your door down, turfing you out of the hotel, dragging you on to a bus and whisking you to the airport. It was a bit like that.”



SWEATING SULLIVAN’S SICK BRAG WHEN Andy signed for West Ham he visit­ed then-chairman David Sullivan, and recounts an odd conversation. He was on loan there in 2012, then made permanent a year later. Sullivan, 77, was accused of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour – which he denies – by the BBC in June and has stepped down from roles at the Hammers. Carroll writes: “My first port of call was David Sullivan’s massive gaff in Essex. “When his housekeeper opened the front door she said, ‘He’s exercising at the moment, take a seat in his office’. “Sullivan appeared after about 20 minutes wearing an oversized Dolce & Gabbana hoodie and sweating like a race­horse. He said to me, ‘Did my housekeeper say I was exercising?’ “ ‘Yeah,’ I said. “ ‘Look out the window.’ I did as I was told and saw a girl of 18 or 19 getting into a taxi. ‘That’s who I’ve been exercising,’ he added triumphantly.”

THAT decision to exile Richarlison is looking riskier by the week.

Because right now Spurs’ goal threat is so negligible, they can ill-afford to shun one of their few players who actually knows how to hit the back of the onion bag.



Boss Roberto De Zerbi insists he had no other choice but to leave wantaway Richarlison out of his Premier League squad following his behaviour in the last month and a half.

But after this toothless stalemate made it four league games, no wins and no goals scored so far this season – despite more than £350million spent – fans will continue to question the sense in ostracising the 29-year-old.



Richarlison was top-scorer last season with 11 Prem goals but was sat watching from the sidelines here, unable to take part.

Meanwhile, De Zerbi’s expensively-assembled new side looked like they would not score in 900 minutes, let alone 90, barring a decent opening quarter of an hour.



They would have lost, too, had Brennan Johnson – the man who won Spurs their first trophy in 17 years with his Europa League final winner two seasons ago – not blazed over late on for Everton.

Regardless of their mega-bucks summer, fans have no idea where their next win is coming from and will be fearing another season toiling at the wrong end of the league.

Spurs actually started OK, particularly through lively widemen Savio and Omar Marmoush.

Jan Paul van Hecke blazed over an early chance when attempting to half-volley home Andy Robertson’s floated free-kick.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

While Van Hecke also played a great ball through for Mateus Fernandes, but the £85million midfielder ended up dribbling into traffic.

After that exciting opening quarter of an hour, though, Everton weathered the storm and suddenly Spurs were looking as short of creativity as they have for much of the campaign.

End product, once again, was sorely lacking.

Coached by the vastly experienced David Moyes, the Toffees looked comfortable and seemed happy for Spurs to have the ball, so long as it was far away from their goal.

It is not like Everton carried much of a threat, either.



Ainsley Maitland-Niles attempted one effort from range but could not replicate his wonderstrike against Manchester United from last week, dragging well wide.

The atmosphere in the ground grew flatter and flatter as the half wore on.

Fans had seen this film far too many times before and seemed in need of a spark from the team to get going, rather than being the ones to supply it to the players with their support.



Everton almost nicked an opener just before the break through James Garner’s free-kick, which had to be smartly palmed away by Antonin Kinsky.

There were no boos as the players went in for the break but you could sense the frustration and anxiety.

Not only had Spurs now made it seven halves of Premier League football this season without a goal.



But the fear was it could get a whole lot worse after the interval if things went against their side, as they have so often done here in the last few years.

Worryingly for De Zerbi, there were ironic cheers from fans when Fernandes fired a tame shot on target from distance two minutes into the second half.

Then came a flurry of Toffees chances, first via Thierno Barry, whose close-range header was saved by Kinsky’s face.

Barry then should have played Brennan Johnson clean through moments later, but inexplicably played it left to Tyrique George, whose cross was blocked.

It was a poor choice as Johnson, who netted the winner in the Europa League final for Spurs two seasons ago, was waiting to pounce.



George then hit a sweet strike which probably would have gone in were it not for a Rodrigo Bentancur’s excellent block.



Bentancur was outstanding in last week’s 0-0 at Nottingham Forest, but even the Uruguayan was looking jittery here as he horribly miscued a routine pass and gave away possession.

Despite the stalemate scoreline, and the lack of goals all season, De Zerbi subbed off centre-forward Dominic Solanke just after the hour, along with Fernandes and Bentancur.

In fairness, the England striker had been anonymous all game and never came close to hitting the net.

With every passing minute, the nerve-jangling intensified around the stadium and for the men in white on the pitch.

It was not helped by Kinsky firing a routine pass out to Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, who had a great opportunity to score but he could not beat the relieved Czech.



Johnson then had a golden chance of his own when Dewsbury-Hall cut it back to him inside the area, but the Welshman’s effort flew over the bar.

He was subbed immediately afterwards and the Spurs fans gave him a standing ovation.

It was because of his Europa League heroics but it could easily have been for his generous miss just seconds before.

Sub Lucas Bergvall drew a smart stop from Jordan Pickford in the final minutes.

But had it gone in it would have been far more than Spurs deserved, as De Zerbi’s side were booed off at the final whistle.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi caught berating Tottenham star after performance branded 'disgrace'
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi caught berating Tottenham star after performance branded 'disgrace'

Roberto De Zerbi's animated interaction with Mathys Tel following the full-time whistle after Tottenham's dismal goalless draw with Everton on Saturday evening has caused a stir

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi lambasted Mathys Tel after the full-time whistle (Image: Mark Leech/Getty Images)

Roberto De Zerbi showed his frustrations in a passionate conversation with Mathys Tel after Tottenham's goalless run continued in a dismal 0-0 draw against Everton on Saturday.

‌



Spurs have now gone over 400 minutes without scoring in the Premier League, with their heavy spending in the summer transfer window yet to bring any improvement in attack. The home side mustered just two shots on target against Everton, prompting some boos at the final whistle.

‌



De Zerbi is never shy in showing his emotions and the way he approached and appeared to admonish Tel in from of the Sky Sports cameras caught the attention of many fans. Tel was introduced in the 63rd minute for Dominic Solanke but couldn't turn the tide.

‌



The Spurs boss was seen gesticulating while trying to explain something to the French forward before abruptly walking off. It didn't go down well with Spurs fans on X. "You can't be mad at him... Stop playing him," one wrote.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"This clown is about to lose the players," a second added. "His man management stinks," a third wrote.

De Zerbi touched on the confrontation in his post-match press conference. "I can't say nothing as an attitude, as a behaviour of the players, no, no. I said to stay calm, maybe to not lose the confidence because we are not scoring, we are not winning," he said.

"Stay calm, improve, work hard and individually try to understand where is the improvement, no? I spoke with Mathys Tel just at the end of the game to explain what was his position today."

‌



A second consecutive 0-0 draw leaves Spurs 17th in the Premier League -- the position they have finished in the last two campaigns.

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi's interaction with Mathys Tel caught the attention of Spurs fans (Image: Shaun Brooks/Getty Images)

"As professionals you're going to look at that, six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a disgrace," Ashley Young said on Sky Sports. "It's not good enough at all and there needs to be a big conversation amongst the players.

‌



"The players need to talk and say: 'We need to take this on ourselves. We've brought in players and we're just not scoring goals, we're not creating chances and we're not looking like a team that's going to score'."

"We played well for the first 30 minutes but then maybe lost energy because our physical condition isn't the best and we are working on that," De Zerbi told Sky Sports. "We didn't shoot for the quality of the play we showed. We have to shoot more times on goal. We went inside the Everton area 74 times but didn't create the a good enough chance to explain the quality of the play we did.

"We have to work for sure and analyse the last decision. We made too many wrong decisions, but I think we played well."

Article continues below

Asked about the frustration of not scoring in the Premier League, De Zerbi replied: "No, I'm not a journalist, I don't write on social media. I just coach and I have to analyse the performances of my players. I have to analyse the potential situation where we could shoot, could score, could make better decisions."

Sports.title: Former Man Utd forward faces ban after 'offensive' gesture towards fans
Sports.content:
Former Man Utd forward faces ban after 'offensive' gesture towards fans

The Dutchman is facing an investigation after an incident in the Copa Libertadores

View 2 Images Memphis Depay is facing a possible ban. (Image: Marcos Brindicci, Getty Images)

Ex-Manchester United forward Memphis Depay could be handed a possible ban after being accused of making an 'offensive' gesture. The Dutchman was in action for Brazilian side Corinthians.

They took on Estudiantes in the first leg of the Copa Libertadores quarter-final. They were 1-0 down at half-time thanks to Alex Castro's fourth-minute goal.

Corinthians were, however, able to draw level in the 49th minute through Kaio Cesar. During the celebrations, Depay appears to put his middle finger up towards the home fans.

The crowd responded with a chorus of boos and jeers. Depay also claimed to the referee that an object had been hurled in his direction.

Man Utd in astonishment over JJ Gabriel after Michael Carrick makes feelings clear READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes disclosure about Man Utd training says it all about Marcus Rashford READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Yet it was his gesture that prompted Estudiantes to lodge a formal complaint. Following the match, the club confirmed they had "'filed a complaint with the CONMEBOL disciplinary unit regarding the offensive gestures made by opposing player Memphis Depay, which were undeniably directed towards our stands."

The second leg of the quarter-final is scheduled for next week, and in response, Corinthians highlighted a regulation that should permit their forward to feature in the fixture. "The deadline for submitting a defence, set by CONMEBOL, is September 17, one day after the Copa Libertadores quarter-final second leg," they stated.

"Therefore, any potential sanction would only be applied after the ruling, which will take place following the presentation of the defence. Respecting the deadline, Corinthians will present this defence to avoid any type of sanction against Memphis Depay."

View 2 Images Memphis Depay during his time at Manchester United. (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

While the regulations suggest Depay is likely to feature in the second leg, he could still face a suspension for future fixtures if found guilty.

The 32-year-old spent two and a half years at United, making 53 appearances during that spell, netting seven goals and chipping in with five assists.

His future was shrouded in doubt this summer after the player publicly hit out at Corinthians for failing to offer him a contract extension. "Very disappointed to read that Corinthians decided not to honour our agreement in place to extend my contract for two more years," he wrote on social media.

"This renewal was explicitly agreed upon by the president as well as the sporting, legal and financial department. Some people decided however to breach this engagement.

"I didn't want this situation and always respected the club throughout the process, but now I am forced to react strongly in order to preserve my interests. In the upcoming days I will speak publicly but rest assured that I will not leave this unacceptable behaviour unsanctioned."

Depay ultimately put pen to paper on a fresh deal with the club, albeit after agreeing to take a considerable reduction in wages.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola needs to find his best Liverpool XI fast after ponderous Fulham draw
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola needs to find his best Liverpool XI fast after ponderous Fulham draw

Andoni Iraola's tactical tinkering against Fulham showed he doesn't know his best Liverpool XI, or how to juggle his unperforming squad across different competitions

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola couldn't get a performance out of his Liverpool side (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

Four minutes of added time had just been signalled when Dominik Szoboszlai was given a set-piece opportunity from fully 30 yards out.

‌



And everyone knows what he can do from there. Even those escaping the torture early stopped in the gangways. There was an expectant hush. Szoboszlai lined up his free-kick with the care of a Ryder Cup golfer on the 18th.

‌



And then hit it at the wall.

‌



That just about summed up his afternoon, that just about summed up Liverpool’s afternoon.

It is going to be a steep learning curve for Andoni Iraola, that is for sure. But his team’s tepid performance should take nothing away from Fulham, easily the more pleasing side on the eye in a largely forgettable contest.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

A statistic doing the rounds ahead of kick-off was that no other Premier League team had taken more touches in the opposition penalty area than Fulham this season. And they were clearly keen to consolidate their position in that particular table, over-elaboration meaning they somehow failed to capitalise on a shocking Alisson pass early in the first half.

In modern parlance, it is under-performing your xG. In old money, it is rank bad finishing. Mind you, it should not have mattered as Alisson’s reckless attempt to compensate for his mistake should have given Fulham a penalty but, mysteriously, the officials decided otherwise. It was a strange one.

‌



It was a big let-off for Liverpool. In fact, the whole afternoon felt like a big let-off for Liverpool. Perhaps their Champions League exertions had taken something out of them but so early in the season, that seems hard to believe.

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz was ineffective for Liverpool (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

But for long spells, they were desperately ponderous. It would be harsh to single out any players but the adaptation period for Florian Wirtz is becoming worryingly lengthy. He seldom looks as though he is going to be clinical and was oddly wasteful with possession.

‌



It said everything about Liverpool’s performance that Iraola had made three tactical substitutions before the hour mark. And it was five 10 minutes later.

Some new managers can hit the ground running, others take longer to fully understand the players they have at their disposal. Iraola is clearly in the second category.

He started with Kostas Tsimikas but had seen enough by half-time and clearly has issues in the full-back positions. He also appears unsure of his best midfield combination. The one he started with against Fulham probably won’t get too many more chances.

‌



View 3 Images Alisson was fortunate to get away with an early blunder (Image: Getty Images)

Fulham walked through them at will. But Alvaro Arbeloa’s side is still without a Premier League victory and they will be beating themselves up for not ending that winless run.

They did not create many clearcut chances but frequently got into positions that should have enabled them to do exactly that. And in Josh King, they had the liveliest performer on the park - that was until Arbeloa decided to take him off for some strange reason.

‌



The contrast between King and Wirtz was stark. But after the managers had finished substituting players, Liverpool finally picked up some momentum and had a couple of half-chances to steal what would have been an undeserved win.

Rio Ngumoha threatened to cause more problems than Bradley Barcola had and Alexis Mac Allister also probed with some intent. But in keeping with Szoboszlai’s long-ranger, though, their work in Fulham’s penalty area lacked any sort of excellence. It was their worst display of the season, that is for sure. They were largely second best.

And while there were no jeers at the full-time whistle, there was a quiet disapproval of what had just been served up by the home side. If there has been any sort of honeymoon for Iraola - and he is still unbeaten as Liverpool manager, don’t forget - it is over now.

Sports.title: Derby vs Birmingham halted as player goes down off the ball and medical staff rush in
Sports.content:
Derby vs Birmingham halted as player goes down off the ball and medical staff rush in

The Championship clash between Derby and Birmingham was brought to a temporary halt

View 2 Images Derby County's Henrik Meister of Derby County was carried from the pitch on a stretcher (Image: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock)

Derby County's Championship clash with Birmingham City was brought to a halt after Henrik Meister went down with no players around him. Medical staff were rushed onto the pitch to attend to the Rams' forward.

‌



They took their time to ensure the Danish striker's neck was stable before moving him onto a stretcher. The 22-year-old, who is on loan with the Championship club from Serie B side Pisa, was applauded by all four corners of the ground as he made his way off the pitch.

‌



Play was halted for around seven minutes while Meister received treatment, going down in the 47th minute just after the half-time interval.

‌



Michail Antonio returns to English football nearly two years after brutal car crash READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

He was replaced by Oscar Fraulo in the 54th minute, with play resuming and Meister was taken straight down the tunnel.

Derby have now provided a positive update on the striker. They wrote on X: "A positive update on Henrik.

‌



The forward was checked over by the club’s medics after being carried off on a stretcher early in the second half. Thankfully, he walked out of the stadium unaided following the final whistle.

"He will now follow the concussion protocols."

Manager John Eustace added: "He's going through the protocols for concussion, so we'll wait and see. It was a disappointing time to lose him. It killed our momentum a bit, which was a shame."

‌



Derby County had taken the lead just before half-time when Bobby Clark found the bottom corner from a tight angle after being set up by Sammie Smodics.

However, their lead would last just two minutes with Birmingham equalising through Carlos Vincente after a Liam Millar cross.

The Blues would take the lead not long after the restart following Meister's medical incident. Substitute Seung-Ho Paik converted another Millar cross from close range to easy any immediate pressure on Chris Davies.

‌



Birmingham found themselves in 15th place before the visit to Derby, having played heffield United, Bristol City, Wrexham, Southampton, Wolves and Norwich, who all hopeful of winning promotion this season.

View 2 Images Birmingham City boss Chris Davies. (Image: (Photo by Nigel French/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images))

"I don't think anyone in the Championship had a harder start than us in terms of opposition," Davies told BBC Radio WM. "It's not an excuse it's a fact.

Article continues below

"We've got some decent results in this period - we've got to keep that same competitiveness and come out of it with a few more results and then we can really push on.

"I want us to be right up there. We've been competitive in every game, had some decent performances and results. We've acquitted ourselves well during that period but of course we want more points.

"We've been more consistent in our performance level this year than last year when we finished 10th. We've got to stick together and I'm sure we can have a better season than we did last season, from what I have seen so far."

Sports.title: Unai Emery confirms Alejandro Garnacho transfer stance after slow start at Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Unai Emery confirms Alejandro Garnacho transfer stance after slow start at Aston Villa

Alejandro Garnacho has struggled badly in recent seasons and life at Aston Villa has not got off to a great start either as Unai Emery offers his thoughts on the winger

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho has made a slow start to life at Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has confirmed the club signed Alejandro Garnacho for the long term amid his early struggles. Former Manchester United forward Garnacho joined Emery's side on loan this summer from Chelsea.

‌



The season-long deal to bring him to Villa Park includes a conditional obligation to buy. It follows several poor campaigns for the Argentine.

‌



Garnacho fell out with former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim during his final season at Old Trafford and was dropped for the Europa League final defeat to Tottenham Hotspur, which sealed his fate. It was then hoped that he could enjoy a new lease of life at Stamford Bridge after completing a £40million move last summer.

‌



But the winger failed to make a significant impact in west London as Chelsea endured a poor campaign, finishing 10th in the Premier League and missing out on European football. Garnacho was then shipped off to Villa in July, where he has made a slow start.

The United academy graduate has been restricted to substitute appearances so far - failing to score or provide an assist in three appearances. Now, Emery has had his say on Villa's plans for the attacker before Saturday's visit of Nottingham Forest.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said: "We want him at the same level he was for Chelsea in the first part of last season and in Manchester two years ago.

"He is a player we have signed for a long time, and we will help him to feel comfortable and confident to get his quality."

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho is now onto his third club in as many seasons (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Garnacho was an unused substitute during Tuesday's 3-2 Champions League win at Club Brugge - dealing a further blow to the player's confidence. But Emery expects the forward to make an impact at B6 and has praised his attitude in a bid to earn more minutes under the former Arsenal head coach.

He added: "First is positive - his attitude. His attitude is very important, he is getting the commitment we need to achieve it.

"Now he needs time. Time, hard work every day, and he is showing it with his attitude. Then, everything he is progressing.

Article continues below

"Every training session we are doing, he is showing he can play matches. He played a few minutes, but it was not enough, firstly due to the minutes he played and the things he showed.

"Progressively, I am seeing him better. The most important thing is being consistent and demanding through the attitude he has. Then, I believe and I trust that he will achieve his best performance."

Sports.title: Man Utd in astonishment over JJ Gabriel after Michael Carrick makes feelings clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd in astonishment over JJ Gabriel after Michael Carrick makes feelings clear

JJ Gabriel has been making waves at Manchester United, with the teenage prodigy scoring a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel continues to impress at Manchester United and is on the fringes of the first team (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United are reportedly 'in total shock' at JJ Gabriel's quality the youngster continues his extraordinary rise towards Michael Carrick's first-team squad. The 15-year-old, who frequently trains alongside United's senior players, was handed a chance to showcase his abilities during pre-season.

‌



While the intention is to manage his progression carefully, the club recognise they possess a genuine talent. United are conscious they have 'a real gem on their hands.'

‌



In the build-up to United's Champions League victory over Sabah FK, their Under-19s were competing at the Leigh Training Centre for the UEFA Youth League encounter.

‌



Gabriel maintained his outstanding start to the campaign, netting a hat-trick as the young Red Devils cruised to a 5-0 triumph, and became the youngest United player in history to achieve the feat in the competition.

Bruno Fernandes disclosure about Man Utd training says it all about Marcus Rashford READ MORE :

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano said: "It's going to be important to see how Manchester United manage JJ in terms of involving him in the first team in official games.

"That's going to be an important topic because everyone at Manchester United, when they speak about JJ Gabriel, is in total shock at how good this boy is. So obviously, his pathway is going to be absolutely important in order to understand more about JJ."

‌



United have already made the call to elevate Gabriel to the U21s setup this season, and he remains on the periphery of the first-team squad. United supporters are keenly anticipating their first look at the youngster in a competitive fixture for the senior side.

Carrick has been a regular presence at United's youth matches, closely monitoring Gabriel's progression. Speaking last month after observing Gabriel, the Red Devils head coach said: "I really enjoyed the game. You could see the quality.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is already making a name for himself aged just 15 (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"JJ is one of the boys. He's obviously got a really big talent. He's trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time. He's physically adapting to each step that he makes, and we're just continuing his development."

The United boss wasn't the only one singing the youngster's praises — U21s manager Adam Lawrence was full of admiration for Gabriel following the UEFA Youth League victory. He told the Manchester Evening News: "Well, I think the first thing in my job is not to ruin him.

"So when you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads of course, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. And I think essentially what you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments.

‌



"Of course, it can't always be free and off the cuff in terms of some of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and some of the pressing things that he's thinking about.

"But again, in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other teammates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space. If you look at that game today, I think he's playing properly.

Article continues below

"I think he's trying to do the right things. It's enjoyable working with him and challenging as a coach because the best players challenge you. When you work with talented players you have to find a way to help them and allow them to flourish and keep improving. Of course, there are things that you can keep working on but he is of course in a real good place."

Sports.title: 'I could barely afford food on £300-a-week at Celtic and was miserable – but I became club icon'
Sports.content:
Stiliyan Petrov says he struggled to afford his weekly shop on a measly £300-a-week wage at Celtic despite signing for £2.8million. The Bulgarian midfielder joined for a hefty fee but struggled during his first few months in Scotland before Martin O'Neill helped him turn a corner.

Petrov joined the Hoops from CSKA Sofia in 1999, agreeing a deal for just under £3m – which was an enormous fee at the time. However, the ex-Aston Villa star admitted his initial time at Celtic was full of financial issues that weren't fixed until O'Neill arrived one year later.

During an appearance on the All Out Football podcast with Laura Kirk-Francis and Gabby Agbonlahor, the 47-year-old revealed his struggles after joining the Scottish giants. When questioned on his wages compared to his signing fee, Petrov said: "Listen, at that time the money wasn't important for me. I was naive to move. It wasn't about the money for me. It was never about the money.

You can listen to brand new episodes of In The Mixer on Spotify and Apple Podcasts!

‌



Celtic and Rangers hit with stadium bans after ugly scenes in Old Firm clash READ MORE :

BBC football pundit breached editorial standards as he apologises after investigation launches READ MORE :

"Listen I could have left Celtic, I could have left Villa for a lot more money in different destinations. It was never about the money. It was about what you want to leave behind you. I've played for two great clubs. I've played with some incredible players and I won't change it."

Petrov's luck changed when O'Neill arrived, as he also struggled with fitting in as part of the team. When asked when his pay changed, he explained: "Six months after, Martin O'Neill took over. Obviously, I was celebrating John Barnes being sacked because I wasn't playing.

"I had a really difficult time. John never really put in any effort to help. I had a really difficult time for the first six months. Forget about bill issues, financial issues, forget about that. But the language barrier was a big problem for me because the dressing room was pushing me away. I wasn't talking to anyone. I wasn't communicating.

‌



"Go to training, get changed, train back home. That was me for six months. I was trying, I was thinking how can I fit in? But you know when you're not in a conversation, when you don't know the people's problem, and I could see they were pushing me away.

"But then the change happened. John Barnes got sacked and Martin took over. He gave me six weeks to get fit and show him that I can play on that team. I had a really good pre-season and had to lose 10 kilos as well. That was a lot in the pre-season. All that not eating and training twice a day."

Highlighting the Celtic manager's handling of his "dodgy agent," Petrov added: "When he [O'Neill] was happy with the pre-season, with everything I've done, he called me and he went, 'I've looked at your contract. I'm giving you more money.'

"So I try to explain about the agent. He said, 'Forget about the agent. Forget about the agent. This I will offer you, are you happy [with it]?' So I went from £300-a-week to £2,500-a-week."

‌



View 2 Images Petrov eventually found his footing at Celtic (Image: Stu Forster/ALLSPORT)

Petrov also recounted a time when his family visited from Bulgaria, and he had to wait for a game bonus to arrive in order to restock his fridge. Explaining how his family weren't aware of his situation, the ex-midfielder added: "The day [his family visited] I was expecting a bonus, a game bonus. So the day they landed in Scotland, I had about £65.

"I couldn't even do the shopping. I just couldn't face them. They never knew my issues, my problems. I wasn't ready to share that."

Petrov's luck eventually changed and he became a prolific figure in the early 2000s for Celtic. He won 10 trophies in Scotland, including four league titles and also reached the UEFA Cup final - now known as the Europa League - in the 2002/03 season.

‌



After spending seven seasons at Villa, Petrov retired in 2013 following an acute leukaemia diagnosis the year prior. The ex-midfielder did return to training in 2016 after recovering from the illness but never returned to the professional game.

Sports.title: Shelton relishing challenge of first Grand Slam final against Zverev at US Open
Sports.content:
Ben Shelton finds himself in unfamiliar territory after reaching his first Grand ‌Slam final at the US Open, with the American now ready to "do it for the USA" when he takes on top seed Alexander Zverev in Sunday's showdown.

Shelton is the first black American man to reach the US Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972, and is aiming to become the first home male player to win the title since Andy Roddick in 2003.

He will have a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd behind him when he takes on German top seed and title favourite Zverev.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Shelton thought he hit a 158mph serve at the US Open semi-finals, but in fact it was an impressive 144mph according to Hawk-Eye

The Spaniard's words of wisdom helped his son reset after his sensational five-set win over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-final.

"I think you learn from your experiences," said 60-year-old former ATP pro Shelton. "He won Montreal, he went to Cincinnati and we said: 'this is going to be the toughest day you're going to have', playing in the first round in Cincinnati after winning a title.

"Very few people come from that and have another good tournament the next week, and he didn't, you know? He lost first round.

"I remember talking to Rafa a couple of days after that match. Rafa was, like, 'you know, you got to be able to get through that first one and have the day off and then be able to get your best tennis again the next week'.

"So it was a lesson for Ben that you've got to be able to bounce back when good things happen, just as you have to bounce back when adversity happens or tough things go on.

"So we talked about him beating Carlos and how important it's really going to be for him to understand that this one is going to be even tougher, you know, to bounce back after that, because a lot of people want to rest after they've had something good and want to celebrate it.

"What we say is don't celebrate until you separate. So you've got to win the next match. You've got to consolidate it. Then somewhere, hopefully next week, we can celebrate a little bit."

Sports.title: West Ham secure first WSL win of season against London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
West Ham claimed their first Women's Super League win of the season with a 2-1 home victory over London City Lionesses.

Kelly Gago put the Hammers ahead after 21 minutes, racing onto Seraina Piubel's pass from near halfway before rounding City goalkeeper Elene Lete.

Viviane Asseyi scored a similar goal three minutes after the break after being released by Riko Ueki, running clear from 40 yards out before firing home.

Image: West Ham's Viviane Asseyi celebrates after scoring to make it 2-0

London City set up a frantic finish after Danielle van de Donk's clever back heel crept in at the near post 14 minutes from time.

But the Lionesses struggled to reproduce the fluency that had seen them overcome Manchester United on the opening weekend.

Guarino: We must show same spirit in every game

West Ham head coach Rita Guarino

"I'm very happy.

"I'm happy with the result, it's three important points at home in front of our supporters, but also for the performance in the way the team played today, and the way the team trained in the week.

"I'm very happy with the result and performance.

"I saw the spirit that I want to see every time, it's part of our identity. We can't forget that we have this kind of value and we need to show it in every single game.
