Sports.title: Iraola bemoans Liverpool's lack of cutting edge and explains Barcola plan
Sports.content:
Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola bemoaned lack of creativity and cutting edge after his side were held to a 0-0 draw by Fulham at Anfield.

The result leaves Iraola unbeaten so far this term, but Liverpool have yet to win at home in the Premier League this season.

Liverpool struggled to create opportunities against a Fulham team that had lost their opening three games, with Iraola insisting afterwards that his side's shortcomings were evident.

"I think what was lacking, I think it was quite clear," Iraola said.

"I think it's the first game since I'm here, I think we've had problems to create chances, to score goals, to make the difference offensively.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Liverpool’s match against Fulham in the Premier League

"That's the main reason. We couldn't create as many chances as we wanted and we haven't scored a goal. And that's why we go just with one point."

Iraola: Players lacked freshness

Image: Fulham's Gonzalo Garcia and Liverpool's Ronald Araujo battle for the ball

The Reds lacked the energy they showed in their midweek Champions League win over Atletico Madrid, but Iraola refused to use fatigue as an excuse for his side's failure to pick up all three points.

"Our players were tired," he said.

"I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it.

"I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60-something hours between the games, after a very big game (against Atletico Madrid) the other day.

Image: Oscar Bobb is challenged by Milos Kerkez

"But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe. But sometimes it's going to happen the same way during the season. We have to adapt to these circumstances.

"It's this kind of game that you need to win, sometimes with a set play, sometimes with a shot from the edge, sometimes from a moment of brilliance from the offensive players and we haven't had that today.

"We've been clearly not as good offensively as we've been in other days."

Barcola makes full PL debut from left

Bradley Barcloa made his full Premier League debut in the game and was deployed from the left in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Victor Munoz starting the game on the right.

Explaining his thinking, Iraola said: "I think I said it a lot of times. I think we have four wingers. Probably, before the season, everyone will say there are more left wingers than right wingers, because they play more there.

"I think all the wingers will play on the right and will play on the left. Depending on the match-up, depending on where we think they are going to be more dangerous, depending on the defensive demand, depending on what we feel, what we analyse, we position them in the right or in the left.

"But I think Bradley, I think everyone. The four of them already have played both sides and it's going to be a whole season like this because of the wingers, with a lot of times the same preferences."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thierry Henry explained why Liverpool supporters should be excited by new signing Bradley Barcola after the France forward completed his move from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth up to £123m

Iraola added: "I think with Bradley now we are building also his physical condition, because he hasn't had any in pre-season and I think there is a good part where today he played, I think, a little bit more than three days ago against Atletico Madrid.

"He had a good chance in the second half, they blocked the shot but he arrived well.

"Probably, we know he has more, but now it's about giving him the minutes, keep building his confidence also and he's a player that is worthy of our support."

Sports.title: Winless Spurs remain goalless after another bore draw against Everton
Sports.content:
Tottenham’s winless and goalless start to the Premier League season continued with a 0-0 draw at home to unbeaten Everton.

It is the first time Spurs have failed to score in any of their first four league games of a season, while it is now over 400 minutes since their last Premier League goal.

Following last weekend's goalless draw at Nottingham Forest, it was another toothless display from Roberto De Zerbi's new-look, expensively assembled side, who were booed off at the full-time whistle.

Image: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi shows his frustration after another goalless display

A disgruntled home crowd watched their side have just two shots on target - the first a weak second-half effort from Mateus Fernandes met with ironic cheers - create one big chance and register a paltry expected goals of 0.64.

Everton had the better moments to earn their first away league win since February, but ex-Spurs winger Brennan Johnson blazed a great second-half chance over, while earlier, Spurs goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky nearly gifted Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall an opener.

The Toffees weathered Spurs' early storm as the home side had four shots in the opening 10 minutes, with Jan Paul van Hecke missing a great close-range chance.

But the defender's fifth-minute effort proved to be Tottenham's best opportunity as De Zerbi's side became the first Spurs team to go on a four-game goalless run in 20 years.

It was also the first goalless draw at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in the Premier League (140th game), and the first time that Spurs have drawn 0-0 in a home game in the competition since September 2017.

Redknapp: Spurs' goalless run 'absolutely diabolical'

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp:

"After spending £300m, I didn't think there would be a problem scoring goals. But to not score in six hours of football is absolutely diabolical.

"For the first 20 minutes, I thought that this is what I want to see. There was a moment when Fernandes had a shot and the whole crowd celebrated. It's not great.

"The connection with the fans and the players is not there. I don't know when they are going to get their first win. It might go on for longer, but I do still see some positives.

"It cannot stay this way with what is at their disposal. There are things that I don't like. Robertson was your left-back and your wide left player because Marmoush wanted to come inside. That balance didn't really work, so you are lopsided with what you're trying to do.

"Trying to get the best squad is what De Zerbi has to solve. The midfield balance also isn't right. You've got to find a way of getting a Kudus into the ten, or Maddison if he gets fit. I'm not sure how Kulusevski's going to be but when he's fit you've got to get him in.

"Even I'm looking and thinking 'how would I change it?' There are more questions than answers. He tried everything today. He couldn't find it. The quality wasn't there, but they have got quality players."

De Zerbi explains Tel exchange

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roberto De Zerbi appears to have a tense exchange with Mathys Tel at full-time after Tottenham Hotspur's 0-0 draw with Everton

De Zerbi was involved in an exchange at full-time on the pitch with Mathys Tel, who was brought on as a second-half substitute.

The Italian explained at his post-match press conference: "I coached him on the pitch. The body shape: he's a striker; the striker can't play with the shoulder on the goal.

"If we are playing with (James) Maddison, (Mohammed) Kudus and Savio, he has to play as a striker, and the striker has to look at the goal, or for the cross of (Andy) Robertson. He has to stay inside.

"He started as a striker; now he's playing as a winger, but he started his career as a striker.

"But I love Mathys as a player, as a guy; that is not a problem."

Moyes pleased with Toffees' resilience but wanted more

Everton boss David Moyes:

"I wanted much more from the team, but I told them about coming here.

"We've not had a great record here. Only a couple months ago we missed out on Europe here. I generally felt that we had to come here and show a bit more.

"Tottenham were so good for 20 minutes. They put us under so much pressure. We found it difficult to escape from it. We created a couple chances ourselves, but we didn't play well enough today when we had the ball.

"We know exactly where we're short and what we could do better at and what we'd like to do better. But there'll be some games where we might have to play that way just to get ourselves through. It wasn't the plan, we were forced into it by Tottenham. I thought we did a really good job of being resilient."

The key moments from north London...

5: SPURS GO CLOSE! Jan Paul van Hecke puts over Andy Robertson's free-kick from close range.

45+1: KINSKY SAVES! The first shot on target of the game is produced by Everton's James Garner from a long-range free-kick, which is palmed away by Antonin Kinsky.

HALF TIME: No shot on target for Tottenham, who fail to score in the first half for a 26th Premier League game since the start of last season.

47: FIRST SPURS SHOT ON TARGET! Mateus Fernandes' weak low shot is straight at Jordan Pickford, but it brings ironic cheers from the Spurs fans.

50: KINSKY SAVES! Thierno Barry's back-post header is saved by Kinsky, who didn't know much about it.

66: KINSKY GETS LUCKY! The Spurs goalkeeper passes it straight to Dewsbury-Hall but he hits his shot straight at Kinsky.

89: FROM ZERO TO HERO FOR PICKFORD! The Everton goalkeeper gives the ball away to allow Lucas Bergvall a shot, which he superbly saves.

Millions spent, but where is the goalscorer?

Image: De Zerbi is yet to celebrate a Premier League goal this season

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

"It doesn't take a genius to figure out where Tottenham's biggest concern lies right now. You can't win games if you don't score goals. That's why Spurs haven't won a league game this season, after going 400 minutes without finding the net.

"They have so many creative players, all of whom were on the pitch against the Toffees. Yet the man who they need to score the bulk of their goals was anonymous. Or at the very least, wasn't found.

"Dominic Solanke's fitness for Tottenham feels imperative. As the only out and out number nine available to De Zerbi, the Englishman has to be picked when fit. Purely because it seems Spurs don't have a choice.

"However, whether it be rustiness following his latest setbacks or another reason, Solanke didn't offer anywhere near enough as the number nine. He managed just 19 touches. That's less than Kinsky in goal.

Sports.title: Brits Skupski, Hewett clinch respective US Open doubles, wheelchair titles
Sports.content:
There was double success for Britain at the US Open on Saturday, with Alfie Hewett regaining his wheelchair singles title and Neal Skupski finally claiming the men’s doubles crown.

Emotional Hewett burst into tears after beating Tokito Oda 6-0 7-6 (7-5) to deny the 20-year-old Japanese star a calendar Grand Slam.

The 28-year-old, who was beaten by Oda in the finals of the French Open and Wimbledon this year, said: "It's taken lot of hard work, a lot of soul-searching at times, a lot of reflecting.

"The Wimbledon pumping was a tough one to swallow. I definitely came away from that one with a lot of regret, took some time off and had a hard, long look in the mirror about who I wanted to be on the tennis court and how I wanted to show up.

Sports.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Big fan of Forty Years On in Sceptre Stakes
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle previews the final day of the St Leger Festival at Doncaster - live on Sky Sports Racing – alongside top-quality action on Champions’ Weekend at The Curragh.

Scott filly can make winning Stakes debut

I've made no secret of my admiration for FORTY YEARS ON who can make an instant impact in Pattern company when she contests the feature race at Doncaster on Sunday, the Japan Racing Association Sceptre Fillies Stakes (3.05).

George Scott, who won Friday's Doncaster Cup with Caballo De Mar, has found a great opportunity for this most progressive daughter of Mayson who was much too good for her rivals in a valuable handicap at Goodwood last month.

She enjoys ease underfoot and can win for the sixth time in eight starts at the possible expense of Shadwell's Touleen, who brings solid Group One form to the race after her luckless run in the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot.

She did look a bit awkward in the Valiant Stakes last time so the cheekpieces may just sharpen her focus, while Planet Seeker looks over-priced on the strength of her York form and her creditable fourth in the Group 3 Oak Tree Stakes at The Goodwood Festival.

Longer trip ideal for Bailey gelding in Mallard

It's hard to fault SAY WHAT YOU SEE in the Betfred Mallard Handicap (3.40) on Sunday following a string of rock-solid races for his trainer Liam Bailey this year.

He built on a near miss at Southwell with an eye-catching run at York's Ebor Festival, staying on from a long way back to finish a closing third over 12 furlongs and should appreciate this longer trip.

There's probably a nice race in Godolphin's Valedictory who was a little one-paced over two miles at York last time, having looked the real deal earlier in the season with back-to-back wins at Goodwood and Newmarket. He has something to prove off his current mark, however.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Doyle bit back at Sky Sports Racing's Seb Sanders after criticism of his winning ride in the Flying Childers at Doncaster, which saw Final Objective veer across the track and cause a rival to stumble badly

Boughey has strong hand in sprint

I like George Boughey's lightly raced ASUKA in the Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (1.55) on Sunday's Doncaster card.

Dropping back to six furlongs on such a big galloping track shouldn't be an issue for the Night Of Thunder gelding who confirmed himself in top form over further at Chester last time when a poor draw and an interrupted run put paid to his chances.

George has a strong hand in the race with stable mate Oliver Show also bringing some strong form to the table. His run behind subsequent winner Inspired at Goodwood last time reads well and the first-time visor is an interesting angle.

Easier surface a positive for course winner

I'm looking forward to seeing LANGSTONE back on an easier surface in the Betfred City Of Doncaster Handicap (2.30) on Sunday.

Clive Cox's three-year-old broke his maiden over course and distance in the spring before following up on the All-Weather but didn't enjoy the fast ground in the Britannia at Royal Ascot. He hasn't been seen in public since so he arrives on Town Moor much fresher than his rivals and remains well treated off a slightly reduced mark of 92.

Zooming should also appreciate a more sympathetic surface for the first time since winning her maiden at Newmarket last autumn. She has been highly tried this year and drops into handicap company for the first time off what looks a workable mark of 94.

Image: The Sceptre Stakes headlines the final day at Doncaster as the fabulous four-day festival draws to a close

Goddess can have her day in the sun

I can't wait to see how SUN GODDESS performs back at Group One level in the Moyglare Stud Stakes (2.50) at The Curragh on Sunday following her demolition job in a valuable sales race at York last month.

Aidan O'Brien's filly had it all to do after running into trouble on The Knavesmire, but her class prevailed in the end as she ran out a most impressive six-length winner. This is much tougher, of course, as she tackles seven furlongs for the first time on a stiffer track, but I'm confident the Phoenix Stakes winner is up to the task.

Green Empress travelled well when getting off the mark in the Group Two Debutante Stakes over course and distance last month, beating the re-opposing Alpha, Ibelieveicanfly and Dancing Destiny and looks the main danger.

Sandals ready to take a big step forward

The way Starlust hit the line behind US raider Bacio in the Nunthorpe Stakes at York tells me he can run another massive race in the BAR 1 Betting Flying Five Stakes (3.25) at The Curragh.

Ralph Beckett's five-year-old came out of retirement following a fruitless spell at stud and looks to have found the form that won him the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint two years ago.

TIME FOR SANDALS' last two runs have been solid, and I like the way she flashed home in the Nunthorpe after repeatedly finding trouble mid-race. If things fall her way, she could be the one they all have to beat with Kieran Shoemark in the saddle.

Image: Time For Sandals (centre) is Hollie Doyle's pick in the Flying Five

Sequoia can post a giant run in National

Juddmonte colt Monogram looked a class act when scoring over course and distance for Joseph O'Brien and can take the step up to Group One company in his stride in the Goffs Vincent O'Brien National Stakes (4.00).

One thing he does lack, however, is experience which could give GIANT SEQUOIA the advantage. Aidan O'Brien's first string won the Group Two Futurity Stakes here last time and is clearly a colt of huge potential.

On the evidence of that run, the son of the great Frankel is still open to enough improvement to make his presence felt at the very highest level so gets my vote in a mouthwatering renewal.

Brilliant Scandinavia set for fifth Group One

With a seven-race unbeaten streak to his name, I can't wait to see the brilliant SCANDINAVIA enhance his reputation in the Comer Group International Irish St Leger (4.35) on Sunday.

Aidan O'Brien's Gold Cup winner steps back to one mile and six furlongs which shouldn't be a problem on such a stiff track, and he can justify short odds in his quest for a fifth victory at the highest level.

Stable companion Jan Brueghel, who, like Scandinavia is a Doncaster St Leger winner, is the obvious danger. He looked as good as ever when winning this season's Coronation Cup and won't mind this greater test of stamina.

Sports.title: Tottenham waiting for first league goal of season after draw against Everton
Sports.content:
Is it too early for a Tottenham crisis? To which the answer is surely that it is never too early for a Tottenham crisis. After four Premier League games, they have yet to score. This kind of run has never happened in their history at the beginning of a league season.

At least they mustered a couple of shots on target this time, having failed to do so last weekend in the 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest. The first – from Mateus Fernandes – at the start of the second half was greeted by ironic cheers from the South Stand. It has certainly not been what the club expected when they spent £300m on overhauling the squad in the summer.

Spurs were anxious, they lacked certainties – apart from the one about how they were never going to score. They were fortunate that Everton, who remain defiantly unbeaten, did not do so at the other end. David Moyes’s team had big chances in the second half through Thierno Barry, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs winger, Brennan Johnson. Everton defended superbly, albeit they were helped by Tottenham’s bluntness, and were full value for the draw. They probably deserved to win.

Spurs have won only one league game at home this year – in do-or-die circumstances against Everton on the final day of last season. Going back to November 2024, their record in the competition here reads: P35 W5 D10 L20. As Everton savoured the result with their fans at full time, the Spurs crowd turned to a familiar soundtrack: a burst of booing.

It was difficult not to remember the game here last season when Spurs won 1-0 to stay up. Defeat and they would have been relegated. It was an extraordinarily nervy occasion for them, all the way to the last knockings of stoppage time. The pessimistic edge about the home support has not gone away. Far from it. You could hear it before kick-off. ‘Good luck? Yeah, we’ll need it.’ That sort of thing. A major part of the mission was to try to tear down the psychological barriers. They failed.

There was hope, too. It always bubbles somewhere in the background. And Spurs did start well, pressing on to the front foot, moving the ball quickly. Rodrigo Bentancur imposed himself. Savio was a ball of pace and tricks. There was a statistic beforehand that rated Tottenham as the worst team in the league for the quality of chances created. What could they do with their possession against an Everton defence that knows how to stifle? It was the question that pounded.

Everton travelled with confidence after good results in their opening fixtures. Their squad is alarmingly thin. But they have enough at this point of the season and the fallout from that disastrous transfer deadline day appears to have bonded the squad. Everton were the second worst team on the chance quality index but they were always likely to be measured by how well they defended.

View image in fullscreen Jordan Pickford makes a save from Lucas Bergvall. Photograph: David Cliff/EPA

Spurs pushed for the first half of the first period, albeit the pickings in front of goal were slim. Jan Paul van Hecke banged a half volley high from a tight angle at the far post after an Andy Robertson free-kick and that would go down as their only chance of the opening 45 minutes. There was a stumble from Fernandes inside the area after a nice ball up through the lines from Van Hecke which summed things up for them. The anxiety transmitted itself to the crowd and bounced back.

James Garner worked Antonin Kinsky with a free-kick at the end of the first half, which went down as the first shot on target. When Fernandes mustered his from distance in the 47th minute, it was met with that sarcasm.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Everton were more proactive after the restart. They fed off the Spurs nerves. They threatened to get in behind. Tyrique George did beat Archie Gray, who stood in for the injured Pedro Porro at right-back; Roberto De Zerbi was also without Destiny Udogie through injury at left-back. George’s cross picked out Barry at the far post and his header hit Kinsky before flying off target. The goalkeeper knew little about it. George also had a blast that hit Bentancur.

Tottenham came to be undermined by terrible errors on the ball. There were so many passes that were woefully off target, including one from Kinsky that he sent straight to Dewsbury-Hall on the edge of his area. Kinsky made amends with a smart block. Dewsbury-Hall cursed the passing up of a golden opportunity.

Everton were the likelier team to score. Spurs battled the internal demons. There were cross words between some of their players, Omar Marmoush overtaken by frustration at one point. Johnson blew his chance on 75 minutes, lifting high after a Dewsbury-Hall tee-up.

Spurs had one flicker at the very end after Jordan Pickford sent a poor clearance straight to James Maddison, who had come on as a substitute. Spurs moved it to another replacement, Lucas Bergvall, and his low drive worked Pickford. It was a comfortable save. Everton were exactly that.

Sports.title: Hull stun Chelsea with Mohamed Belloumi double before João Pedro rescues a point
Sports.content:
The chants from the away end about winning the league were sung in jest, but Hull continue to show they are here to stay. Sergej Jakirovic’s dogged, intelligent side are third in the Premier League after extending their unbeaten start to four games and can even count themselves unfortunate not to have beaten another of the Big Six after pushing Chelsea to the limit in an absorbing battle at a frustrated Stamford Bridge.

Hull were 2-1 up at half-time and they had the chances to snatch the points during the second half. It took two big saves from Emiliano Martínez to prevent an upset, but this was not a good day for the Chelsea goalkeeper or his new teammates. He was one of several at fault when Hull, having dusted themselves down after conceding from Morgan Rogers early on, went ahead through Mohamed Belloumi’s quickfire double. The ease with which Chelsea’s advantage was handed over left the normally calm and considered Xabi Alonso accusing his side of being “soft” without the ball.

Alonso craves the comfort of a forgettable win. Chelsea have been exhilarating in attack, but they cannot defend. They are conceding two goals per game and the basketball nature of Alonso’s approach has created chaos rather than control. “It’s all entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win,” he said. “It will take time. When we get the lead you still need to be competing and not to give the chance so easily for them to come back.

“Especially in the first goal, we can do much better. It was too soft to give them hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances, but that changed the mood. We will get better, but it’s having an impact on our performances.”

It is ridiculous that Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro are having to do so much in attack. Chelsea led after seven minutes, surging forward when they left four players forward at a Hull corner. João Pedro’s pass reached Rogers and the £117m signing from Aston Villa drove past Regan Slater before beating Konstantinos Tzolaki at his near post with a low, hard and early shot from the left.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro fires home Chelsea’s equaliser in the second half. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA

Chelsea should have pushed on after becoming the first side to breach Hull since their promotion. Pedro Neto tested Tzolakis from the right, but the hosts became vague and complacent. This was the first time they have dominated possession in a league game this season and the result was not convincing. Hull limited them to an xG of 0.89, highlighting Chelsea’s issues against low blocks, and were clinical when they attacked.

The soft defending Alonso referenced for the equaliser started with Malo Gusto failing to deal with a long punt from Tzolakis in the 28th minute. Ryan Giles outmuscled the right-back and hooked a cross to the far post. Jorrel Hato misread the Hull left-back’s delivery, leaving Belloumi to rap a shot past Martínez.

Chelsea are without a win against promoted sides in five home games. They do not smell danger, while Alonso’s decision to leave Maxence Lacroix out at centre-back and shift from a back three to a 4-2-3-1 system backfired. Hull had so much space on the flanks. They pushed again and Belloumi’s flick found Lewie Coyle, who ran off Rogers but saw his shot cleared off the line by Levi Colwill.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it,” Alonso said. “Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

There was no response from Chelsea after Colwill turned Coyle’s shot wide. A corner came in from the left, Martínez flapped and Semi Ajayi’s header hit the bar. The ball came to Belloumi, whose shot flew in thanks to a deflection.

Alonso reacted at half-time, Hato making way for Pep Chavarría at left-back. Reece James drew a save from Tzolakis with a free-kick but Hull carried a threat on the break. They almost extended their lead when Martínez spilled a shot from Slater.

Martínez redeemed himself, blocking the rebound from McBurnie, and Chelsea soon levelled. Palmer, otherwise quiet, surprised Hull with a direct run. The No 10 drove down the left and picked out João Pedro, who lashed a shot into the roof of the net.

Hull refused to lie down. Ajayi, Giles and John Egan were outstanding at the back and the visitors maintained their shape when losing Nobel Mendy after a nasty collision with João Pedro.

Jakirovic made bold substitutions. Alonso threw Danny Welbeck on. Palmer scooped over from 20 yards and Tzolakis thwarted Rogers, but Hull had the best chance. Giles crossed again and Mohamed-Ali Cho shot straight at Martínez from close range.

Hull settled for a point. Jakirovic quashed talk of qualifying for Europe, insisting that survival remains the aim. The Bosnian has everyone pulling in the same direction. Before the start of the season he told his staff he would give them seven days off if Hull took eight points from their first five games. Mission completed with a game to spare.

Sports.title: Frustrated Liverpool lack any spark as Fulham claim deserved first point
Sports.content:
Álvaro Arbeloa was often the obstacle to Andoni Iraola’s international ambitions back in the days when both were vying for a right-back role with Spain. On his return to Anfield, and under the watchful eye of former manager Rafael Benítez, Arbeloa thwarted Iraola once again to claim his first Premier League point as Fulham head coach against an ineffective Liverpool.

Fulham belied their lowly position and run of three league defeats to take a merited point from a Liverpool team that was a pale imitation of the one that beat Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday. Iraola fielded a front four that cost almost £400m but the most impressive forward on display was the Fulham academy graduate Josh King. The draw was Liverpool’s third in four league games under their new head coach and the seventh in 12 Premier League matches at Anfield in 2026. Progress can be painfully slow at times.

“It is the first game we’ve had problems creating chances and making the difference offensively,” Iraola said. “It is easy for me to say the players were tired (after Atlético). There was a lack of freshness and, we cannot hide it, it was the worst turnaround in terms of 60-70 hours. But this is going to happen in the season and we have to adapt. Sometimes you need a set play or a moment of brilliance to win these kind of games but we were not as good offensively as other games.”

Liverpool were sluggish and sloppy – Florian Wirtz and Kostas Tsimikas put simple passes straight out of play in the first half, setting the tone for a disjointed performance – while Fulham bypassed the central midfield pairing of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch repeatedly. The visitors’ confidence and composure on the ball, along with their defensive organisation, was hugely impressive considering the start to the season under the former Real Madrid interim coach and Liverpool defender. With more conviction in front of goal, Arbeloa’s side could have capitalised on Liverpool’s malaise.

Bradley Barcola created an early, difficult chance for Alexander Isak that the striker swept wide of the far post. Victor Muñoz went closer still with a glancing header from a Szoboszlai corner. Bernd Leno, the Fulham goalkeeper, reacted superbly to claw the ball away. But that was the sum total of Liverpool’s first-half enterprise.

Fulham were gifted a glorious opportunity when Alisson played a ridiculous pass to Gravenberch, who was under pressure from Sander Berge. Berge’s challenge fell to King, who was sent flying by the Liverpool goalkeeper but the referee, Thomas Bramall, played a good advantage as Gonzalo García received the loose ball. García had time to pick his spot but Jérémy Jacquet blocked his shot in front of the goalline.

View image in fullscreen Jérémy Jacquet clears the ball off the line to deny Fulham the lead. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

The visitors prospered down their left and Oscar Bobb missed another good opening when, unmarked and 18 yards out, he miscontrolled Alex Iwobi’s pinpoint delivery. Jacquet came to Liverpool’s rescue once again seconds later when preventing García breaking through with an excellent challenge.

Liverpool were deserving of a few home truths during the break – chiefly, you would have been lambasted for this last season under Arne Slot – and performed with more intensity in the second half. But not with any more threat. The introductions of Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and Milos Kerkez brought modest improvement but Fulham continued to contain the hosts comfortably. The new signing David Affengruber had a fine debut and Calvin Bassey was commanding against Isak.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors remained dangerous on the counterattack and Alisson pushed away a King effort that was heading for the top corner. King’s replacement, Rodrigo Muniz, let a decent chance run away from him inside the area and the substitute Kevin dragged a shot wide from 18 yards. Isak finally escaped Bassey’s attentions in stoppage time but his flicked header from a Szoboszlai corner sailed wide.

Arbeloa said: “When you are not winning games it’s not so easy for your players to believe in your ideas. But they believe in the way we have been working and I showed them the things that we were doing so well. We were more balanced and controlled the transitions well. I’m happy with the point but more with the performance of my players and the character, the personality and the ambition they showed in this stadium.”

Sports.title: London City’s superstars brought down to earth in WSL defeat at West Ham
Sports.content:
West Ham claimed their first Women’s Super League win of the season with a 2-1 home victory over London City Lionesses. Kelly Gago put the Hammers ahead after 21 minutes, racing between the centre-backs Mapi León and Isa Kardinaal to latch on to Seraina Piubel’s pass from nearly halfway and rounding Elene Lete in the London City goal.

Daniëlle van de Donk was denied an equaliser when Constance Picaud-Inconnu saved low, with Alexia Putellas, another of London City’s big-name summer signings, lifting the rebound over the bar under the challenge of Inès Belloumou.

View image in fullscreen Kelly Gago is congratulated after scoring the opener. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

Viviane Asseyi doubled West Ham’s lead three minutes after the break after being released by Riko Ueki, running the length of the London City half before firing home.

London City set up a frantic finish after Van de Donk’s clever backheel from Kadidiatou Diani’s low cross crept in at the near post 14 minutes from time.

View image in fullscreen Danielle van de Donk flicks home for the Lionesses. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

The veteran Netherlands forward had scored a similar goal with the winner against Manchester United on the opening weekend – this defeat at Chigwell Construction Stadium was a reality check for Maestre’s side as they seek to challenge the top teams in the WSL.

West Ham bounced back after their defeat to Tottenham. “I saw the spirit that I want to see every time, it’s part of our identity,” said their head coach, Rita Guarino. “We can’t forget that we have this kind of value and we need to show it in every single game.”

Sports.title: Farke’s blueprint for revitalised Leeds continues upward trajectory
Sports.content:
Eleven years have passed since Daniel Farke mounted a magnificent palomino horse and rode round the perimeter of the pitch at Lippstadt, waving farewell to a capacity crowd. It seemed a fun way for the lower-tier German club’s centre-forward turned manager and sporting director to say goodbye. Yet few in the stands knew Farke was scared of horses and hauled himself into the saddle only out of politeness towards his chair, who had arranged this special surprise.

“I couldn’t deny him,” he said. “But it cured my fear – it was enjoyable.”

These days the Leeds manager is demanding similar bravery, as well as instant adaptability, from his players. “We want to be hard to predict,” said Farke as he prepared to welcome his compatriot Matthias Jaissle’s rapid counterattacking Newcastle team to Elland Road on Monday night. “We have different approaches. For example, if a team has two very good centre-backs who dominate aerially it makes sense to build with more low passes.

“It’s always in our DNA that we want to be on the ball and, in the buildup, we always want to be brave. Also it’s possible to break the [opposition] pressing by playing good football out from the back.”

View image in fullscreen Daniel Farke says ‘anything is possible’ for Leeds this season ahead of match with Newcastle on Monday. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Not that Leeds are averse to taking the direct route. This season only Hull and Nottingham Forest have played a higher percentage of their passes long than a Leeds XI invariably spearheaded by the formidable Dominic Calvert-Lewin. As Farke says: “We very often have a physical target player up front that we can be a bit more direct into.”

If such tactical variety is designed to keep rivals guessing, a fusion of alternative styles also befits a coach who admires the contrasting approaches of his close friends Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp.

Adaptability almost certainly saved his job last season. From 4 October to 29 November Leeds played seven Premier League games, losing six. They have since completed 28 league fixtures, losing five, while reaching an FA Cup semi-final.

Farke is negotiating from a position of strength as he discusses extending a contract that has less than a year to run. “Daniel’s done great,” the Leeds managing director, Robbie Evans, said this week. “We want him to be here long term and we’re working on it.”

View image in fullscreen Daniel Farke’s half-time changes against Manchester City in November transformed Leeds’s fortunes. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

Everything changed on 29 November. Leeds lost 3-2 at Manchester City but Farke’s half-time switch to a back three, allied to Calvert-Lewin’s introduction, provided him with a timely lifeline. The changes enabled the visitors, trailing 2-0, to level in a transformative second-half performance spoiled only by Phil Foden’s stoppage-time winner.

It marked the start of an upward trajectory that has continued this season as Leeds, alternating between three and four at the back, have remained unbeaten, like Newcastle.

A watershed perhaps came when England’s James Trafford arrived this summer from City for £40m – a record fee for a British goalkeeper. Given Newcastle had tried to buy Trafford on three occasions his signing represents something of a coup for Leeds. Throw in the abundance of diggers, hard hats and hi-vis vests on view at Elland Road as the stadium is expanded from a capacity of just under 38,000 to 53,000 and the sense of a club on the up is almost palpable.

“Something’s going well here,” Trafford said after signing. “They [the owners, 49er Enterprises] want to take the club back to where it has been historically and I think everyone here believes that is going to happen.

“With the energy, physicality and quality in this team anything is possible this season. The spirit is incredible. It’s really, really good and that can take you a long way.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

If such harmony can be attributed to Farke’s “no dickheads” policy when it comes to potential signings and the midfielder Ethan Ampadu’s impressive embrace of the captaincy, astute recruitment is steadily raising the team’s calibre.

The Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-half Tarik Muharemovic is proving an outstanding defender and a fine distributor. The £34m buy from Sassuolo is emblematic of the amalgam of robust athleticism and technical ability that increasingly characterises a Leeds team further enhanced by Harry Wilson’s arrival from Fulham.

View image in fullscreen Tarik Muharemovic scored for Leeds against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and has already proved to be an astute summer signing. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Not that Farke is getting carried away. After seeing Trafford’s deputy, Michael Zetterer, overwhelmed as a rotated Leeds lost 6-3 at Chelsea in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday he was not in the mood for excuses.

“Let’s be honest, it was a nightmare debut,” Farke said on Thursday. “You feel a bit for him, but sometimes in life you have the worst possible start. He will have pressure next time, but he’s a good goalkeeper. They live a privileged life and he’s playing for a big club.”

On Monday, he will offer Jaissle a somewhat warmer greeting. They share a friendship with Klopp and Thomas Tuchel, but the Newcastle manager’s recent posting in Jeddah with Al-Ahli helped ensure that, until now, their paths have not crossed.

“He’s made a bright start,” Farke said. “Newcastle are very dangerous, especially counterattacking and it will be difficult. But we want to be on top of their challenge. We want as many points as possible.”

Sports.title: Emery takes responsibility as Forest strike late at winless Aston Villa
Sports.content:
This summer there were a couple of significant pieces of the puzzle for Oliver Glasner to put into place at Nottingham Forest. The first was a mobile striker to lead the line and the other was a right wing-back to fit his favoured 3-4-3 system. Enter Liam Delap and Daniel Muñoz, both of whom had a big say in Forest’s first win under Glasner, though the match-winner was one of the old brigade in Igor Jesus.

Delap registered his first Forest goal in style, a powerful shot from 25 yards and Muñoz was involved in the slick move that culminated in Igor Jesus reading Morgan Gibbs-White’s exquisite backheel to down Aston Villa, who remain winless in the Premier League.

That the winner came down Villa’s left made things even more painful from their perspective. For the final 12 minutes, including six in stoppage time, John McGinn was operating as an emergency left-back after Ian Maatsen’s injury reduced them to 10 men. By the 63rd minute, after sending on Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye for their Villa debuts, Unai Emery had used all five substitutions; Pau Torres was forced off with a hamstring problem midway through the first half that could sideline him for a month and Tammy Abraham and Alysson, who pulled Villa level, arrived at the interval. Abraham replaced Nicolas Jackson, who Emery felt was at risk of a second yellow card.

Those changes left Villa unable to replace Maatsen after the full-back was cynically fouled by James McAtee, whom Emery felt should have been sent off for the challenge. Emery said the video assistant referee, Timothy Wood, should have flagged the incident to the referee, Andy Madley. “It’s a clear tackle behind the player and, for me, it should be a red card,” he said. “But it’s not an excuse for how we played the second half. We played so poorly and this is my responsibility.”

View image in fullscreen Unai Emery, the Aston Villa head coach, is without a win in the Premier League this season. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

For the second successive season, Villa are winless in their opening four league matches and for so long it seemed they would again fail to score. Alysson’s header from McGinn’s dainty cross after a short corner meant they were spared ruminating on the moment Matz Sels twice denied Victor Lindelöf. In between Sels repelling Lindelöf with his feet and taking his side-foot shot to the face, Murillo smacked an attempted clearance against his own post. Lindelöf has scored one goal in almost six years, his last in November 2023.

Villa were rattled by Forest seizing the lead 45 seconds into the second half. Murillo dispossessed Emiliano Buendía, snapping into a challenge after Boubacar Kamara’s flick and then Delap jinked clear of Ross Barkley. Delap’s next couple of touches took the ball out of his feet, dribbling diagonally across the pitch before sending an unerring right-foot shot into the Villa net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Emery sent on Mbaye and Manzambi in place of Buendía and Barkley but their arrivals did not bring instant success. Instead Delap thought he had doubled his and Forest’s tally, only for the offside flag and a VAR check to deny him. A few moments earlier Tyrone Mings, a first-half substitute for the injured Torres, made a desperate block to thwart Dan Ndoye after superb holdup play by Delap.

Forest, without key defenders Nikola Milenkovic and Jair Cunha through injury, had been readying Igor Jesus when Villa scored, but the striker still arrived to replace Ndoye, who, after a first-half collision with Maatsen, was left with what Glasner described as “a nose like a boxer in the 12th round”. At that point, Villa Park was primed for a grandstand finale, but Forest also roused. Zion Suzuki was twice called into action, his best save clambering down to his right to keep out a Xaver Schlager header, but then Igor Jesus popped up with the winner.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap (right) opened his account for Nottingham Forest with a 46th-minute strike. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Muñoz exchanged passes with Gibbs-White, who eliminated three Villa defenders with a sumptuous flick before Igor Jesus coolly passed the ball past Suzuki to maintain Glasner’s pristine record against Emery. Glasner has not lost in eight meetings against Emery, winning six and drawing two.

“I spoke to him before the game and it’s still 5-2 for him, five European trophies to two,” said Forest’s head coach. “So I said to myself: ‘Oliver Glasner, stay humble.’ And this is how I will stay. The players deserve all the credit, because they did so well, and our fans deserve credit because they supported us, and so now we all go back and will have a lovely Saturday evening.”

Sports.title: European football: Dortmund win again but Freiburg top after Gladbach rout
Sports.content:
Felix Nmecha scored twice and Fábio Silva grabbed another as Borussia Dortmund won 3-0 at home to promoted Paderborn to continue their perfect start in the Bundesliga. Dortmund’s win made it three from three in the league this campaign, their best start in 11 seasons, dating back to Thomas Tuchel’s time.

Starting up front alongside Serhou Guirassy for the first time this season, Silva converted a clever pass from the Guinean to give the hosts the lead after five minutes. Guirassy had two goals disallowed for offside in the first half but Dortmund were rarely troubled by the toothless visitors, who are yet to score since returning to the top flight.

Nmecha came off the bench to score twice, wrapping up victory for the hosts with a stunning late bicycle kick.

Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck made his first appearance since picking up an ankle injury at the World Cup and told Sky Germany he kept his comeback under wraps. “We just hadn’t communicated that much yet because I didn’t want to,” Schlotterbeck said, adding “I missed it terribly. It was a serious injury but I’m glad to be back now.”

Freiburg thumped a poor Borussia Mönchengladbach 5-0 at home to climb to the top. Yannik Engelhardt and Igor Matanovic netted twice each and Maximilian Eggestein added a late fifth as the hosts sent Gladbach, who finished with 10 men, to the foot of the table.

View image in fullscreen Freiburg’s Matthias Ginter (centre) congratulates Igor Matanovic on the opening goal against Borussia Mönchengladbach. Photograph: Philipp von Ditfurth/DPA/AP

A 2-2 home draw with Bayer Leverkusen ended Augsburg’s short stint as leaders. Augsburg were top after the last matchday for the first time in their history but were held by Leverkusen despite a double from Michael Gregoritsch.

Eintracht Frankfurt won their first match of the campaign with a 3-1 victory at neighbouring Mainz, with Can Uzun’s double either side of a Jonathan Burkardt goal. Frankfurt’s goalkeeper Noah Atubolu kept his remarkable penalty-saving record alive when he stopped a first-half effort from Nadiem Amiri. Atubolu’s save was his sixth in a row, extending his own Bundesliga record.

West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug kept his excellent run of form since returning to the Bundesliga going, scoring the equaliser for Werder Bremen in a 1-1 draw at Cologne. Thijs Dallinga missed a penalty after eight minutes but teammate Linton Maina put Cologne ahead moments later.

Füllkrug’s goal came in the 69th minute and is his third in four games since returning to Germany. He only found the net three times in 29 matches for West Ham and scored just once in 20 games on loan at Milan last season.

Elsewhere, Hoffenheim won 2-1 at home against Stuttgart thanks to a double from Adam Hlozek. On Sunday, Bayern Munich travel to promoted Elversberg – who have a 100% record – while RB Leipzig host Hamburg.

In Spain, Alavés missed the chance to go top overnight with a 2-1 defeat at Racing Santander. On Saturday evening, Real Madrid can go second ahead of Alavés and move level on points overnight with Barcelona by beating Rayo Vallecano at home. Barça are at Levante on Sunday afternoon.

In Italy, Diego Moreira scored twice as Milan came from two goals down to hold early season Serie A pacesetters Lazio 2-2 in Rome on Saturday. Moreira came off the bench at half-time and hauled Milan level after Matteo Cancellieri and Tijjani Noslin had given the hosts the lead at the interval.

Despite losing their 100% record having started the season with three wins, Gennaro Gattuso’s side move to the top of the table. Ruben Amorim’s Milan are fourth on eight points, after also drawing last weekend at Juventus.

View image in fullscreen Milan’s Diego Moreira celebrates scoring in his side’s 2-2 draw with Lazio. Photograph: Riccardo Antimiani/EPA

Cancellieri opened his account for the campaign after 10 minutes when he connected with a Mattia Zaccagni cross. A dominant Lazio had good chances to pull further clear before Noslin doubled their lead after 39 minutes with a close-range finish.

Amorim attempted to stem the tide by making three substitutions at half-time, bringing on playmaker Christian Pulisic and Moreira. His changes bore fruit after 65 minutes as Moreira volleyed home to halve the deficit. Less than two minutes later, the former Strasbourg player equalised with a fierce strike from outside the box, but neither side could find a late winner.

Atalanta welcome Cagliari in Saturday’s late game, while Genoa picked up their first point in a 1-1 draw with Frosinone. Champions Inter host Udinese on Monday, with Roma heading to Torino and Como at home to Parma. Inter and Roma have both won each of their first three matches.

Sports.title: Aston Villa warned record signing Nicolas Jackson’s discipline is an ‘absolute disgrace’ after being hooked at half time
Sports.content:
Aston Villa warned record signing Nicolas Jackson’s discipline is an ‘absolute disgrace’ after being hooked at half time

Jason Cundy has cautioned Aston Villa over Nicolas Jackson and his ill-discipline after he was booked against Nottingham Forest.

The striker was shown a yellow card by referee Andy Madley before half-time in the 2-1 Premier League defeat at Villa Park.

4 Jackson was booked late on in the first half of Villa's home defeat to Forest Credit: Getty

Tammy Abraham was then brought on to replace Jackson at the start of the second half by manager Unai Emery with the score 0-0.

It was a change that didn't deliver the desired effort on the pitch as Villa extended their winless league run to four.

Reacting to the substitution on the GameDay Phone-In, Cundy said: "It's a big call that, bringing off Nicolas Jackson and bringing on Tammy Abraham at half-time, that's a big call.

"Whenever you see that, you think, 'Right, he's obviously not doing what he wants'. If you take a striker off and go with a straight swap... that's a strange decision, and then it doesn't work..."

Villa fan Ez then called into the show and explained what happened in regards to Jackson's yellow.

"He got needlessly booked in the first half. We were in possession two thirds of the way down the pitch and for some reason, we look back and there's a Forest player on the floor."

Jackson discipline is a 'problem'

talkSPORT's resident Chelsea fan Cundy then recalled what he saw in regards to Jackson and bookings at his beloved side before the 25-year-old signed for Villa in a club-record £65million deal.

"I promise you now, Nicolas Jackson's discipline is an absolute disgrace. I watched him pick up red and yellow cards for fun, he won't learn. He has a discipline problem."

Ez then revealed: "We must have had a little break for an injury or something, and the players gathered around the touchline by Emery.

"I could see him absolutely bawling at Nicolas Jackson, and then he didn't come on in the second half. So, I think it's a discipline thing."

4 Jackson was hooked at the start of the second half Credit: Getty

4 Emery is said to have been furious with the striker on the touchline Credit: Getty

Jackson received 18 yellow cards in 81 appearances at Chelsea and was also shown two straight reds, with Cundy offering more insight into the ill-discipline.

"The thing with Jackson, he will pick up a yellow card not for a tackle.

"He'll pick it up for saying something to the referee, pulling someone's shirt... kicking the ball away, all of that, not when you put in a mistimed tackle."

"His ill-discipline is terrible," he added. "Maybe that's it, maybe that's why Emery has gone, 'Right, I ain't having that. I've warned you, off.'"

Emery revealed after the full-time whistle that the booking played a role in his decision to bring Jackson off.

"Nico Jackson had a yellow card and the referee was telling us that he needed to keep calm.

4 Villa lost out on the three points as Thiago bagged a late winner for Forest Credit: Getty

"If not, he was close to having another yellow card. I know Jackson and he could have one action with his power being dangerous for another yellow. It was my decision."

Jackson's appearance against Forest was his fourth for Villa since the summer move from Chelsea.

Liam Delap and Igor Thiago scored either side of an Alysson goal to hand Forest their first win of the season.

Sports.title: Frustrated Roberto De Zerbi gives immediate post-match lecture to star as Spurs set unwanted club record
Sports.content:
Frustrated Roberto De Zerbi gives immediate post-match lecture to star as Spurs set unwanted club record

Tottenham's disastrous start to the season officially sank to its lowest ebb.

Roberto De Zerbi's side were held to a scoreless draw at home against Everton on Saturday evening, prolonging Spurs' wait for a first win of the season.

3 Spurs had the majority of the ball but nothing to show for it against the Toffees Credit: Getty

Worryingly, the result extended Spurs' Premier League goal drought.

The 0-0 scoreline meant it is the first time in Spurs' history that they have failed to score in any of their first four league fixtures in a single campaign.

Tottenham's wait for a goal was not aided by an overwhelmingly toothless display in the final third against the Toffees as they mustered just two shots on target.

Roberto De Zerbi in heated exchange with Mathys Tel

Amid his side's attacking woes, De Zerbi was left frustrated by substitute Mathys Tel.

Immediately after the full-time whistle, the Italian went on to the pitch and animatedly gave a lecture to Tel, who stood with his hands on his hips.

Tel, who entered the contest just after the hour mark, struggled to make his mark as he completed just 12 passes and mustered only one shot.

De Zerbi later addressed the incident in his post-match press conference, explaining that his gestures to Tel were intended to convey that 'the striker can't play with his back to the goal.'

Why did De Zerbi give a post-match lecture to Tel?

"He has to play like a striker, looking at the goal, or on the cross for [Andy] Robertson," De Zerbi said.

"He has to stay inside. He started as a striker, now he's playing as a winger.

"But I love Mathys as a player and a guy, there is not a problem."

3 De Zerbi made sure he got his point across to Tel Credit: AFP

The Frenchman was not alone when it came to an anonymous display, prompting ex-Spurs midfielder and talkSPORT host Jamie O'Hara to unleash in a furious post-match rant.

Jamie O'Hara reacts to Spurs' draw

"It's absolute guff," O'Hara said on the GameDay Phone-In.

"Honestly, I can't get my head around it. They are bang average. They [Everton] just sat there, parked the bus.

"It's like 11 lads on the pitch who have never played with each other.

"It's a joke. We are a joke. We can't score a goal.

"How can you play in the Premier League and not score a goal?"

3 Spurs' draw with Everton was their second in a row from the opening four games Credit: Getty

O'Hara also questioned a string of Spurs' summer arrivals, especially given their gargantuan transfer spend.

"Savio runs down dead ends," O'Hara said.

"Marmoush looks like he's got cement in his feet. Solanke's miles off it. Bergvall comes on and looks like a kid. Tonali, we spent £100m and he's non-existent in a game.

"What is going on with this side? It's absolutely shocking."

Sports.title: Unai Emery fears Aston Villa star could be sidelined for a ‘long, long time’ in brutal injury blow
Sports.content:
Unai Emery fears Aston Villa star could be sidelined for a ‘long, long time’ in brutal injury blow

When it rains at Villa Park, it pours.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery fears Ian Maatsen faces a 'long, long time' on the sideline after he suffered an ankle injury in the 2-1 loss to Nottingham Forest.

3 Maatsen had established himself as Villa's starting left-back following Lucas Digne's departure Credit: Getty



Maatsen was scythed down by Forest's James McAtee in the 80th minute but could not continue.

Unfortunately for Villa, they had made all of their substitutions, so they could not replace the Dutch left-back.

It meant John McGinn, who began the match at right wing, had to moonlight as a makeshift left-back.

In a brutal twist, Forest's winner came down that side as Daniel Munoz's cross was deftly flicked on by Morgan Gibbs-White to Igor Jesus, who swept home from close range.



Unai Emery gives worrying update on Ian Maatsen's injury

Speaking after the contest, Emery conceded he did not have a concrete update on Maatsen's injury.

"But the information I have, an ankle injury, it may be a long, long time," Emery said.



The Villa boss was also frustrated that McAtee was allowed to remain on the pitch.

"The tackle, it was one for VAR," Emery continued.

"I think VAR should call the referee to watch it and show a red card.

"We finish with 10 men and they finish with 11."

3 Emery's side are now winless in their opening four league fixtures Credit: Getty



Worryingly, Maatsen wasn't the only Villa starter who picked up an injury against Forest.

Star centre-back Pau Torres also exited early, coming off in the first half with a hamstring issue.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis set for Champions League inclusion

The Spaniard's injury now looks set to result in Taylor Harwood-Bellis being drafted into Villa's Champions League squad.

Harwood-Bellis joined Villa this summer from Southampton for an initial £25million but was a notable omission from Villa's 23-man squad for Europe this season.



However, the one-time England international now looks set to be jettisoned into Villa's Champions League list.

Per UEFA rules, a player who has been injured or ill for at least 60 days can be temporarily replaced by a player who was registered with their club before the List A deadline.

3 Torres' absence will be keenly felt due to his importance in Villa's build-up play Credit: Getty

Speaking on Harwood-Bellis, who was not included in the matchday squad for the loss against Forest, Emery noted 'his time is coming after Pau's injury'.



Villa will look to pick up their first domestic win this season next Wednesday when they make the short trip to Coventry City in the Carabao Cup third round.

Sports.title: ‘Atrocious’ – Chelsea make unwanted 65-year history as ex-Premier League boss left stunned
Sports.content:
Hull City became the latest club to breach Chelsea's fragile defence and condemn the west London club to an unwanted record.

Mohamed Belloumi's 28th-minute leveller ensured the Blues have now gone 20 league games without a clean sheet for the first time in 65 years.



5 Hull's leveller ensured Chelsea reached the defensive milestone

The Blues reached the unwanted feat in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Hull at Stamford Bridge.

It is the first time they have conceded two or more goals in the first four matches of a league campaign in ten years as well.

Xabi Alonso’s side were aiming to banish the memories of last weekend’s defeat at Arsenal and started in blistering fashion.



Morgan Rogers’ expertly-taken finish fired Chelsea into a seventh-minute lead but some suspect defending handed Hull a way back into the match.

A hopeful ball into the box was misjudged by Jorrel Hato, allowing Belloumi to fire the Tigers level.



Chelsea, who have conceded three times in two of their three home games in all competitions this season, once again showed their defensive frailties and talkSPORT co-commentator Steve Bruce issued his own scathing assessment.

Defensive flaws

“Absolutely atrocious from Chelsea,” Bruce said on Game Day Live. “A long punt up the middle. They haven’t dealt with that one for a start.



“Then it’s gone into the corner flag, then they haven’t stopped the cross coming in.

“The cross is one of these looping things that’s come into the box.

“Hato’s misjudged it badly, got underneath it, bounced over the top of him and there was Belloumi to strike it with his left foot and give the ‘keeper no chance.

5 The Chelsea boss was seen deliberating with his side as they chased a leveller Credit: Getty

“It’s the first time they’ve been anywhere near Chelsea’s goal, I can’t remember the goalkeeper touching the ball but they’ve got themselves level.”



Things got even worse for Alonso’s men just six minutes later when Belloumi lashed home from the edge of the box to fire the Premier League new boys in front.

Chelsea got themselves back on level terms in the 66th minute when Joao Pedro produced a neat finish after good work from Cole Palmer down the left.

But there is plenty of work to do for Alonso and his shaky backline who conceded three in the midweek Carabao Cup win over Leeds.

The Spaniard lined up against Hull with a back four comprising of Hato, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Malo Gusto.



The midweek cup goalfest followed Sunday's 2-1 defeat at Arsenal and the 4-3 win over Brighton.

5 Joao Pedro rescued a point for his team with a well-taken finish

The Blues set the tone for a potentially leaky campaign by shipping twice in their season opener at Fulham.

Chelsea's only clean sheet this season came in the 2-0 Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town last month.



Bruce lauds Hull's start to the season

"If one team was going to win it towards the end it was Hull," the former Tigers boss said.

"Chelsea threw everything at them in terms of forward players on the pitch.

"God knows what formation they were playing at the end but every attacking player was on there and they left themselves wide open defensively.

"Hull brought on their subs and had a bit of pace and power and caused them all sorts of problems in forward areas.



5 Steve Bruce was left hugely impressed by his former club's display at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

5 Hull City fans rightly serenaded their players after the hard-fought 2-2 draw Credit: Getty

"They had a big opportunity with about two minutes left and they'll be regretting that chance they missed.

"Hull have done very, very well I have to say," Bruce continued. "They're well-drilled, well-organised, difficult to play against, difficult to beat.



"On the counter attack, they're a threat. You can understand why they've picked up a few points.

"They've got big confidence from the number of points they've picked up over the last few weeks.

"They've given themselves a right opportunity and who'd have thought with the fixture list that they started with this season, they'd be practically top of the Premier League."

Sports.title: Sorba Thomas makes Premier League appearance one day after rollover car crash
Sports.content:
Sorba Thomas was brought on for Hull City against Chelsea a day after being involved in a rollover crash.

Images of the Wales winger's car upside down on a residential road spread across social media on Friday morning.

2 Thomas has returned to the pitch following his crash Credit: Getty

Hull later revealed that Thomas, who was signed from Stoke City in a £10million deal, escaped was 'completely unscathed'.

He was named in their matchday squad for the Premier League trip to Chelsea, with the 27-year-old featuring as a substitute.

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic opted to bring him on for Elliot Stroud in the 60th minute of the 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge.

It was his second league appearance for the Tigers, with the first coming in the 0-0 draw with Aston Villa last weekend.

Many were surprised to see him in action given the state of his car just over 24 hours ago.

Chelsea and Hull battle for draw

Thomas entered play as Hull led 2-1 courtesy of two goals from Mohamed Belloumi.

But Joao Pedro brought Chelsea level, having assisted Morgan Rogers for their opener earlier in the match.

Chelsea became the first side this season to score against Hull, who did not concede versus Manchester United, Coventry City or Villa.

However, the Tigers remain unbeaten on their top flight return and have the joint-best defence with Arsenal and Leeds United.

They are third in the table and may well have dismissed any fears over relegation back to the Championship.

2 Chelsea and Hull shared the points in a tight contest Credit: AFP

As it stands, Hull could be in contention to qualify for Europe later in the season.

It would be a remarkable story for a club who last played Premier League football before the current campaign in 2016/17.

Chelsea on the other hand are a point behind them in fourth and have conceded at least two goals in every leage match.

The reverse fixture at the MKM Stadium is scheduled for March 20.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers joins elite Chelsea group just four league games into Blues career
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers joins elite Chelsea group just four league games into Blues career

Morgan Rogers continued his stunning start to life at Chelsea with yet another goal.

The club-record £117million signing from Aston Villa found the target inside six minutes of the 2-2 draw with Hull City on Saturday.



2 A fine strike from Rogers put Chelsea ahead at home to Hull Credit: Getty

Rogers was fed the ball from Joao Pedro, and then fired low into the bottom corner to hand Chelsea an early lead.

He has joined an elite group of Chelsea heroes who have scored or assisted in each of the first four Premier League games of a season.

Didier Drogba was first to do so in the 2010/11 campaign as he netted four and assisted four.



Cesc Fabregas followed him with six assists in 2014/15, as Diego Costa scored seven in that same run.

Costa also bagged four goals and an assist in 2016/17, and then Eden Hazard hit two goals and two assists at the start of 2018/19.



Hull then equalised shortly before the half-hour mark as Mohamed Belloumi struck after some poor Chelsea defending.

The Algerian scored a second moments later as the visitors fought back to lead.



However, Joao Pedro was on hand to score a second for Chelsea by thumping into the roof of the net.

Rogers goals and assists for Chelsea so far

On his Premier League debut for the club, Rogers scored for Chelsea in their 3-2 victory against west London neighbours Fulham.

He then assisted Pedro Neto as they beat Brighton 4-3, before hitting an early opener in the 2-1 loss at Arsenal.

2



Rogers' goal against Hull came after he came off the bench and assisted three times in the 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds United.

Whilst their attacking quality was on show once again, Chelsea still have concerns over their defence.

They have conceded two goals in all of their matches this season bar one, the 2-0 Carabao Cup win over Luton Town.

Saturday's result at home to Hull has left them fourth in the table and a point behind their opponents.

Sports.title: Derby player stretchered off in neck brace after lengthy stoppage as manager gives update
Sports.content:
Derby player stretchered off in neck brace after lengthy stoppage as manager gives update

Derby striker Henrik Meister was stretchered off in a neck brace after going down off the ball during the clash with Birmingham.

The worrying scenes unfolded at the start of the second half at Pride Park, as the Dane went to ground, causing play to be temporarily halted.



4 Meister received immediate medical attention after going down with no one near him

4 The striker was stretchered off the pitch and was seen in a neck brace

Appearing to have suffered a head injury, medical staff immediately came on to the pitch, before a stretcher was called for.

A seven-minute delay followed, as Meister received treatment, with it becoming clear the player would be unable to continue.



Meister was ultimately moved onto a stretcher and was carried off the pitch to a standing ovation from both sets of fans.

Reporting the incident at the time, Derby wrote on X: "A lengthy delay at the start of the half as Meister goes down off the ball and is stretchered from the field.



"We're all with you, Henrik."

Meister 'OK', says Derby boss

After the match, which saw Birmingham claim a 2-1 win, Derby boss John Eustace revealed Meister was in a stable condition, and said he will undergo concussion protocols.

Giving an update, Eustace said: "To lose him just after half-time was tough.



"It was difficult, but he's OK now. He's having concussion protocols. We'll just have to see how he is. I've been speaking to him and he seems okay."

Meister had been making his first start for Derby after being handed his debut in a 3-0 Championship defeat at West Ham last weekend.

The 22-year-old joined the club on a season-long loan from Serie B side Pisa less than two weeks ago.

4 Henrik Meister joined Derby this summer



With the score at 1-1 at the time of Meister's substitution, Birmingham went on to take the lead through Paik Seung-ho on 64 minutes.

The Rams went in front on 40 minutes, as Bobby Clark fired in from a tight angle.

But Birmingham hit back immediately, as Carlos Vicente equalised less than two minutes later.

The Blues opted for an early substitution at half-time, as manager Chris Davies brought Paik on for Jhon Solis in midfield.



And the switch paid off almost instantly, as the South Korean headed home from Liam Millar's corner.

This proved to be the winning goal, as Birmingham held on to their lead even through 13 minutes of second-half injury time, largely due to Meister's injury.

4 John Eustace is navigating a tough start to the season

The result leaves Derby still in the Championship relegation zone, as they remain 21st in the table.



John Eustace's side have made a disappointing start to the campaign which has seen them win just once.

The Rams have lost six of their opening seven league matches, as well as claiming a draw against Cardiff in their second game.

As for Birmingham, victory moves them into eighth place on 10 points, with this the last of the Championship play-off places following the league's decision to expand this last term.

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis appoints manager considered by Tottenham and Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Tottenham and Bournemouth both came close to appointing new Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil, talkSPORT understands.

Alguacil took charge of the Greek giants earlier this week, as he was chosen by Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis to succeed Jose Luis Mendilibar following his brief tenure.

5 Imanol Alguacil takes charge of Olympiacos having built a strong reputation in Spain

In a manner which has become familiar, Marinakis axed Mendilibar just seven matches into the new season.

The departing manager became the 25th coach dismissed by the Greek businessman, who also owns Forest and Rio Ave, in 16 years.

Hours later, his successor was revealed to be Alguacil, who carved out a strong reputation during his seven years in charge of Real Sociedad.

The 55-year-old led the Basque outfit between 2018 and 2025, during which time he won the Copa del Rey in 2020 – the club’s first trophy in 34 years.

Having taken on Sociedad as a mid-table LaLiga outfit, Alguacil went on to European qualification in five consecutive seasons - reaching the last 16 of the Champions League and Europa League.

Premier League interest

With Alguacil building an impressive CV in Spain, talkSPORT can reveal this led to him being considered by Premier League clubs.

After the Spaniard left Sociedad at the end of the 2025/26, Tottenham explored the possibility of hiring him before ultimately settling on Thomas Frank.

This proved an ill-fated appointment, with Frank lasting just eight months in charge while Spurs went on to narrowly avoid relegation.

And more recently, talkSPORT understands Bournemouth identified Alguacil as a candidate for their head coach vacancy this summer.

With the tactician spending seven months at Saudi Pro League side before departing in February, the Cherries shortlisted him among their managerial options after Andoni Iraola's departure.

5 Evangelos Marinakis bought Olympiacos in 2010 Credit: Getty

5 Spurs and Bournemouth kept tabs on Alguacil after he left Real Sociedad and had a brief spell in charge of Al Shabab

Marco Rose instead took charge at the Vitality Stadium, and is searching for his first win after setting an unwanted Premier League record in his first three games.

Alguacil is also understood to have been high up on Liverpool's list of options, with his work at Sociedad ranking him highly in their data, before Iraola ultimately took the role.

And while the Spanish coach missed out on a Premier League role, he is said to have been sold on the project at new club Olympiacos.

Discussions centred on their sporting project - with Marinakis' goal to compete strongly in Europe and the opportunity for Alguacil to build something rather than simply taking the next available job.

Rated by Mourinho and Enrique

As well as being considered for major vacancies, Alguacil's rising stock has seen him earn praise from some of football's leading managers.

Alguacil’s record of 153 wins and 95 losses in 330 matches at Sociedad led to the legendary Jose Mourinho admitting he struggled to find a weakness in his team after facing him as Roma manager.

5 Alguacil's only managerial silverware so far is the 2020 Copa del Rey with Real Sociedad

5 Real Madrid boss Mourinho was full of praise for Alguacil when the pair faced off in 2023 Credit: Getty

Speaking in 2023, the ex-Manchester United and Chelsea boss said: “It’s difficult to find weaknesses in Real Sociedad.

"Imanol is a very good coach; he has a very well-prepared team.

“In addition to the quality they have, they are also capable of changing systems from one match to another or even during the same game.”

Mourinho isn't his only admirer, with PSG's back-to-back Champions League-winning boss Luis Enrique also claiming Sociedad played the most impressive best in LaLiga under Alguacil.

After facing Alguacil's Sociedad, Enrique said: “What a great team, what a way to compete!

“They are wonderful. I’ll tell you something: Real Sociedad is the Spanish team that plays the best football, without any doubt. Imanol Alguacil deserves congratulations.”

Sports.title: A goal drought of SIX HOURS, no wins this season and £320m spent... Tottenham's attack is truly dismal and Roberto De Zerbi urgently needs results after 0-0 with Everton, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
If there was anything to be said about the reign of Daniel Levy, it is that his failures were delivered on the cheap. This latest version of Tottenham has no such excuses and even fewer finishers of any competence.

After four league games, Roberto De Zerbi has amassed zero wins and, for the first time in the club's history, zero goals. It would seem that his superiors in the recruitment department skipped the most important aisle on their recent trolley dash.

Because how is it possible to spend £320million in the pursuit of such a blunt object? Where is the protein in this meal? If scoring is the main aim of this silly game, then the early signs point to colossal failure, over and again, and there isn't much further to fall after back-to-back finishes of 17th.

It is alarming, truly, and perhaps made worse by the one redeeming feature of this performance against Everton – they dominated the ball. They controlled large passages of the game. They have men who are comfortable in possession and those individuals did create openings.

Alas, they would struggle to hit a barn door from five yards. We can excuse Jan Paul van Hecke for the moderately easy one he launched over the bar early on – he's a centre-half and proved again here that he is very good at his core job. But what about Matheus Fernandes? He embodied the sheer panic that seems to ripple through this side in the final third when he received a Van Hecke delivery unmarked in the area and needed four touches to control.

As with the Nottingham Forest draw, finishing and composure was the glaring shortcoming of Tottenham's evening. But we are also yet to see anything of great consequence from the £100m invested in Sandro Tonali. For the amount they spent, that is a shocking scenario, and amplified by the realisation that Spurs are yet to face a giant this season.

A dire Tottenham have now failed to score in all four Premier League games - despite spending £320million in the summer

Results are now urgent, with a repeat of back-to-back 17th-place finishes unthinkable

To De Zerbi, the striking issue is as much psychological as it is physical – he said his players feel 'blocked' and added: 'If we unblock ourselves I think the team is extremely strong. We can score goals and win games.

'We have not got the right physical condition yet. We played well the first 30 minutes and maybe we lost energy. Maybe we lost confidence. If we extend 30 to 60, 70, 80, 90, my opinion is we will win many games. We have to improve in the last third for sure.'

That much is obvious. As is the urgency for results. But that will be contingent, in part, on De Zerbi establishing some clarity in his own mind around personnel. In his latest spin of the wheel, four changes were made to the side deployed against Forest.

Two were necessitated by injuries to his full-backs, Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie, allowing starts for Andy Robertson, who was excellent, and Archie Gray, who struggled in his latest deployment at right-back. His versatility is a curse as much as a blessing.

Further upfield, Fernandes and Dominic Solanke came in for Mathys Tel and Conor Gallagher, with the upshot that Omar Marmoush shifted from the tip of the spear to the left to accommodate Solanke's first start of the season.

No doubt David Moyes would relish such freedoms of choice.
