As such, the Scot's tinkering was significantly more modest than that of De Zerbi, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles given a start after impressing against Manchester United. Contrary to some wishes, Jack Grealish began on the bench but for a chunk of the first half Everton had no need for attacking mavericks.

Backs pressed to the wall, they were at Tottenham's mercy and saved only by Jordan Pickford and a chronic lack of decisiveness from their hosts. Van Hecke missed the first of the chances but that was nothing compared to one botched by Fernandes after Van Hecke split the defence with an excellent ball through the middle. There is no doubting the threat that lurks in those fast feet of Fernandes but too often he can kill a quick move with an extra touch. Or four.

De Zerbi's gesticulations would suggest he agreed, but a scoreless first half had positives for Spurs. Savio, for one, was a menace to Vitaliy Mykolenko in the initial stages of their duel before he faded. Robertson, a free signing, was excellent on the left throughout. He overlaps well for an old boy.

Brennan Johnson came the closest to scoring for Everton against his former employers

But Robertson was an isolated high-point in the second half, when De Zerbi's concerns about the squad's conditioning were highlighted by the shift in the balance of the game. In one instance, Tyrique George demonstrated that gathering sluggishness by skipping around Gray easily and floating a ball to the far post. Antonin Kinsky blocked Barry's header.

Kinsky then saved again from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall after a mindlessly bad attempt to pass through Everton's frontline.

In between, De Zerbi made a triple change to restart his attack but he was working with a duff motor. His only relief came from the fact a former Tottenham man in Brennan Johnson blew a great chance late on – maybe this magnificent stadium leaves a lasting effect on those forwards who pass through it.

Sports.title: Liverpool 0-0 Fulham: Andoni Iraola's misfiring £1BILLION squad fail to find a way past pointless visitors as new Reds manager's wait for a first Anfield win goes on
Sports.content:
One of these teams boasts the most expensive squad in world football. The other sat winless and pointless with speculation of unrest already growing around their new manager. For a little more than 90 minutes, you would not have been able to tell which was which.

And so the wait for Andoni Iraola’s first win at Anfield goes on. Liverpool have just four of them in the league this year. Many inside this famous old stadium were already filing up the concrete steps for home when the final whistle brought this unfulfilling goalless draw with Fulham to an end. Plenty were long into the concourse by the time Rio Ngumoha saw the last of Liverpool’s half-chances come to nothing.

CAN’T BLAME DRAW ON TIRED LEGS

For this was a shadow of the Liverpool from Wednesday night, where they came away deserved winners against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. This was a leggy, sloppy, uncertain Liverpool. Error-strewn and unsure of themselves. How much of it was because Iraola only made three changes from that midweek triumph? Not enough to excuse Florian Wirtz and the usually dependable Dominik Szoboszlai from either passing the ball straight out of play or frequently to the opposition.

It was not the lack of recovery time that compelled Alisson to play the ball to Ryan Gravenberch inside the Liverpool box despite him being surrounded by two Fulham players and need Jeremy Jacquet to clear Gonzalo Garcia’s goal-bound strike off the line.

It told you everything about the performance from Liverpool that the biggest cheer of the afternoon came when the stadium announcer updated the crowd on the half-time scores and told them Chelsea were losing to Hull.

Liverpool were held to a 0-0 draw by Fulham in a frustrating afternoon at Anfield

Alvaro Arbeloa's Cottagers have had a sluggish start to the season but deserved their point

For the rest of it, the sounds emanating from the stands were ever-increasing groans and cries of frustration. ‘Absolute garbage’ one spectator grumbled to anyone within earshot as he made his way home after the full-time whistle.

Fulham played through Liverpool at will. Josh King was afforded the freedom of Merseyside late on to fire on goal from the edge of the box. Arbeloa’s side played with a debonair confidence but lacked the cutting edge when it mattered. Liverpool created pockets of half-chances but little more than that. The closest they came was when Victor Munoz saw his header clawed away by Bernd Leno and when Isak nodded another wide from a stoppage-time corner.

‘What was lacking was quite clear,’ said Liverpool boss Iraola. ‘It was the first game that we have had problems creating chances to score goals and make the difference. We couldn’t create as many chances as we wanted. That is why we came away with just one point.

‘There is definitely a lack of freshness, we cannot hide that. It was the worst turnaround in terms of hours after a very big game but this is going to happen and we have to adapt.’

BEST STILL TO COME FROM BARCOLA

They couldn’t find either. Wirtz was back to his frustrating worst, dragging shots wide and misplacing passes in dangerous areas.

Bradley Barcola, the £123m signing, manufactured Liverpool’s first chance in an otherwise underwhelming first Premier League start when he played a neat pass through the Fulham defence to Isak, who fired wide from a tight angle.

Yet there was little sign of that fear-inducing forward, who posted the quickest speed of anyone in the Premier League this season just minutes after coming off the bench against Ipswich. Rarely did he attempt to show his man a clean set of heels. He fluffed the chance to slip Isak in again in the second half and saw a volley at the back post deflected behind.

Andoni Iraola passes on instructions to Alexis Mac Allister with the Reds firing a blank

‘We are building up his physcial condition,’ said Iraola. He didn’t have a pre-season. He played well three days ago. We know he has more but it is about giving him minutes. He is a player that’s going to give us a lot.’

Even Szoboszlai couldn’t use his free-kick wizardry in stoppage time to snatch a victory as he did here against Arsenal last season as his dipping effort flicked the top of the wall.

BREATHING ROOM FOR ARBELOA

Fulham continued to get under Liverpool’s skin with Iraola visibly frustrated on the touchline with how long the visitors were taking to get on with their own set pieces. That, by the end, was the least of his concerns. He has a lot of work to do to get this billion-pound squad firing.

For Arbeola, who already finds himself under pressure amid speculation of dressing room unrest, it was a welcome moment of relief.

‘When you are not winning games, it is not easy for your players to beleve in your ideas,’ said Arbeloa. ‘I am happy with a point but more with the performance of my players, with their character, their personality and their ambition I know that everything is about points, not about what you deserve. We were a little bit unlucky but if we keep playing like this we will win games. I am so proud of my players.’

During their playing days, Iraola and Arbeloa often battled it out for the right-back slot in the Spain national team. Arbeloa usually got the better of him. He didn’t quite do the same here but, on reflection, will probably think he should have done.

Sports.title: Zian Flemming keeps Ipswich on track with 3-2 win but Pierre Sage's Crystal Palace have to find answers soon, writes BOBBY MANZI
Sports.content:
Ipswich Town profited from Axel Disasi’s disastrous mistake to secure their second win of the season.

Crystal Palace controlled the affair and were good value for their lead after 14 minutes when Anan Khalaili capped an incisive move with a delightfully drilled finish into the bottom corner.

Against the run of play, though, Ipswich got back into the game when the Palace backline switched off, allowing Leif Davis to cross from the right with Emersonn on hand to guide a free-header past Walter Benitez.

The defence had completely stopped - Ipswich were able to open Palace up far too easily.

Palace continued to look comfortable, though, until Disasi was late on Jack Clarke in the middle of the park, flying over the ball with his studs up and catching Clarke on the shin.

Dismissing the centre-back was a simple decision for referee Chris Kavanagh, leaving Palace to defend for 55 minutes with 10 men.

Ipswich had been dull but the red card sparked them into life and before half-time they had taken the lead.

Emersonn’s miscued attempt fortuitously struck his shoulder and fell for Davis at the far post, where he was free to head past Benitez.

There was a retreat in the second half, though, and O’Neil needs to be wary of that and breed greater consistency into his side’s performances.

They allowed Palace, feeding off the crowd, back into the game as Jorgen Strand Larsen shrugged off Issa Diop to get a shot away from just inside the area and drill it past Kjell Scherpen.

Palace were in the ascendancy and the impetus had swung in their favour despite being a man down.

Khalaili, who had scored his maiden Palace goal in the first half, should have wrapped up three points when he skied over the gaping net from just a few yards out shortly after the equaliser.

They made Palace pay for that miss when the clock struck 90 minutes. Davis latched on to a cross from deep and headed towards goal. His attempt struck the crossbar but dropped kindly for substitute Zian Flemming, whose scuffed contact secured all three points.

Zian Flemming scored late-winner against ten-man Crystal Palace

All things considered, it has been an impressive start from Gary O’Neil’s side. This was the first time Ipswich had come from behind to win in the Premier League since beating Tottenham Hotspur away in December 2001.

Yes, they have lost twice, but those defeats came against Liverpool and Manchester United.

The reality is that they are beating the middling clubs they need to if they have any chance of staying up.

In fact, their two wins in four games have come against two of the Premier League’s three Europa League representatives, following their victory over Sunderland on the opening day.

Palace, though, should be apprehensive considering their defence’s dismal start to the season.

Pierre Sage’s side have shipped 11 goals in their first four Premier League games, and the inconsistency of the backline is not helping, with the starting back three changing in every game.

They did have 10 men for just under an hour on Saturday, but basic errors and moments of lost concentration had been prevalent in the previous games, too.

For Ipswich’s first goal, the defence expected the linesman to raise his flag for offside and froze, gifting Ipswich a lifeline.

Pre-empting the whistle would be deemed criminal on a school playground, let alone in elite football.

Most worryingly for Palace, Sage conceded in his post-match press conference that his players had made the same mistake in training this week.

There is no stability; Jaydee Canvot was dropped from the squad completely after one bad game. How can Sage expect his backline to gel?

Meanwhile, Palace have not kept a clean sheet in their last 10 Premier League matches - the problems precede Sage but he has shown little sign of finding the answers.

Sports.title: Chelsea 2-2 Hull City: Dire defending finally catches up with Blues, as Joao Pedro spares blushes for Xabi Alonso and Tigers roar ever-louder on rampant return to Premier League
Sports.content:
Chelsea 2-2 Hull City: Dire defending finally catches up with Blues, as Joao Pedro spares blushes for Xabi Alonso and Tigers roar ever-louder on rampant return to Premier League

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Chelsea chaos continues, only this time against a Hull side showing why their ascension is no fluke, the awesomeness of the attack could not compensate for the direness of the defence.

We knew it would catch up with Xabi Alonso’s side eventually. It simply isn’t sustainable, relying on bagging a bundle of goals in order to outscore the opposition every single week. They beat Fulham 3-2, and Brighton 4-3, but those wins may have only papered over the cracks.

And Chelsea are cracking rather than showing the solidity needed to challenge towards the top. Even Alonso described the defending as ‘soft’ after this draw with Hull, who remain unbeaten under Sergej Jakirovic and who might have even sneaked a late winner themselves here.

Jakirovic revealed afterwards how before this season started, he promised his staff a week off if they could somehow secure eight points after five games. They have reached that target in four.

As for Alonso, there will be no days off awarded, least of all for his defenders. Chelsea have ‘JPMorgan’ up top in Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, but a piggy bank at the back, waiting to be smashed open at the slightest knock, as it was twice here after Rogers' opener.

That was the first goal conceded by Hull since their return to the Premier League, but Jakirovic’s visitors were hardly made to work hard to turn this match around in their favour.

Chelsea have ‘JPMorgan’ up top, but a piggy bank at the back, waiting to be smashed open at the slightest knock, as it was twice here

Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro got a goal apiece so that Xabi Alonso could avoid losing to Sergej Jakirovic’s streetwise Hull side

Do not let the ball bounce. It is defending 101. The no-no we are all taught as children when we dream of making it as a professional player. Yet Jorrel Hato broke that basic rule.

Hato let the ball bounce in front of him and loop over him after it was launched into the box from the left wing by Ryan Giles, with Chelsea’s other full back Malo Gusto having failed to stop that cross from coming. While Hato was watching, Mohamed Belloumi was waiting, there behind him to blast beyond Emiliano Martinez and make it 1-1.

Hato was hooked at half-time for good reason. This 28th-minute equaliser made it 20 Premier League matches in succession that Chelsea have failed to keep a clean sheet. Their last one arrived in a 2-0 home win over Brentford in January, in what was Liam Rosenior's first league match as head coach as he kickstarted his doomed tenure.

That leveller injected belief into Hull. Jakirovic’s visitors were in the ascendency from then on, and they scored again in the 34th minute after yet more Looney Tunes defending from Chelsea.

Martinez was flapping as Hull’s corner came in. Semi Ajayi headed into the crossbar. The rebound fell to Belloumi, who, via two deflections which made Chelsea’s six-yard box resemble a pinball machine, scored for 2-1.

The Hull fans loved it, of course. ‘We’re top of the league,’ they sang. ‘We’re gonna win the league,’ they added. ‘Sorba Thomas, he parks where he wants,’ they chanted in a nod to their winger who crashed his car on the way into the training ground this week. Despite flipping his Land Rover Defender upside down, Thomas escaped without harm, and came on as a substitute here. Speaking afterwards, Jakirovic joked: ‘You saw the images? He’s Max Verstappen! No, no, everything is fine, thank God. It was an accident. it could happen to anyone.'

Hull remain unbeaten in their first four games following promotion to the Premier League

Hull’s formidable start to this season is no accident. They have won two, drawn two, lost none. They are a solid side who play to their strengths, though it was always going to be a big ask for the visitors to hold on their lead here.

That is because we know how good Chelsea’s attackers are, and that Alonso's side would be throwing everything at them as this game wore on. The Blues had scored within the opening five minutes of their first three Premier League fixtures against Fulham, Brighton and Arsenal. This time it took a little longer – six minutes and 16 seconds for Rogers to score – but it put Chelsea into a strong position until their defence undid them.

While trailing 2-1, it took Palmer carrying the ball down the left before setting up Joao Pedro for Chelsea to equalise. It was a fine finish from the Premier League’s player of the month; precisely what we have come to expect from the striker.

Alonso went for the win late on, replacing Gusto with Danny Welbeck after 78 minutes and introducing Estevao after 86. That was a little late for some Chelsea fans who feel the 19-year-old Brazilian is a terrific talent deserving of more minutes.

However, Hull held firm and so, after riding their luck in wins over Fulham and Brighton, Chelsea’s defence finally cost them. Alonso has overseen six games in all competitions with 30 goals involved in total. It is exhilarating for us neutrals, but exhausting for Chelsea's manager.

Sports.title: Liam Delap delivers barnstorming second-half display for Nottingham Forest, while Aston Villa boss Unai Emery fights his instincts and is beaten AGAIN by Oliver Glasner in 2-1 defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Liam Delap delivers barnstorming second-half display for Nottingham Forest, while Aston Villa boss Unai Emery fights his instincts and is beaten AGAIN by Oliver Glasner in 2-1 defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Unai Emery may have won 12 major trophies in his career but when he faces Oliver Glasner the Spaniard seems as helpless as a kitten.

Aston Villa now have one point from four Premier League games and even though Emery greeted Glasner warmly before kick-off, the Nottingham Forest boss was the last man Emery wanted to see in the opposite dugout.

This was Glasner’s first win over Emery as Forest boss but his sixth in just eight matches. This was his fourth victory over him in the league alone, and his Crystal Palace side also defeated Villa in the FA Cup and the Carabao Cup.

While Glasner’s reign is up and running after a first win at Forest, these are concerning times for Villa. They lost six key players over the summer and in his programme notes, Emery denied that his team had lost its spine. Based on this early-season showings, it is hard to agree with him.

Emery brought on Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi (combined cost £100million) for their debuts and when Ian Maatsen was injured late on, Villa had to finish the game with 10 men as they had used all their replacements.

At that stage, the game looked to be heading for a draw after Alysson had cancelled out Liam Delap’s first goal for Forest but the visitors made the most of their one-man advantage as substitute Igor Jesus scored the winner two minutes from full-time.

Unai Emery has won 12 trophies in his career but Oliver Glasner seems to get the better of him

After a horrible season at Chelsea, Delap now has a coach who trusts him. Better days lie ahead

Delap makes his mark

We cannot change the verdict from last week, when Daily Mail Sport wrote that Delap was not a £50million striker – and we stand by that.

However, with Ezri Konsa now at Arsenal and Pau Torres off injured after 25 minutes, Delap had an easier challenge against Tyrone Mings and Victor Lindelof – centre-backs with a combined age of 65. After a quiet first half, Delap produced a barnstorming display after the break. First he seized on a mix-up between Boubacar Kamara and Emi Buendia to fire home a fabulous drive from 25 yards, just 45 seconds after the restart. He had a second disallowed for a fractional offside – to the relief of Lindelof, who Delap held off with ease before hammering past Zion Suzuki.

What that must have done for Delap’s confidence. After a horrible season at Chelsea, Delap now has a coach who trusts him. Better days lie ahead.

Emery fights his instincts

It was fascinating to watch Emery go against his natural caution with new players and send on Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye for their debuts after an hour.

Had the scores been level at that stage, Emery would surely have left it a little longer. Generally, the Villa boss favours a gradual approach with new signings as he believes they take time to master his instructions. In an ideal world, the new pair would not have been brought on until much later, if at all.

Mbaye made more of an impact than Manzambi as his shot led to the corner that brought Villa’s equaliser but both players will need time.

The greater worry for Villa is that they may go into next week’s match at Tottenham without a single member of their first-choice back four. Konsa and Lucas Digne have departed, Matty Cash is injured and Pau Torres picked up a knock here, as did Ian Maatsen.

Emery went against his natural caution with new players and sent on Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye after an hour

North Stand quandary

To have any chance of closing the financial gap to the elite, Villa need to expand and have decided to rebuild the North Stand this season.

Their ambitious target is to have it open again at the start of next season but in the meantime, they are playing in a three-sided ground. This stadium has been a huge asset to Villa during the Emery era yet they will find it difficult to recreate that fearsome atmosphere this term.

Emery knew this all along. When former chief executive Christian Purslow proposed expansion at the end of the 2023-24 season, the Spaniard pushed back as he could not face the idea of playing Champions League football in a partly-built ground.

UEFA’s punishing spending rules mean they now have no option to press ahead. These are early days but so far, the cost of this reconstruction is far outweighing the benefit.

Sports.title: England survive scare as Joe Root guides hosts to series whitewash over Pakistan at Edgbaston
Sports.content:
England survive scare as Joe Root guides hosts to series whitewash over Pakistan at Edgbaston

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Following a summer of chaos, it was apt that the cool head of Joe Root was there at the last to see England over the line, wrapping up an eight-wicket win and a Rothesay Test series whitewash of Pakistan.

Root had arrived in the middle at Edgbaston in the first over, with Mohammad Abbas seemingly having the ball on a string and England’s openers, both bewitched by his new-ball mastery, back in the changing room.

Abbas had been one of Pakistan’s tail-end heroes on Friday evening to breathe new life into a match that appeared to be in its dying embers, and in striking twice early on the fourth morning, provided hope of a comeback for the ages.

England set off in pursuit of 130 in the knowledge that only once had Pakistan successfully defended so few runs in Test history - against New Zealand back in 1993 when, with Waqar Younis and Wasim Akram in their pomp, they won with 127 to play with.

Not since the 1997 Ashes when Australia imploded for 104 had any team managed to seal a Test match win in this country when faced with 130 or fewer in the bank.

In Abbas, they couldn’t have wished for a better exponent of late-season English conditions to rewrite history: floodlights on, murk in the air and damp in the September surface.

Half centuries from captain Joe Root (above) and Jordan Cox wrapped up a 3-0 whitewash of Pakistan at Edgbaston

Ben Duckett rounded off the most miserable of series with a first-ball departure, held low down by wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori. Then, a dramatic start took in another twist when Abbas switched round the wicket to immediate reward: Emilio Gay pinned leg before by one that nipped back off the seam. Not for the first time this summer, Gay needlessly took a review with him.

Any hope of Pakistan pulling off a spectacular heist went, however, when Mohammad Ali overstepped for the 17th time in the series. Their delight at Root chopping into his stumps was transformed into agony by Paul Reiffel’s signalling of new ball and England, who should have been 35 for three, never looked back.

Yes, Root and his third-wicket partner Jordan Cox rode their luck at times, using the pace of Razaullah to flash early boundaries behind square. Root also edged perilously close to first slip on 34, but with the removal from the attack of Abbas - who, intent on making the most of the cloud cover, rejected the original ball handed to him before the start of play and selected his own from fourth umpire Russell Warren’s box - went Pakistan’s threat.

In the circumstances, England cantered home inside 25 overs, providing a modest crowd with 50% refunds, and the Test team with a first series win since 2024, by the widest of margins.

When Cox, whose 50 came at a slower tempo than Root’s, struck his 76th delivery into the covers and pounced on a misfield to scamper the winning run, the sense of fulfilment for England’s captain was palpable.

It has proved the most turbulent of Test summers, taking in multiple off-field indisciplines, the retirement of his close friend Ben Stokes and sacking of coach Brendon McCullum.

‘There's been a lot of chaos around this series before a ball was bowled and I think the way we've handled it on and off the field, the way everyone understands what is expected of them - both as a player and how we want to carry ourselves - is a really good thing,’ said Root.

‘The start of the series we wanted 3-0 and we've been clinical enough to do that.’

With their relationship thus far restricted to almost daily phone conversations, Root is scheduled to meet incoming Test coach Stephen Fleming for the first time in person between the New Zealander’s arrival in the UK on Monday and linking up with England’s one-day squad next weekend.

One of their most pressing tasks in preparing for their first assignment together, in South Africa from December, will be how to accommodate the returning Jacob Bethell. Both Cox, his replacement at three, and Dan Lawrence, named man of the match here, have staked claims to remain in the top six.

Sports.title: Premier League star Sorba Thomas pictured for the first time since flipping his £160,000 Land Rover - before coming off the bench for Hull City's clash with Chelsea just a day after accident
Sports.content:
Sorba Thomas has made a substitute appearance for Hull City a day after he flipped his Land Rover on his way to training.

The 27-year-old walked away from the crash, which happened on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am on Friday. His vehicle, a grey Land Rover Defender with a personalised number plate, was pictured on its roof, with broken windows.

The club said on Friday it was 'relieved' to hear its player, who joined the Tigers from Championship side Stoke City earlier this month, was unharmed.

In a statement Hull City said: 'The club is aware of images of Sorba's car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed.'

Thomas travelled to London and was pictured heading into Stamford Bridge ahead of Hull City's Premier League clash against Chelsea on Saturday afternoon. He was brought on for Elliot Stroud in the 60th minute.

Thomas has travelled to London and was pictured heading into Stamford Bridge ahead of Hull City's Premier League clash against Chelsea on Saturday afternoon

Thomas was involved in a crash that saw his car flip onto its roof on his way to training

A woman who lives at the scene said the crash woke her up, the BBC reported.

'I was laid in bed (and) heard a noise – crash, bang,' she said. 'I got up, come down and the car is in my hedge.'

An NHS worker who lives on the road said the incident had left him unable to go to work as the road was blocked.

'There will be patients who will miss appointments because of this,' he said.

Thomas, who has been capped 27 times by Wales, has now featured three times for the Tigers since joining for £10million on deadline day.

Hours before the crash, Jakirovic had praised the winger saying he had 'no doubt' about his capability to play in the Premier League.

He said: 'I don't have any doubt about Sorba because he made a difference in the Championship.

'He is a left winger and we can use him inside like a left-sided number ten. He knows football. He is very good in delivery and his end product is good. Also, he has very good set-pieces.

'He is sharp and has speed. Also, in defence, he is very responsible. I think he suits us a lot. Like always, I hope he can help us.'

Thomas started Tuesday night's 1-0 Carabao Cup loss to Sunderland and made an appearance off the bench in the club's 0-0 draw against Aston Villa in the Premier League.

After his cameo against the Europa League champions, Thomas shared his delight on Instagram. He posted: 'Pinch (me) moment for me and my family today!!! Premier League debut.'

Sports.title: Lando Norris stuns Kimi Antonelli with 'perfect' lap to snatch Spanish Grand Prix pole in Madrid - while Lewis Hamilton has to settle for fourth
Sports.content:
Lando Norris stuns Kimi Antonelli with 'perfect' lap to snatch Spanish Grand Prix pole in Madrid - while Lewis Hamilton has to settle for fourth

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lando Norris relit his world championship hopes by taking pole position for the Spanish Grand Prix. He came from nowhere to do so.

The British driver was delighted by his achievement, letting out a yelp of delight in the cockpit, almost as if disbelieving his achievement on the perilous new track on the outskirts of Madrid.

The world champion qualified 0.011sec ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli, with Max Verstappen third and Lewis Hamilton fourth for Ferrari. George Russell was fifth for Mercedes.

Norris celebrated with his mother Cisca after his pole, hugging her. He is 96 points behind Antonelli and overhauling the 20-year-old Italian will be a tough job over the final 10 rounds of the season. But his McLaren team, helped by upgrades and gathering momentum, are on the rise.

Lando Norris has taken pole at the Spanish Grand Prix with a 'perfect' lap

The British driver got the better of championship leader Kimi Antonelli in Madrid

‘I am shocked and a little bit surprised to be here now, but my God, it was probably one of the best laps I have done in my career,’ said Norris.

‘It was one of those laps where everything came together. It was just whether my brain allowed me to do it, and in the end it was perfect.

‘You look at the lap time, and you are like, ‘Oh s***, that feels pretty good.’

Prior to Norris’s perfect ambush, Hamilton had set the fastest time in first run of Q3, having crashed in practice earlier in the day.

It was Norris’s 19th pole position on this road circuit.

‘How I did it is a secret even I don’t know,’ he added.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: Conor Benn shows off remarkable weight transformation after piling on 32 pounds in just HOURS, having been 'dragged to the pits of hell' during excruciating weight cut ahead of mega-fight with Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Conor Benn shows off remarkable weight transformation after piling on 32 pounds in just HOURS, having been 'dragged to the pits of hell' during excruciating weight cut ahead of mega-fight with Ryan Garcia

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Conor Benn has shown off a dramatic 32lb weight gain just hours after coming in one pound under the 147lb welterweight limit ahead of his bout with USA's Ryan Garcia.

The 29-year-old Briton came in at 146lb (66kg) at Friday's weigh-in for Saturday's fight, half a pound heavier than champion Garcia.

Just 12 hours later, Benn revealed on social media that he had added 32lb, taking him to 12st 10lb (80.73kg).

Speaking at a ceremonial event in front of fans later on Friday, Benn already appeared noticeably bigger, with his face and shoulders having filled out.

'Did it look hard? How did I look?' he asked. 'We'll see tomorrow night how good I really feel.'

Benn had previously said he could weigh as much as 12st 7lb (80kg) by the time he stepped into the ring on Saturday evening (around 4am Sunday, UK time).

‼️ Conor Benn has rehydrated to 178.4 pounds already.



📈 He is up 32.4 pounds (including clothes etc) in just 10 hours! 😱 pic.twitter.com/m6netuS2c1 — EverythingBoxing | Darshan Desai (@EverythingBoxi2) September 12, 2026

Benn revealed on social media that he had added an incredible 32lb hours after the weigh-in

The 29-year-old Briton had come in at 146lb (66kg) at Friday's weigh-in for Saturday's fight, half a pound heavier than champion Garcia before quickly adding it back on

Speaking at a ceremonial event in front of fans later on Friday (above), Benn already appeared noticeably bigger, with his face and shoulders having filled out

He has not fought at welterweight for more than four years, having moved up through the divisions before competing at middleweight during his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Now, for the biggest fight of his career, taking on Garcia for the World Boxing Council (WBC) title under the bright lights in Las Vegas, he has had to come all the way back down.

'It feels like I've been dragged down to the pits of hell, had a fight with Satan and God brought me back to life,' he told BBC Sport earlier this week.

'Making weight has been the hardest thing I've done. I haven't made weight for four and a half years so it's going to be hard.'

Whether the weight cut affects Benn's strength and power on Saturday night will be one of the central questions of his WBC world title fight.

Garcia has suggested Benn's move back down could leave him vulnerable, but Benn was dismissive of that concern when he spoke to Daily Mail Sport earlier in the week.

'You think I've been up at middleweight, mixed it with someone who's competed at super middleweight? You think I'm worried about what a lightweight can do to me?' he told this publication.

'You think I'm concerned in the slightest about this guy? I'm not concerned about one little thing he brings to the table… that silly left hook of his is useless. He can bring whatever he wants. It don't concern me.'

USA's Garcia claimed the WBC title with a dominant points victory over Mario Barrios in February and is making the first defence of his belt against Benn on Saturday

Benn's unusual route to this fight has been shaped by his rivalry with Eubank.

Their first meeting at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April 2025 was the culmination of years of animosity between the two families, with Benn and Eubank Jr inheriting a rivalry that began with their fathers in 1990.

The fight itself was fought at a catchweight above 160lb, with Benn stepping up significantly from his previous division. Eubank won a close decision, leaving Benn to reflect on a performance in which he felt the occasion and the emotion had affected him.

Seven months later, the pair met again at the same venue. This time Benn won the decision, dropping Eubank twice in the final round in a dramatic conclusion to their second fight. It left them level at one victory apiece and appeared to finally close the door on one of British boxing's most talked-about rivalries.

Benn insisted the atmosphere this week is nothing like those two nights when asked whether his hatred for Garcia compared.

'This is nothing like the Eubank fight,' he said. 'The Eubank fight, there was nothing pleasant or friendly or fake about the Eubank fight. There was a lot more raw emotion in that fight and I let that get the better of me the first time. That won't happen here.'

Garcia has won 25 of his 28 professional fights, including 20 by knockout, with two defeats and one no-contest. He claimed the WBC title with a dominant points victory over Mario Barrios in February and is making the first defence of his belt against Benn. Benn has 25 wins, 14 by knockout, and one defeat.

Benn said of his rival: 'He just carries on like a spoiled brat, like a big child who throws his toys out of the pram. I'm not worried about him in the slightest. If anything, I'm gonna have a bit of fun with him. He's a little bit sensitive, highly emotional, and a little bit insecure.'

There is also an uncomfortable shared history between the two men when it comes to drugs testing.

Benn's original 2022 fight with Eubank was cancelled after he returned two adverse findings for clomifene, something he has consistently denied intentionally taking. Garcia subsequently returned an adverse finding for ostarine following his 2024 victory over Devin Haney, which he also denied intentionally taking.

Both men were asked at the fight's press conference whether they had concerns that the other could use performance-enhancing drugs ahead of Saturday's contest.

Neither appeared keen to make it a central issue, with the focus instead returning to the fight itself.

Benn defeated Chris Eubank Jr by unanimous decision to take revenge in their rematch at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last November

Garcia has also questioned whether Benn's career has prepared him for this level of opposition, arguing that the Briton is taking a step too far by challenging for the world title.

Benn's response was typically blunt. 'How is this too far? He quit against Tank Davis. He got outclassed by Rolly (Romero), and then got a world title shot with Barrios,' he said.

'Then there is me. Stepping up to fight the contenders up at middleweight, fight of the year up at middleweight, avenging my loss. Two big stadium shows. Just come off beating a two-time former world champion and having to make 147, which again I ain't made in four years in six weeks.

'What's he talking about? Ultimately, who cares what he thinks? I don't listen to quitters anyway.'

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia was banned for racial slurs, hit with a $1m doping fine and U-turned on his support for Donald Trump... but America's controversial rock-and-roll boxer is out to save his sport by beating Britain's Conor Benn
Sports.content:
A dazzling talent just reaching his prime will enter the T-Mobile Arena here this Saturday night with the hopes of a fighting nation resting on his shoulders. Conor Benn, not so much. British boxing is enjoying a boom, not least with its dominance in the marquee heavyweight division. The young man the son of Nigel is challenging for the world welterweight crown carries the burden of restoring America to its historic pre-eminence in the prize-ring. Not just by adding to an unusually low head count of their champions but by resuscitating the excitement, the stardust, the impudence, the controversy, the brilliance and the fascination of the public over here with the hardest game of all. Ryan Garcia is the only poster boy left to them following the retirement of Floyd Mayweather. Vitally, he has all it takes to bring a new generation of fans clamouring to his fights. At 28 he has the matinee idol looks of a young Elvis Presley which brings the girls squealing into the crowds. A rock and roll bad-boy reputation which chimes with the lads. Showmanship within the ring and charisma outside the ropes. Ryan Garcia will take on Conor Benn on Saturday night with the American carrying the hopes of a fighting nation on his shoulders Garcia has reconciled with Andrea Celina Velarde (left), the beautiful mother of two of his three children (above) Benn has arrived in Las Vegas with the aim of taking the WBC welterweight belt from Garcia Glamorous blondes vie for his favours. Even though he is resisting those temptations now he has scrapped divorce proceedings and reconciled with Andrea Celina Velarde, the beautiful mother of two of his three children. And, boy, can he box. The speed of hand and foot. The knock-out punching power. The taunting evasion. And, yes, the conceit which on occasion gets him into trouble. The two defeats scarring his 28-fight record – against two of America’s other world champions Gervonta Davis and Rolly Romero – came when he was at his most arrogant and complacent. The no-decision verdict which negated his stand-out victory over Devin Haney was imposed for failing a post-fight drug test for performance-enhancing Ostarine. Like Benn he protested his innocence: ‘I’ve never knowingly taken drugs.’ His relatives revealed he had been struggling with his mental health and against alcohol. But unlike Conor he preferred taking his punishment – a $1million fine and a 12-month ban – rather than financing a protracted court case which would also have kept him under lengthy suspension. Not that King Ry - he wears a gold crown for his ring entrances - is prone to compromising his regally unvarnished opinions. Garcia was a vociferous backer of Donald Trump in his first presidential election campaign. But given his Mexican roots he criticised Trump’s second-term deportation policy. Finally he renounced his support, denouncing the Trump administration’s handling of the Epstein Files. A devout Christian, he called rapper Eminem a satanist and posted on Twitter: ’I don’t support the LGBTQ+. F*** you guys. Rot in hell.’ He called for a boycott of the Olympics for ‘disrespecting Jesus Christ' with the section of the opening ceremony of France 2024 in which drag queens imitating Greek gods were widely supposed to be parodying the Last Supper. Garcia scrapped divorce proceedings with influencer Andrea in August 2025 Garcia turned down WBC offers to help with his mental health difficulties but progress has been deemed to be made, leading to him fighting and beating Mario Barris in February The rock-and-roller came out in him when he was arrested for causing $150,000- worth of damage while trashing a room and a corridor at the ritzy Waldorf Astoria hotel in Beverly Hills. That risked a short prison term, which has not been applied. Another suspension was imposed. This one from competing in fights sanctioned by the WBC for racist slurs live on the internet against the black community and muslims. President Mauricio Sulaiman reported that Garcia had turned down a number of offers from the WBC to help Garcia with his mental health difficulties. Sulaiman relented last November, saying he recognised the progress made in that regard by the fighter’s large family. Promptly, this February, Garcia defeated the highly rated Mario Barrios to claim the WBC welterweight belt, inflicting a first round knockdown on his way to a unanimous decision. The braggadocio bubbles to the surface before fights. As soon as this weekend’s bout was announced he told Benn to his face: ‘You box like amateur trash. You're just a flashy trash can. I’m going to throw you out with trash.’ All the ingredients are there for the making of a turbulent, troubled super-star son of this angry and violent 21st century. All wrapped up in the rare skills and brave heart of a potentially great fighter. Some indication of whether all that will be enough for him to kindle another golden age in US boxing may be seen in how he deals with Benn. The huge scale of that task is evident in this, my overwhelmingly American list of the 20 greatest boxers of all time, with Lennox Lewis the Brit who came closest to inclusion...
